items.title: Open Source Radar — 2026-09-19
items.body:
# Open Source Radar — 2026-09-19
_Rotation slot 4 — data, search, documents, RAG_

## Executive Summary
Today's run landed on a genuinely useful document/search cluster. The headline find is Xberg, the confirmed successor to Kreuzberg (whose HTML→Markdown component was already tracked here) — now a full 107-format document-intelligence engine with OCR, transcription, code intelligence, and an MCP server, spanning 15 language bindings. Alongside it, Timescale shipped a small, permissively-licensed Postgres extension that closes the BM25-ranking gap left by plain `tsvector` search, without dragging in a second datastore or an AGPL license. Two further finds sit closer to the product-opportunity axis: a permission-aware enterprise-RAG platform that treats access control as a first-class retrieval concern rather than an afterthought, and a self-hosted, drop-in-compatible replacement for paid Firecrawl/Tavily scraping API bills. The GitHub Search API surfaced heavy volume in the "AI agent memory," "AI agent gateway," and "PDF/document extraction" spaces again today — the extraction wave in particular is now large enough that Xberg's broad scope made picking a single best-in-class entry straightforward rather than requiring a hard call between near-duplicates.

## Today's Best Discoveries

### 1. Xberg — 8.8/10
**Decision:** USE NOW

**What it is** — A polyglot document-intelligence engine with a Rust core: extracts text, tables, metadata, and structured data from 107 formats, with OCR, audio/video transcription, layout/table reconstruction, code intelligence for 371 languages, embeddings, and schema-driven structured extraction, callable as a library (15 bindings), CLI, REST API, or MCP server.
**Why I should care** — One engine replaces the multi-library pipeline (PDF parser + OCR engine + table extractor + chunker) most RAG ingestion code assembles by hand, and it's natively callable from Node.js, not just Python.
**What it could replace** — A hand-rolled document-ingestion pipeline, or a paid document-intelligence API (Unstructured-style services) for a product's ingestion layer.
**Ways I could use it** — Single ingestion step for a RAG pipeline handling mixed document types; OCR + layout reconstruction for scanned uploads; code-intelligence extraction for syntax-aware RAG chunking over a codebase; schema-driven structured JSON extraction without hand-written prompts; point a coding agent at it via its built-in MCP server.
**Agent opportunity** — Ships an official MCP server out of the box; REST mode (`xberg serve`) works as a shared ingestion microservice.
**Integration effort** — Low: `pip install xberg` / `npm install @xberg-io/xberg` / Docker/Helm for a standalone service.
**Maturity** — Mature engine under a young rebrand: 9,325 stars, created Jan 2025, actively maintained (pushed today), real CI + Codecov, multi-contributor.
**License** — MIT, verified against the LICENSE file. No commercial restrictions.
**Alternatives** — yfedoseev/pdf_oxide + office_oxide (narrower but faster for pure PDF/Office extraction, more language bindings); firecrawl/pdf-inspector (Firecrawl's narrow scanned-vs-text PDF classifier); docling-project/docling (similar scope, Python-first, no first-class Node bindings); catalogued opendataloader-pdf (narrower, PDF-only).
**Why this one** — Broadest scope of anything in the extraction/intelligence space reviewed today, with a first-class MCP server and Node.js bindings that most competitors lack.
**Recommendation** — Point it at a real mixed-format document set (PDF + scanned images + a code directory) to validate the OCR and code-intelligence claims before deep production use.

### 2. pg_textsearch — 8.3/10
**Decision:** USE NOW

**What it is** — A PostgreSQL extension adding BM25 relevance-ranked full-text search via a simple `content <@> 'query'` operator, built by Timescale.
**Why I should care** — Closes the real gap between plain Postgres full-text search and a dedicated search engine — proper BM25 ranking — without adding a second datastore.
**What it could replace** — A bolted-on Algolia/Typesense integration, or standing up Elasticsearch/OpenSearch purely for ranked keyword search when the data already lives in Postgres.
**Ways I could use it** — Add ranked keyword search to an existing Postgres table; pair with pgvector/pgvectorscale in the same database for hybrid retrieval; per-tenant partitioned search indexes in a multi-tenant SaaS.
**Agent opportunity** — Natural backing store for an MCP server needing keyword search over structured records already in Postgres.
**Integration effort** — Low: prebuilt binaries for Linux amd64/arm64, or build from source; requires a `shared_preload_libraries` change and a restart to install.
**Maturity** — Emerging: pre-1.0 (v1.4.0), created July 2025, real CI + benchmark workflow + Coverity Scan badge.
**License** — PostgreSQL License (permissive, BSD/MIT-style), verified against LICENSE file.
**Alternatives** — paradedb/paradedb (broader all-in-one Postgres search+vector platform, but AGPL-3.0); Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (assumed known, much higher operational overhead for this narrow a need).
**Why this one** — Narrow, permissively-licensed, single-purpose extension rather than an AGPL all-in-one platform, from a maintainer (Timescale) with a track record in the Postgres extension space.
**Recommendation** — Install against a non-critical table first given the pre-1.0 status, then pair with pgvector for hybrid search.

### 3. PipesHub AI — 7.8/10
**Decision:** PROTOTYPE

**What it is** — An open-source platform connecting enterprise knowledge sources (drives, wikis, chat, email) to AI agents with permission-aware retrieval — results are scoped to the querying user's actual access rights, with citations back to source.
**Why I should care** — Permission-aware retrieval is the part most hand-rolled RAG setups skip until a security review forces the issue; this ships it as a first-class concern.
**What it could replace** — Hand-built per-source connectors plus a custom permission-inheritance model, a multi-week project most teams underestimate.
**Ways I could use it** — Internal "ask our docs/wiki/drive" assistant that respects real document permissions; RAG layer for a support agent where source systems have different access boundaries; baseline for a permission-aware knowledge-search feature in a B2B product.
**Agent opportunity** — Positioned explicitly as the retrieval layer AI agents call, not just a human-facing search UI.
**Integration effort** — Medium: full platform (connectors, indexing, permission engine, UI) via Docker, not a single library.
**Maturity** — Emerging: pre-1.0 (v0.8.0), created March 2025, real multi-contributor team, active Discord/roadmap.
**License** — Apache-2.0, no commercial restrictions.
**Alternatives** — onyx-dot-app/onyx (32,161★, larger and more established, similar connector model, not deep-reviewed this run); building permission-scoped retrieval by hand on pgvector/pg_textsearch.
**Why this one** — Ships permission-aware retrieval with citations as the core feature rather than an add-on, which is directly relevant given the MSSP/PTaaS-adjacent context where access-boundary correctness matters.
**Recommendation** — Worth a small real trial if a permission-scoped internal-knowledge assistant becomes a real need; audit the ACL-inheritance logic directly before trusting it with real access boundaries.

### 4. fastCRW (crw) — 7.5/10
**Decision:** PROTOTYPE

**What it is** — A self-hostable Rust web scraper/crawler/search engine exposing a Firecrawl/Tavily-compatible API as a single ~6 MB binary, turning URLs into clean Markdown or structured JSON.
**Why I should care** — Drop-in API compatibility means an existing Firecrawl/Tavily integration can point at a self-hosted binary instead of a metered API with no code changes beyond the base URL, for non-JS-heavy pages.
**What it could replace** — A recurring Firecrawl or Tavily API subscription for scrape/crawl/search calls in an agent pipeline.
**Ways I could use it** — Give a coding agent a local `crw search`/`crw scrape` tool with no per-call cost; RAG ingestion step for turning URLs into Markdown; site-mapping/crawling for a small product's content-indexing job.
**Agent opportunity** — Ships an official MCP server (crw-mcp) that auto-registers with Claude Code/Cursor/Codex/Gemini CLI/OpenCode/Windsurf on install.
**Integration effort** — Low: single binary or Docker.
**Maturity** — Emerging: created March 2026, active (pushed today), but contributors skew heavily to a single author (997 commits vs. next-highest human contributor at 4).
**License** — AGPL-3.0. **Flagged loudly**: self-hosting a modified version as a network service others query requires releasing source under AGPL or a commercial license; running it internally/locally has no such obligation.
**Alternatives** — Firecrawl and Tavily themselves (the hosted, paid services this is compatible with); browserbase/stagehand (heavier, browser-automation-first, different use case).
**Why this one** — The only self-hosted entrant found this run with genuine drop-in API compatibility with two specific paid services, backed by published head-to-head benchmarks.
**Recommendation** — Trial it for non-JS-heavy scraping/crawling to cut a Firecrawl/Tavily bill; verify the AGPL implications before any embedding into a hosted product, and keep an eye on the single-maintainer bus-factor risk.

## Meaningful Updates
**html-to-markdown (Kreuzberg)** — previously catalogued (USE NOW, 8.3) with its description noting the org's "broader product is a document-intelligence engine." That broader product has now shipped and grown to 9,325 stars — catalogued today as **Xberg**, which the README confirms is "the next iteration of Kreuzberg, rebuilt and rebranded under a fresh v1 line." This doesn't change the html-to-markdown entry's own recommendation (still a valid narrower/lighter option for HTML-only conversion), but the full-scope engine is now separately trackable. Catalog updated: Yes (both the html-to-markdown entry's notes/project file and the new Xberg entry cross-reference each other).

## Still Worth Trying
Projects flagged USE NOW/PROTOTYPE that haven't been tried yet, rotated away from the last four runs' picks (ctx/mex/Gortex on 2026-09-18; AdminForth/LoongSuite Pilot/Rebase on 2026-09-17; Vercel Skills CLI/Benjamin-Plus Skill/SIMURG on 2026-09-16; Bernstein/Sidequest/Kingfisher on 2026-09-15):
- **Monoscope** — USE NOW, 8.6/10, first seen 2026-08-31 (19 days ago). AI/agent-aware observability platform; smallest next step is pointing it at one existing service's logs/traces for a day to see whether the AI-native query layer actually beats a raw log grep.
- **OpenDataLoader PDF** — USE NOW, 8.5/10, first seen 2026-08-29 (21 days ago). PDF-to-accessible-AI-ready-data parser, directly on-theme for today's slot; smallest next step is running it against one real PDF with tables/forms to confirm the accessibility-automation claims hold up.
- **haiku.rag** — PROTOTYPE, 8.3/10, first seen 2026-09-05 (14 days ago). Lightweight local-first RAG toolkit; smallest next step is standing up one small collection and comparing retrieval quality against a hand-rolled pgvector query.

## Small but High-Leverage Utility
None met the bar today — the strongest small-utility candidates (pdf_oxide's raw extraction speed, pdf-inspector's scanned/text classifier) are narrower components of the broader Xberg pick above rather than standalone finds, and are noted there instead of promoted separately.

## Worth Watching
- **samyama-ai/samyama-graph** (172 stars, Apache-2.0) — a Rust graph-vector database with 99.9% OpenCypher TCK pass rate, LDBC SNB Interactive/BI benchmark completion, and a claimed 1B edges on one machine. Technically ambitious and worth studying architecturally, but too small a community (created Jan 2026) to recommend adopting yet.
- **serenedb/serenedb** (758 stars, Apache-2.0) — positions itself as "the first real-time search analytics database." Real homepage and steady growth since Aug 2025, but not deep-reviewed against ClickHouse-class incumbents this run; would need a head-to-head before a full entry.
- **readur/readur** (795 stars, MIT) — a modern, Rust+TypeScript self-hosted OCR/document-management platform (WebDAV/S3 sync, OIDC, multi-language OCR). Solid engineering, but sits in the same niche as the already-widely-known paperless-ngx without an obviously decisive differentiator surfaced this run; worth a second look if paperless-ngx's OCR pipeline becomes a real pain point.

## Rejected / Duplicate Candidates
- **manticoresoftware/manticoresearch** (12,018 stars, GPL-3.0) — already-established search database, created 2017 with a long Sphinx-successor history; no material new development flagged this run.
- **PDF/document-extraction wave around today's Xberg pick** (yfedoseev/pdf_oxide, yfedoseev/office_oxide, firecrawl/pdf-inspector) — all narrower than Xberg's scope; filed as alternatives inside its entry rather than separate picks, though pdf_oxide is a legitimate standalone choice if raw single-format extraction speed matters more than breadth.
- **paradedb/paradedb** (9,283 stars, AGPL-3.0) — broader Postgres search+vector platform, but AGPL-3.0 vs. pg_textsearch's permissive license for the same core BM25-ranking need; filed as an alternative in that entry.
- **run-llama/liteparse** (12,330 stars) — high star count likely reflects the parent LlamaIndex org's existing audience rather than independent traction for this specific new tool; not deep-reviewed, worth a second look once it has its own track record.

## Run Notes
Sources used: GitHub Search API (primary — 14 parallel topic/keyword queries covering RAG, vector databases, document processing, search engines, embeddings, data pipelines, OCR, PDF/data extraction, knowledge graphs, full-text search, and Postgres+search intersections), GitHub REST API for repo/release/contributor metadata and license-file verification on the shortlist, raw.githubusercontent.com for README/LICENSE fetches, PyPI and npm registries to cross-check published versions against GitHub tags. WebSearch/HN/Lobsters were not used this run — GitHub Search API alone surfaced more than enough slot-4 volume, consistent with recent runs. No sources failed or timed out; GitHub API rate limit stayed well under the 8,350/hr ceiling (~45 requests used). Did not perform a full meaningful-update sweep of the other ~106 previously catalogued projects' release feeds this run — budget went to new-discovery review depth instead, beyond the one meaningful update (Kreuzberg → Xberg) surfaced incidentally by today's discovery.

items.title: Inspect memories, tune extraction and ask questions through a Loom assistant
items.body:
### Component

Dashboard

### Use case

Users need to ask Loom whether their agents use its features appropriately, understand why recall or ingestion behaves poorly, and ask ordinary questions over the content they can access.

Examples:

- "Did this agent read memory before answering during the last week? What can we actually prove?"
- "Are we storing documents, coordination state or structured records as memory claims? Show examples and the appropriate destination."
- "Why does this namespace have repeated writes, poor recall or growing storage cost?"
- "Show what this user, agent or session remembers, then propose better categories and extraction instructions from those examples."
- "What did we decide about this feature? Cite the memory revision and design document."
- "Which ingestion jobs are failing, and which document versions are searchable?"

This makes sense as a conversational layer over Loom's existing diagnostics, retrieval and observability. It should explain evidence and propose actions. Format compliance alone does not prove factual correctness, retrieval quality or agent efficiency; an LLM cannot establish these by inspecting database rows alone.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Build a Loom assistant with read-only investigation first, supporting both ClickHouse-only and ClickHouse+Postgres deployments. Quality is the first priority; scalability and latency are measured release requirements. Keep the assistant independent of the chat client. Evaluate LibreChat as an optional client using Loom's MCP tools before committing to an embedded interface or a new required service.

#### Inspect, tune, apply

Expose three clear stages in the product:

| Stage | Behavior | Permission to change data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspect | Read authorized memories and their sources, history, categories and available creation settings for a selected user, agent or session | Read-only |
| Tune | Draft category, extraction-instruction and supported setting changes from the selected evidence, with before/after examples | Read-only proposal; no configuration changes |
| Apply | Show the exact diff, scope and effects, then commit only the actions an authorized person approves | Explicit approval and normal write authorization |

User, agent and session are filters within the caller's authorized scope, not new tenant boundaries. Define each filter precisely: an agent-authored row or a session-created row is different from all shared knowledge that agent or session could read. Show those views separately, including empty and incomplete results, rather than claiming that an authorship filter reconstructs everything an agent knows.

Tune should change the process that creates memories as well as recommend record repairs. Read the applicable namespace guide, registered categories, extraction instructions and effective settings when authorized. Propose evidence-based changes with supporting and counterexamples, expected effects and limits. A preview may compare extraction outputs over a bounded, reviewed sample without publishing them; show model cost and coverage. Do not optimize only for fewer memories or shorter text at the expense of important facts and source fidelity.

Existing operator extraction policy is readable and writable only by an organization administrator; keep that boundary and its precedence. Do not invent a persisted per-user or per-session setting where only an organization, namespace or request setting exists. A proposal must name the actual supported target, all affected consumers and whether it changes future extraction only. Re-extraction, recategorization or rewriting historical memories is a separate selected action with its own impact preview and authorization. Tuning cannot silently weaken an administrator's mandatory policy, change grants or modify storage schema.

#### Scoped chat and project configuration

The entry screen explains that users can inspect what a user, agent or session remembers, then propose changes to the categories, instructions and settings that create those memories. Include an explicit scope selector and a Review changes panel with pending proposals and their approval state. Scope comes from the authenticated user's allowed placements and collections; a scope selected in chat cannot widen permissions.

Offer these conversation starters using Loom's own terminology:

| Starter | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Show relationships between facts | An authorized, bounded graph view with cited source facts, edge provenance and validity; distinguish asserted, inferred and disputed relationships |
| What is in this project? | A scoped inventory of available memories, documents, records, runs, integrations and capabilities, with counts, freshness and incomplete sections labeled |
| Analyze one user's memories | A selectable authorized user view, evidence-backed findings, and optional tuning proposals; distinguish authorship from shared visibility |
| Who are the users in this project? | A permitted, paginated directory or explicitly labeled observed identities for the selected scope; memory subjects, authors and registered members are different populations |
| Configure this project | Inspect available data and effective configuration, identify a supported goal, and draft a reviewed configuration plan with examples |

Resolve project to an existing registered organization/workspace/namespace/collection boundary and show it plainly. Do not invent a new tenant identity or silently treat every project as an organization-wide view. A user directory requires the applicable membership/directory permission; reading memories alone is not permission to enumerate all users. Omit hidden identities and aggregates that reveal their existence, and do not render the unset identity sentinel as a real user.

Reuse authorized entity-graph operations for relationships. A graph connection does not establish causality, truth or permission to read its endpoints. Check both endpoints and supporting facts; a hidden node or supporting source must not leak through edge labels or path explanations. Starting to persist or monitor a new relationship is a proposed write/subscription with its own approval, not an incidental effect of inspecting the graph.

The guided configuration flow analyses authorized data, usage and effective settings to propose custom extraction instructions, categories, namespace guidance and supported retrieval or other project settings. State which inputs were inspected and which were unavailable; do not claim full project analysis from a few retrieved examples. Ask for the user's goal when it cannot be inferred from the selected workflow, rather than assuming that every project should use every feature.

Each plan names the supported configuration target, current value/version, proposed value, evidence, expected behavior, affected agents/users, cost or latency implications, validation results and rollback limits. The UI shows the exact diff and lets an authorized approver accept individual actions, reject them or revise the plan. No configuration or domain content changes while drafting. Approval is explicit and scoped to that plan; a conversational suggestion or a starter click does not approve it. The assistant cannot configure additional rights or tools for itself.

Configuration applies prospectively unless the approved plan separately selects reprocessing of existing data. Evaluate proposed instructions/categories against representative examples and counterexamples before recommending them, and preserve source fidelity, required policy and available capabilities. Do not claim that custom settings are optimal without task-specific quality measurements. Use the same approval, authorization, concurrency and audit contract as record repair; this is one workflow in this issue, not an independent chatbot or configuration subsystem.

#### Reuse the existing diagnostic layer

Start with `namespace.audit`, `namespace.validate`, `namespace.summary`, `namespace.guide_get`, `mentor.brief`, `mentor.guide`, authorized agent activity, cost and retrieval-trace operations. Existing dashboard audit/mentor panels and the namespace optimization procedure already cover parts of this workflow. Extend gaps in these shared operations rather than implementing a second rule engine inside a system prompt.

Separate three kinds of result:

| Result | Examples | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract violation | A value violates a declared schema or verified provenance requirement | Server checks the applicable contract and returns evidence |
| Usage heuristic | Double-encoded values, documents as claims, excessive version churn, low search activity | Explain the rule, counts, exceptions and uncertainty; a warning is not proof of misuse |
| Semantic recommendation | Split a claim, choose another plane, change metadata or revise a contradiction | Cite the source and intended use; present a proposal requiring review |

Preserve existing finding codes and severity. Version new rules, scope them to the actual record type and namespace policy, and show skipped checks. Valid typed records, supported JSON values, exact-key workflows and intentionally unused planes must not be labeled incorrect merely because another representation is common. Distinguish a disabled feature, ingestion/index backlog, insufficient access and missing telemetry from agent misuse.

Return structured findings that the CLI, dashboard, MCP clients and chat can share. Each finding includes its rule/version, source operation, scope, observation window, computation time, count/denominator, sample limit, evidence references and revisions, coverage/skipped checks, proposed remedy and applicable uncertainty. Human-readable explanations must preserve those fields. A sampled report cannot claim complete coverage.

#### What agent usage evidence can prove

Distinguish a tool attempt, successful read, committed write, indexed write, returned retrieval hit, explicit client acknowledgment and task outcome. Operation counts alone do not show that a result reached the model, influenced its answer or improved the task. Report "retrieved" or "not observed in this window" when that is all the evidence supports.

Add missing telemetry only where a concrete question needs it: correlate existing request, session, agent and revision identifiers; mark gaps, retention limits, delayed events and sampling. Optional client/outcome evidence must declare its source and trust. Do not infer causal quality gains from a higher call count or present self-reported adoption as independent verification. Keep the assistant's own reads identifiable so its audits do not inflate the agent usage it reports.

#### Access to ClickHouse and Postgres

Use this access path:

`Chat client -> Loom assistant/tool dispatcher -> authorized Loom operations -> backend adapters -> ClickHouse and/or Postgres`

The backend has the database access needed to answer the question; the model receives bounded authorized tool results. Do not give the model, browser or shared chat agent database credentials or an unrestricted SQL tool.

- In ClickHouse-only deployments, reuse the existing authority and authorized retrieval paths.
- Under #142, read current state, grants, policy and committed job status from the Postgres authority; use ClickHouse for retrieval, historical analysis and telemetry where its documented contract permits. Revalidate search candidates and cite the actual visible revision. An old ClickHouse row cannot override a newer Postgres revision, erasure or grant.
- Declare cross-store report checkpoints, projection/event lag and partial results. Do not invent a transactionally consistent snapshot from independently read stores. Reauthorize referenced content before returning it; missing authority or revocation evidence fails closed. A backend outage is an unavailable check, not a healthy finding.
- Follow registered tenant/placement routing. The tenant is the organization, with namespace, collection and user restrictions preserved. The feature does not require a database per user or a database per tenant.
- Add bounded typed diagnostics for missing questions. Let backend code compile allowlisted aggregates and query templates with server-supplied authorization predicates. Keep arbitrary model-generated SQL out of the initial feature. Any later SQL capability needs separate qualification for parsing, functions, external access, execution budgets and authorization before aggregation.

A platform operator's infrastructure diagnostics and a customer's content assistant have different permissions. Namespace access does not imply access to all organization telemetry, another user's private collection or platform logs. Apply authorization before aggregation, sampling and model context construction; a filtered final answer cannot repair an earlier data leak.

#### Ordinary user questions

Use the existing authorized search/ask and exact-record operations for memories, knowledge, code, tracker, conversations and runs where available. Route document/data questions through #157 when that capability is released. Exact counts and numerical questions use authorized structured queries rather than estimates from retrieved text chunks.

Answers cite stable record/document identifiers and revisions, pages or source locators, and observation time. Distinguish source statements, calculated results and model interpretation. Resolve conflicting evidence explicitly and abstain when evidence is insufficient. Recommendations do not mark underlying claims verified or upgrade imported/derived provenance.

Provide general conversation when it is useful, but clearly separate it from an answer grounded in Loom. External web search or other connectors are optional and separately authorized. General conversation must not trigger a database-wide scan. The assistant's chat history is not automatically durable memory: saving claims or documents uses the ordinary admission and provenance workflow.

#### Chat interface and LibreChat decision

LibreChat supports MCP tools, reusable agents and per-user authentication mechanisms, making it a candidate for the first integration. Ship a documented integration using a small read-only tool set and evaluate it against a native dashboard chat using the same Loom operations.

Qualify a pinned release for identity delegation, transport compatibility, tool errors, citations, streaming/cancellation, tenant boundaries, deployment dependencies, license and maintenance. UI resource sharing is not Loom data authorization. Every tool call must use the initiating user's validated identity and no broader access than that user currently holds; neither a shared service token nor a user ID supplied in a prompt is a substitute.

Keep Loom as the authority for memory, documents, retrieval and diagnostic rules. LibreChat's own persistence may hold UI/conversation state under a declared policy; it must not silently create a second canonical memory store or independently index copies of tenant content. Inventory its transcripts, tool outputs, search caches and attachments for retention, erasure and #159 recovery coverage. An optional chat deployment must not add its databases to the mandatory Loom storage architecture.

#### Reviewed repairs

The first release investigates and recommends. A later repair workflow presents exact affected records, before/after values, destination plane, expected revisions and effects for approval by an authorized user. Use the existing namespace optimization procedure, dry runs and normal write operations; preserve redirects and provenance where applicable.

Approval binds to the displayed plan and content/revisions. Apply rechecks permissions, current state, pins, locks, blacklist and erasure fences. Changed records require a refreshed plan. Report partial results and make retries idempotent. No direct table updates, automatic deletion, unreviewed conflict resolution or background rewriting of a namespace. A request to audit is not permission to repair.

Category, instruction and setting changes need the same protection: retain a versioned diff and audit record, validate effective scope and policy, and reject stale approvals atomically. Add optimistic concurrency to an underlying configuration operation if it lacks it before exposing conversational apply; a read followed by an unconditional write is insufficient. Provide reviewed rollback for configuration, with separate status for any historical data reprocessing that rollback cannot undo.

#### Quality, scale and latency

Run deterministic checks without an LLM and use bounded, resumable background scans or maintained aggregates for expensive reports. Cache reusable facts and aggregates by effective authorization scope, rule version, window and backend checkpoint. Recheck authorization on read and invalidate or fence revoked/erased source content, including cached narratives and stored reports. Use incremental scans only with declared coverage and periodic reconciliation.

Keep analysis and model orchestration outside memory write/search critical paths. Bound query time, scanned rows/bytes, results, model context, tool calls, retries and concurrent jobs per tenant. Use workload isolation and fair scheduling; stream progress, support cancellation, and send expensive investigations to asynchronous jobs. A small question should fetch its evidence without running a whole-tenant audit.

Honor the organization's model policy, approved providers, spend caps and disabled-model mode. Deterministic reports remain available without synthesis. Retrieved documents, guides and tool text are untrusted data: they cannot grant tools, change policy, redirect credentials or approve repairs. The initial tool set excludes shell/code execution and arbitrary outbound destinations.

Before release, set numeric targets for finding precision/recall, citation correctness, answer correctness/abstention, p95/p99 latency, time to first output, scan/model cost and maximum impact on concurrent ingest/search. Compare candidate clients/models on the same labeled cases and evidence. Publish the measured tradeoffs; do not trade answer correctness for lower latency without stating the capability limit.

#### Delivery and acceptance

1. Inventory existing diagnostics, telemetry coverage and access contracts. Define missing structured findings and labeled evaluation cases.
2. Deliver read-only inspection, tuning proposals and cited questions through shared Loom tools, with a qualified optional LibreChat integration or a native interface chosen from the evaluation.
3. Add scheduled reports, scoped incremental analysis and alerts using the same rules and coverage contracts.
4. Add approved configuration changes and reviewed record repairs only after investigation, isolation and concurrency gates pass.

- [ ] Double encoding, oversized claim blobs, stale/conflicting records, valid typed records, intentional exact-key reads, delayed indexing and unavailable telemetry produce the expected distinct findings. Report precision/recall against reviewed labels.
- [ ] Answers cite the actual visible source revision and distinguish facts, heuristics, missing evidence and recommendations. A successful read is never reported as proven task adoption without supporting evidence.
- [ ] ClickHouse-only and ClickHouse+Postgres qualification includes stale projections, conflicting revisions, cross-store gaps, authority failover and unavailable backends. Unsupported checks are explicit.
- [ ] Cross-tenant, private collection, restricted telemetry and revoked-access tests cover tools, aggregates, samples, citations, chat sharing, reports, caches and exports. Revoked or erased content cannot reappear through saved chat context or cached answers; it is revalidated before reuse.
- [ ] Adversarial memories/documents/tool outputs cannot widen access, invoke unapproved tools, expose credentials or authorize repairs. Client-supplied scope is checked against validated identity on every tool call.
- [ ] Labeled ordinary questions cover memory, documents, code and supported structured queries, with contradiction and abstention cases. Mathematical answers match the authorized query result.
- [ ] Load qualification measures multi-tenant fairness, model/query cost, p95/p99 impact on normal ingest/search, cancellation, queue delay and recovery from interrupted scans. Fix numeric budgets before qualification; no paid benchmark is authorized by filing this issue.
- [ ] Read-only mode remains useful with models disabled. Any repair requires an approved plan and passes stale-revision, protected-record, idempotency and partial-failure tests through ordinary operations.
- [ ] Inspect and Tune perform no domain or configuration mutations; previews have only declared temporary/job/audit effects. User/agent/session views distinguish authorship from visibility. Category, instruction and setting proposals name their real scope, affected consumers, evidence and future-versus-historical effects; Apply rejects an unauthorized, stale or widened plan. Historical reprocessing requires separate selection.
- [ ] Scoped conversation starters cover project inventory, user analysis, permitted user enumeration and fact relationships. Tests distinguish members from observed identities and shared visibility from authorship; hidden users, nodes, edges and supporting sources cannot leak through counts or explanations. Configure-project tests cover per-action review, changed settings after preview, partial application, rollback and separately approved historical reprocessing.
- [ ] Chat persistence and derived reports are included in erasure, retention and backup inventories. Integration dependencies, supported versions and backend capabilities are documented.

Update applicable operation definitions, generated SDK/MCP surfaces, CLI/dashboard, policy settings, architecture and operational documentation as each workstream ships. Do not advertise a proposed operation or client capability as already implemented.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Existing audit/mentor panels and CLI: already answer deterministic questions; keep them. Chat adds investigation across findings and cited explanations rather than replacing their rule engine.
- A bot with direct CH/PG administrator access: bypasses application policy, exposes unrelated data and couples prompts to storage schemas. Server-owned typed tools preserve authority and budgets.
- An LLM that reads the database and assigns one efficiency score: lacks ground truth and hides missing telemetry. Return inspectable findings and task-specific measurements.
- Require LibreChat for every deployment: adds operational and persistence commitments before validating the workflow. Keep it optional until the client comparison establishes its fit.
- Automatically repair every warning: heuristics can flag legitimate designs. Use a reviewed plan through normal admission and concurrency checks.

### Where the need comes from

The need is mine, an AI tool helped shape the proposal

### Additional context

Feature proposal based on documented capabilities, not a reproduced runtime failure. No live tenant audit, database export, repair, client deployment or paid benchmark was run. The linked Loom documents were checked against main at the pinned revision.

Related: #142 (Postgres authority and ClickHouse retrieval/history), #157 (document and structured-data questions), #159 (portable bundles and recovery), and the in-progress storage implementation #158. This assistant depends on their released contracts without changing their authority boundaries.

Existing Loom capabilities:

- [Namespace health and mentor](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/features/namespaces-and-sharing.md)
- [Namespace audit and reviewed optimization](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/guides/optimize-namespace.md)
- [Mentor evidence and partial-result fields](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/reference/operations/mentor.md)
- [Agent activity, usage and cost](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/features/observability/cost-and-usage.md)
- [Existing dashboard audit and mentor surfaces](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/features/dashboard.md)
- [Operator extraction policy scope, permissions and precedence](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/blob/fda33a7c98345fae55db670d9bb004d4485aa707/docs/features/memory/extraction.md#operator-extraction-policy)

Client references: [LibreChat MCP tools](https://www.librechat.ai/docs/features/mcp), [agents](https://www.librechat.ai/docs/features/agents), [MCP authentication configuration](https://www.librechat.ai/docs/configuration/librechat_yaml/object_structure/mcp_servers), [access control](https://www.librechat.ai/docs/features/access_control), and [default deployment dependencies](https://www.librechat.ai/docs/local/docker). These establish available integration mechanisms, not a verified Loom integration or permission-equivalence guarantee.

items.title: Feature: reusable ontology-pack integration contracts and conformance
items.body:
### 2026-10-14 accepted tenant-isolation checkpoint

Public authenticated dispatch plus two pinned Spanner databases and 10 workers is verified for Core+User+Memory versus Core+PDLC+Memory:184 main + 12 restart assertions, independent audit and Astra acceptance. Final data retained; no database creation/deletion. [Verification and scope](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/4bd47dd/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/tenant-isolation-verification.md).

This checkpoint does not close this issue. Tenant native webhooks/global metrics/import/cursors/prune/replay/reconsolidate, general pending/draining/forced termination and pilot readiness remain outside the accepted proof; hierarchy #49 remains parked. Earlier dated source observations below remain historical context, while the feature requirements remain open.

## Latest checkpoint — User attachment/retry slice, 2026-10-13

- Completed and independently verified the bounded UA01–UA07 slice: 277 accepted Spanner assertions across Core+User, Core+User+Memory and User-off Core+PDLC.
- #20 interest attachment and #59 canonical User personalization are resolved; #59 is a native sub-issue of this umbrella.
- Newly discovered #60 is also a native sub-issue: production consolidation shutdown can leave SDK writes after task completion. It remains open and is a pilot prerequisite. Healthy harness coordination is not a production fix.
- #42, #39, #41 and this umbrella remain open for their broader scope. Enrichment #29, wider combinations, tenant isolation and the pilot have not started in this checkpoint. Stop for stakeholder review before the next stage.
- Code: `782ab1e`; [walkthrough and acceptance evidence](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/61475be/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/user-attachment-verification.md); [Astra final review](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/61475be/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/user-attachment-review/astra-final-review.md). Final assessment data is retained at epoch29 with matching post-process fingerprints; historical migration remains excluded.

The original buckets below remain the owning feature structure; no additional feature bucket is required for these defects. Dated earlier execution/context statements retain their original evidence boundary.

---

## Latest G04 milestone — verified 2026-10-08

31real-Spanner checks passed for Change→Release→failed/successful deployment, with exact links/properties/evidence and no-write invalid/retry checks. PDLC3.0 scopes deployment identities by repo/service (catalog26events). #47 is the newly confirmed identity bug, fixed and cloud-verified. Evidence update: https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/issues/34#issuecomment-6053441691

This umbrella remains OPEN for remaining acceptance. No new feature bucket; no separate foundation reruns or migration. G05 requires separate approval and has not started. This checkpoint supersedes older milestone/status paragraphs retained below.

---

## Current G03 milestone — 2026-10-08

Goal Three verifies explicit planning → ticket → PR → reviews and verification through ordinary Engram HTTP, five workers, real Spanner and actual retrieval. PDLC2.1 adds bounded reference mappings, reviewer recording, edge-level commit SHA and trace weights; event count remains25. Both changes-requested/approved reviews and failed/successful test runs remain visible. Missing references do not cause invented links; invalid nested keys/verdicts/outcomes reject before ledger append. Detailed final evidence and remaining work are linked in the G03 comment.

This issue remains OPEN for acceptance beyond the bounded journey. G04 and later remain unstarted pending explicit stakeholder approval. Historical migration is excluded from all current disposable-experiment goals; in-run revision/retry/recovery checks remain functional coverage. Public multi-tenant dispatch and native document/source adapter compatibility are not signed off by this single-bound normalized-producer experiment.

---

## Current scope decision — 2026-10-08: disposable experiments

Stakeholder explicitly excludes historical-data migration, old-pack identity conversion and cross-version historical upgrade work from ALL current goals. Do not spend analysis/implementation/review effort on migration or treat it as a completion blocker. Focus on actual Engram ingestion, ontology projection and retrieval on real Spanner using disposable data. In-run revision history and same-pack retry/recovery remain covered. Existing migration-only scenarios/tickets stay deferred, never falsely passed or closed. Goal Three is still unstarted pending approval.

Persisted goal-wide scope and verification standard: https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/9294db7/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-08-small-goal-inventory.md . This scope decision overrides historical migration acceptance text below for current goal execution.

---

## Current verified milestone — 2026-10-08

Goal Two verifies the bounded normalized PRD → Requirements ← HLD ← LLD planning journey, revision-specific approval and supersession, duplicates/conflicts/rejections, missing-reference fill and focused retrieval through actual Engram HTTP, five workers and real Spanner. Core remains mandatory; memory/user are disabled for this configuration. PDLC 2.0 extends the catalog from 23 to 25 and changes Requirement/DesignElement revision keys. Historical migration is not proved. #46 is the newly discovered retrieval defect; its final evidence is linked in the milestone comment.

This issue remains OPEN: G02 does not prove all PDLC journeys, whole-pack or multi-tenant compatibility. The original 32 child issues remain tracked; newly discovered #45 and #46 are additional children under #34. The exact executed foundation snapshot is preserved with the evidence; unrelated local foundation work remains preserved. G03 and later require stakeholder authorization. Detailed verification and run links are in the G02 milestone comment below.

---

## Historical context — 2026-10-07 (superseded by current G02 status above)

**Scope:** Feature #34 owns composable packs and agreed journeys, with mandatory core, optional memory/user, tenant-specific database/bundle routing and both retrieval paths.

**Required proof:** All originally reconciled 32 native sub-issues plus newly discovered #45 and linked prerequisites remain tracked. #41 is separate cloud sign-off, not evidence that this feature is complete.

**Shared decisions:** Core is mandatory. Optional memory/user/domain capabilities compose through declared dependencies, without pairwise hardcoded flows. Authenticated tenant identity resolves its authorized Spanner database and pack bundle; processing and retrieval use that same context. Never infer authorization from agent_id, caller-chosen database or artifact IDs.

**Tracking and status:** Parent #34 holds the reconciled six-bucket scope; #35/#42 own composition/capability controls, #43 tenant routing, #39 exact conformance and #41 real-Spanner execution. This is a scope/context reconciliation, not a fresh runtime verification. The issue remains open; historical reproductions below retain their original revision, backend and run scope. Local slice-one work includes optional contracts for all 23 PDLC events, path checks and bounded fixtures; admission, complete oracles, capability routing and cloud acceptance remain unfinished. Historical memory probes are diagnostic evidence, not cloud acceptance. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration are required. Pinned documentation links below are historical published snapshots; newer local reports/run artifacts remain unpublished unless explicitly linked to a published revision.

---

Engram needs a reusable, versioned agreement between ontology packs and the engine so a new compatible pack can produce its declared artifacts, evidence and retrieval behavior without pack-specific engine code. Loading YAML or accepting an event does not currently establish that agreement.

This is an umbrella **feature/enhancement**, not a replacement for existing defect issues. PDLC is the full-pack acceptance case; CRM and an unfamiliar fixture pack establish generality. Astra medium review verdict: **ready with conditions**. Blocking decisions must be resolved before their affected implementation slices; no compatibility sign-off is implied.

### Deliverables
- Explicit pack capability/activation checks, owned event contracts and authorized cross-pack subscribers.
- Reviewed source-to-event mappings and shared validation/trust across single, batch, import and webhook ingress.
- Defined event-to-artifact semantics: missing versus null, bounded list expansion, conditional/no-op behavior, ordering/stale-write policy and property ownership.
- Immutable duplicate policy for same ID/different content, including source-binding revision changes.
- API/worker interpretation compatibility and available historical rules before accepting new metadata; safe replay/upgrade policy.
- Exact relationship/transition evidence and correlated applied/skipped/deferred/failed/unknown processing outcomes, reusing current surfaces where possible.
- Reusable pack conformance fixtures with expected normalized events, exact graph deltas, forbidden effects and retrieval answers/evidence.

### Implementation sequence and review findings
| Slice | Required design/acceptance work | Existing issues |
|---|---|---|
|1: contracts and fixtures|PE-01 missing/null/cardinality; PE-02 ordering/property ownership; PE-04 duplicates; PE-05 revision/obligations; PE-06 capabilities; PE-08 exact fixtures for all23 PDLC events plus third pack|#4 #5 #8 #9 #17 #22 #28 #29|
|2: shared ingress|All-route validation/trust; persisted metadata round trip and compatible/refused N/N-1 worker behavior; valid/invalid unfamiliar pack; uncertain commit and conflicting duplicates|#4 #5 #17 #28; prerequisites #27 and applicable #26|
|3–4: recovery and artifacts|PE-02 A/B/A convergence; PE-03 claim/relationship evidence; PE-07 completion observations; worker ordering, missing endpoints and retention|#8 #9 #10 #14 #18 #19 #20 #29 #30|
|5: retrieval|Exact supporting events and excluded edges; uncertain negative answers; bounded pagination/deadlines|#6 #7 #24 #25 #31 #32|
|6: historical acceptance|Replay/rebuild/cutover, pack visibility and complete bounded Spanner journeys|#11 #12 #13 #21 #22|

PE identifiers refer to the persisted Astra report below. Existing issue associations are not evidence those issues already contain or implement the expanded scope. Track the disposition of each finding here and update affected implementation issues before executing each slice. Do not open eight duplicate bugs automatically.

### Acceptance checklist
- [ ] Resolve blocking contract decisions in slice1 and document the chosen policies; do not assume last-write-wins.
- [ ] Every one of23 PDLC event declarations has a contract and exact supported/no-op/extraction-only/refused classification; the current local classification is 16 deterministic, one extraction-only and six missing mappings.
- [ ] Each event has fixture-linked normalized values, exact artifacts/evidence or deliberate no-op, invalid inputs and retrieval expectations.
- [ ] CRM and an unfamiliar compatible pack exercise the same mechanisms without adding engine type-name switches.
- [ ] Test omitted versus null fields, mismatched lists/write bounds, A/B/A and competing subscriber updates, same-ID changed content, revision mismatch, disabled required worker, duplicate/replay and partial failure.
- [ ] Separate real public records/documents, reconstructed webhook wrappers and synthetic cases; retain source gaps explicitly. Current captures have not been executed.
- [ ] Run applicable end-to-end journeys through actual Engram→Spanner, recording bounds, fingerprints, exact outcomes, defects and cleanup in the existing run ledger. No Redis/Neo4j runners or memory substitution for these cloud journeys.
- [ ] Independent review and targeted acceptance evidence support each completed slice; no blanket compatibility claim from source inspection or counts.

### Scope guardrails
Reuse current registry, adapters, projector, consumers, evaluation and tracking. Add only demonstrated missing checks/metadata. Automatic adapter generation through PRs, general raw-capture infrastructure and a new orchestration service are outside this feature's critical path. No Redis-to-Spanner migration. Future packs must stay within supported DSL/capabilities; arbitrary ontology formats/algorithms are not promised.

### Persisted design and evidence (published documentation snapshot)
- docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review-prompt.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md

Astra review was code/document/corpus inspection only; no new runtime tests or cloud calls. Existing defect and compatibility statuses remain unchanged.


## Sub-issue implementation map — reconciled after pack/tenant discussions

These are the original six feature buckets, with the newer requirements incorporated. Buckets group scope; implementation follows the dependencies and reviewed slices. Core is mandatory and cannot be disabled. All accepted normalized events use the common Event envelope, enforced in ingestion code; domain payload contracts add checks. Only selected optional capabilities may be assumed available.

| Original feature bucket | Concrete scope, including latest discussion | Owning issues |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Pack contracts and activation | Compose required core with optional memory/user and compatible domains; dependency/version/conflict checks; explicit reusable capabilities; retain specialized workers without pack-combination branches; API/worker agreement; payload contracts and authenticated source trust. | #4 #5 #35 #42 |
| 2. Source mapping and ingestion | Explicit raw-source-to-normalized-event adapters; common envelope plus selected pack payload validation across single/batch/import/webhooks; duplicate conflicts and source/normalization identity; tenant binding before append; clear stored-versus-processed receipt. | #17 #28 #37; shared contract work #4/#5 and tenant context #43 |
| 3. Projection, ordering and evidence | Core Event/history plus selected pack rules; field mapping, omitted/null, bounded fan-out, ordering and ownership; shared Entity writes; transition/relationship provenance; missing endpoints and late causal links. No schema-based guessing of missing mappings. | #8 #9 #18 #20 #29 #30 #36 |
| 4. Worker completion and recovery | Enabled worker responsibilities and subscriptions; extraction/projection handoffs; retries and unprocessed-content retention; applied/skipped/deferred/failed outcomes; keep core summaries/retention independently controlled from optional memory. | #10 #14 #19 #38; composition gates #42 |
| 5. Retrieval and conformance acceptance | Audit both retrieval paths for fixed optional-pack assumptions and fallback behavior; selection-aware intents/seeds/traversal/evidence, historical disabled-data visibility, pagination/deadlines and honest incomplete answers; exact fixture proof across all declared PDLC events, agreed PRD→requirements→HLD/LLD and other journeys, CRM, unfamiliar pack and compatible combinations. | #6 #7 #22 #24 #25 #31 #32 #39 #40; capability gates #42 #45 |
| 6. Versioning, replay and historical acceptance | Interpretation identity and available historical rules; upgrades, disable/re-enable/catch-up, replay, incomplete rebuild failures and same-backend graph cutover preserving ledger; historical evidence and visibility policies. | #11 #12 #13 #21; bundle agreement #35 |

### Cross-cutting requirement: tenant isolation

#43 is a native feature sub-issue spanning every bucket. Confirmed direction: one Spanner database per tenant; a shared Spanner instance is permitted. Resolve tenant from authentication to authorized database plus composed pack/capability bundle. Handshake, ingress, workers/checkpoints, graph/search, retrieval/evidence/caches/cursors, replay/upgrades, admin/maintenance and evaluation must preserve that identity. Do not trust caller-selected database/agent identity, mutate global active routing per request or fall back silently. Different tenant pack selections and colliding IDs require adversarial verification. Separate Engram deployments are not required by this product decision.

### Cross-cutting proof: Spanner compatibility

#41 is a separate linked umbrella, not a duplicate feature or reparenting of defects. Track the 65-row baseline (14 passed, 36 failed, 13 not fully executed, 2 blocked at the recorded checkpoint) separately from new composition/tenant acceptance groups COMP-01–06 and TEN-01–03. These nine groups are planned, not executed; bind exact executable inputs and expected graph/read/forbidden effects before running. All cloud execution goes through Engram on real Spanner with recorded runs, redacted evidence, linked defects and independent review. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration. No compatibility sign-off from schema loading, local probes, 2xx receipts or plausible answers.

### Sequence clarification

Start by defining and enforcing composable pack/capability boundaries (#42/#35) with mandatory core, and tenant/database/pack routing (#43/#35). Define full event contracts and exact fixtures, enforce shared ingress, harden projection and worker handoffs, verify both retrieval paths and full agreed journeys, then complete historical/recovery acceptance. Prove a bounded end-to-end path early on Spanner and expand; it is not full feature completion. Existing partial runtime work stays explicitly partial.

Existing source/ingress/projection/retrieval/replay bugs remain reused. Adapter/schema/lifecycle prerequisites #23/#26/#27 and pruning #33 remain tracked in their existing waves. Optionality and tenant requirements were reviewed by Astra medium in the local pack-optionality report/probes; those artifacts are currently unpublished, and issue bodies carry the concrete scope/acceptance. The former combined autonomous goal is paused and retired from the execution plan. Only G01 (eight PR activity scenarios through actual Engram on real Spanner) is currently authorized. Every later goal requires explicit user approval. The original 32 sub-issues remain tracked, with new retrieval defect #45 added as a native sub-issue in bucket 5. Subsequent implementation/review/run comments carry their precise evidence scope; this reconciliation text alone is not runtime or compatibility proof.

## Published implementation context

- [This issue’s slice, scope and review gates](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pack-integration-context.md) — slices **1–6**.
- [Full design and implementation sequence](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md).
- [Astra medium review and conformance requirements](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md).
- [PDLC event contracts inventory](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv), [payload experiment matrix](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv), and [public-source corpus and remaining gaps](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md).

Links are pinned to documentation commit `5e9c883` on `feature/engram-walkthrough`. This publishes design context, not unfinished runtime code or new compatibility results. Raw execution artifacts remain local; the context index states the evidence limits. All acceptance checklists retain their current open/scoped status.


## Connected PDLC journey coverage

PDLC journey coverage is now tracked by sub-issue #40. The23-event inventory is not a completeness gate. Define schema/source/mapping/evidence coverage for PRD→requirements→HLD→LLD first; continue the bounded generic engine foundation while implementing the pack changes behind its prerequisites. Full-PDLC acceptance under #39 requires the agreed connected journeys.


## 2026-10-13 — bounded enrichment checkpoint

Enrichment ordering (#29) is verified and independently reviewed: EN01–EN07 passed across Core, Core+User, Core+User+Memory, Core+PDLC and Core+PDLC+Memory on real Spanner, 58 assertions each (290 total). Authenticated ingestion, actual workers, pending/restart recovery, exact public annotations, stale projection/duplicate preservation, provider degradation and partial vector-write recovery are covered. Source/runtime commit79d8779; evidence41f2e37.

[Stakeholder walkthrough and exact results](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/41f2e37/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/enrichment-ordering-verification.md); [Astra completeness review](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/41f2e37/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/enrichment-ordering-review/astra-final-review.md). Final assessment data retained at epoch36; fresh owner/fingerprint, all215 source hashes, five prior exports and final/retained snapshots verified. Failed01 (UUID subgraph access defect #61) and failed02 (omitted OntologyState oracle corrected explicitly) are preserved.

This proves common enrichment under the five configurations, not all optional-pack producers or concurrent tenant isolation. Existing retry elapsed-time/repeated-restart limits, cached predecessor #18, shutdown #60 and UUID access #61 remain open. No historical migration, ANN quality, live Neo4j or pilot claim. Next slice/pilot not started. No new umbrella needed; all findings fit #34.

## 2026-10-14 — bounded consolidation shutdown checkpoint

Consolidation shutdown (#60) is verified and independently reviewed: all seven bounded lifecycle cases passed on real Spanner, 109 assertions. Actual SDK Summary transactions were held after mutation scheduling; cooperative stop and three parent cancellations stayed unfinished until complete cycle drain. Both controlled SDK and subscription fencing paths joined before propagating errors; ordinary storage failure kept its existing logged-cycle policy and rolled back. Every successful admitted cycle itself committed episode/session/agent summaries. Fresh restart preserved exact Summary/Episode identities and twelve evidence/lineage edges.

[Stakeholder walkthrough and exact results](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/cf8bec8/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/consolidation-shutdown-verification.md); [Astra final completeness review](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/cf8bec8/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/consolidation-shutdown-review/astra-final-review.md). Runtime/harness9e3ff0a; evidencecf8bec8. Final assessment data retained at epoch37 after a verified epoch36 export; fresh owner/all-table fingerprints, all216 runtime/script hashes, exact public source/Episode evidence and SDK commit/rollback records checked. Targeted73 passed; broad2831 passed/13 skipped predates the final extra test-only continuation case and excludes the known PDLC evaluation-gate file.

Scope: cooperative stop and public run-task cancellation of ConsolidationConsumer, including optional Memory Episode production in Core+PDLC+Memory. No external consolidation-lock shutdown workaround or manual graph repair. No process-kill, retroactively detached work, direct private-child cancellation, general worker rewrite, concurrent-tenant, ANN quality, live Neo4j or pilot claim. #18/#61 and wider composition/isolation remain separate. No new umbrella needed; this fits #34. Next slice/pilot not started.

### 2026-10-14 checkpoint — #61 resolved

UUID subgraph access fixed and independently reviewed.228 live assertions;2834 local tests passed/13 skipped with documented evaluation-gate exclusion. Final assessment epoch39 retained. [Verification walkthrough](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/08cf908/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/subgraph-access-verification.md). #61 closed; this umbrella remains open. Broader composition/isolation/pilot not started.


### 2026-10-14 checkpoint — selected combinations verified

Core; Core+User; Core+User+Memory; Core+PDLC; Core+PDLC+Memory passed 793 real-Spanner assertions after #62 identity/evidence correction and complete rerun. Astra accepted the bounded checkpoint. Final assessment epoch48 retained. [Walkthrough/evidence](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/ae0f46c/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pack-combination-verification.md). This issue remains open; public/concurrent tenant isolation and pilot work have not started.

items.body:

Stakeholder explicitly excludes historical-data migration, old-pack identity conversion and cross-version historical upgrade work from ALL current goals. Do not spend analysis/implementation/review effort on migration or treat it as a completion blocker. ---

## Current agreed context — 2026-10-07

**Scope:** Real-Spanner compatibility remains unsigned: baseline 65 rows is separate from planned composition/tenant extensions and feature acceptance.

**Required proof:** Maintain all scenario assertions, publish redacted evidence, resolve failures/partial/blockers and verify tenant-bound handshake, ingestion, workers, both retrieval paths and operations.

**Shared decisions:** Core is mandatory. Optional memory/user/domain capabilities compose through declared dependencies, without pairwise hardcoded flows. Authenticated tenant identity resolves its authorized Spanner database and pack bundle; processing and retrieval use that same context. Never infer authorization from agent_id, caller-chosen database or artifact IDs.

**Tracking and status:** Parent #34 holds the reconciled six-bucket scope; #35/#42 own composition/capability controls, #43 tenant routing, #39 exact conformance and #41 real-Spanner execution. This is a scope/context reconciliation, not a fresh runtime verification. The issue remains open; historical reproductions below retain their original revision, backend and run scope. Historical memory probes are diagnostic evidence, not cloud acceptance. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration are required. Pinned documentation links below are historical published snapshots; newer local reports/run artifacts remain unpublished unless explicitly linked to a published revision.

---

Track Engram’s end-to-end compatibility with real Google Cloud Spanner. This is the execution and sign-off umbrella; #34 owns reusable ontology-pack integration and its implementation slices. Existing defects remain linked rather than duplicated or reparented.

## Baseline and evidence

Current baseline: **65 scenarios: 14 passed, 36 failed, 13 not fully executed, 2 blocked. No compatibility sign-off.** `not_run` includes partial execution whose complete assertions remain open. These are scenario counts, not unique defect counts. The 36 failed scenarios map to existing defects across #4–#33; local fixes and scoped reviews do not close cloud scenarios without reruns.

- [Scenario matrix](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/scenarios.csv)
- [Execution ledger](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs.jsonl)
- [Findings](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/findings.md)
- [Compatibility and implementation plan](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883/docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md)

The published links are immutable baseline snapshots. Current working records live at the same repository paths. Raw `runs/` artifacts are currently local and unpublished; a recorded evidence path is not a public artifact link. Publish reviewable, redacted evidence before final sign-off.

## Execution rules

- Exercise Engram APIs, workers, admin tools and retrieval against real Spanner. No Redis or Neo4j runners; memory tests cannot substitute for cloud acceptance.
- Track every run in the execution ledger before starting. Record scenario IDs, source revision and working diff, configuration, resource scope, observations, linked defects, cleanup and final outcomes. Keep credentials out of evidence.
- Use the authorized disposable databases `engram` and `engram-compat-target` on `portiq-mvp/engram-experiment`; preserve databases and schema. Serialize destructive fixture resets and record their scope.
- Classify failures as shared Engram engine, Engram Spanner adapter, test harness or environment. Link each confirmed product defect and rerun affected scenarios after fixes.
- Test ontology updates and rebuilt-graph cutover within Spanner while preserving the ledger. Redis-to-Spanner migration is outside scope.
- Keep this checklist and the CSV synchronized. Check a scenario only when all its listed assertions have passed. Track partial assertions in subchecks; do not promote partial results to passes.

## Full baseline checklist

### Failed — 36

- [ ] **BOOT-01** — startup; `API lifespan + worker CLI`. Verify: all five ports Spanner; independent processes share data; shutdown/clients. Defects: #26. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-04`.
- [ ] **BOOT-03** — schema; `API/worker startup`. Verify: missing/wrong database/schema/dimensions/index readiness; creation disabled. Defects: #23. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-04`.
- [ ] **ING-01** — single; `POST /v1/events`. Verify: valid/invalid fields/payload; naive/aware/future time; namespaces; trusted ID. Defects: #4, #5, #15. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-01`.
- [ ] **ING-02** — batch; `POST /v1/events/batch`. Verify: empty/max/max+1; mixed outcomes; duplicate/conflicting IDs; indices. Defects: #4, #5. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-07`.
- [ ] **ING-03** — transport; `single/batch/import`. Verify: gzip truncation/CRC/trailing/multiple members; byte/decoded size; timeout. Defects: #16. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-01`.
- [ ] **ING-04** — idempotence; `single/batch/import retry`. Verify: uncertain commit; concurrent same ID; changed contents; committed prefix. Defects: #28. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **HOOK-03** — webhook boundary; `signed webhook routes`. Verify: signature/secret/unsupported source; changed delivery redelivery; malformed nested shape; timestamp; fanout partial writes; stalled body. Defects: #4, #17. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-01`.
- [ ] **LED-01** — JSON; `ingest → worker reads`. Verify: nested float tags/null/bool/list/unicode/datetime; lossless round-trip. Defects: #27. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-04`.
- [ ] **LED-02** — ordering/paging; `ingest/import → worker/retrieval`. Verify: commit/batch ties; page0/1/many; same-session arrivals; predecessor; unknown/missing docs. Defects: #18, #19, #21, #30. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **SUB-02** — retries; `actual worker loops`. Verify: live transient/permanent failure; bounded backoff; DLQ; pending beyond one page; partial ACK. Defects: #14. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-04`.
- [ ] **SUB-03** — restart; `worker stop/kill/restart`. Verify: crash before/after graph write/ACK; orphan pagination; surviving replica; stop during retry. Defects: #14, #19. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-02`.
- [ ] **SUB-04** — concurrency; `multiple worker processes`. Verify: same/interleaved sessions; conflicting transactions; repeated side effects; per-session order. Defects: #18. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-04`.
- [ ] **PROJ-01** — structure; `projection CLI loop`. Verify: Event/FOLLOWS/CAUSED_BY; missing parent; session end; idle/stop flush; cache eviction. Defects: #18, #30. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **PROJ-03** — pack lookups; `projection CLI loop`. Verify: direct/list/latest/prefix; limit boundaries; no silent subset; absent endpoint. Defects: #8. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-05`.
- [ ] **PROJ-04** — lifecycle/evidence; `projection CLI loop`. Verify: guarded transitions/order; state evidence; planning error/DLQ; partial write failure. Defects: #9, #18. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-05`.
- [ ] **ENR-01** — enrichment; `enrichment CLI loop`. Verify: keyword/importance/embedding persistence; missing doc/node; projection lag; duplicate delivery. Defects: #29. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **ENR-02** — embedding failure; `enrichment CLI loop`. Verify: disabled/failing/wrong dimension/zero vector; provider vs storage error. Defects: #14. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **EXT-02** — user extraction; `extraction CLI loop`. Verify: profiles/preferences/skills/interests; contradiction supersession; evidence; reobservation. Defects: #20. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-01`.
- [ ] **EXT-03** — extraction races; `extraction CLI loop`. Verify: projection lag; partial writes; repeated delivery/restart; limits. Defects: #10, #29. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-06`.
- [ ] **PEXT-02** — pack evidence; `pack_extraction CLI loop`. Verify: authoritative node/link preservation; known-item caps; missing endpoints; extraction first. Defects: #10. Latest run: `20261006-cloud-coverage-reconciliation-05`.

- Add explicit versioned scenario rows for those extensions before execution; preserve the 65-row baseline and show the added denominator separately. Cover the complete PDLC event inventory, CRM and an unfamiliar pack, including coexistence, rather than treating one successful PR example as pack conformance.
