items.title: Spec：企业共享知识库在线入库、持久化会话与权限控制

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified and ready for implementation by an agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

当前系统已经能够通过 Manifest 和命令行脚本解析银行监管 Word、PDF、Excel 文件，建立 Qdrant 向量索引和 BM25 关键词索引，并通过 FastAPI/React 完成带原文证据的问答。但它仍是一次性建库与浏览器页面内会话模式：企业成员没有统一登录，刷新页面后对话消失，历史消息由浏览器直接随请求发送，知识库维护者也不能通过网页持续上传知识文档、查看入库状态或安全更新企业共享知识库。

这使系统无法作为一个企业长期维护的知识工作台使用。企业需要在不重建整套系统、不暴露半成品索引、不中断旧版本检索的前提下，允许获授权的知识库维护者持续增加资料；企业成员需要拥有自己的持久化对话，并由服务端在受控 token 预算内管理上下文。与此同时，公开作品仓库需要清楚区分已经实现的可信 RAG 能力和本规格新增的企业化能力。

## Solution

把现有可信 RAG 问答系统扩展为“单企业、企业共享知识库”的受控应用：所有用户通过 Keycloak 登录；企业成员使用同一套企业共享知识库提问，但每个人只管理自己的对话历史；知识库维护者可以上传受支持的知识文档，并在知识库管理页查看文档和入库任务。

上传后，后端在 PostgreSQL 中创建知识文档、文档版本和入库任务，把原始文件写入 MinIO，再通过 Redis 队列交给后台 Worker 解析、切块并构建 Qdrant 与 BM25 检索产物。新版本只有在所有产物完整成功后才成为当前有效版本；失败或处理中产生的内容不能被问答检索，旧版本继续服务。问答服务从 PostgreSQL 读取当前对话，按预算组合历史摘要、近期消息和检索证据，再调用 `deepseek-v4-flash` 生成可追溯原文的回答。

正式 React 前端按照已确认静态原型实现登录页、可折叠历史侧栏、问答区、账户菜单、知识库管理页和上传弹窗。原型是视觉与交互基准，不作为后端能力已经存在的证明。

## User Stories

1. As an 企业成员, I want to use an enterprise login, so that only authorized people can access the system.
2. As an 企业成员, I want my login session to survive page refreshes, so that I do not need to log in repeatedly during normal work.
3. As an 企业成员, I want to log out from the account menu, so that I can safely end my session on a shared device.
4. As an 企业成员, I want to see my identity and business role, so that I know which capabilities are available to me.
5. As an 企业成员, I want the question page to remain the default workspace, so that knowledge retrieval stays the product's primary purpose.
6. As an 企业成员, I want to create a new 对话, so that an unrelated question starts with a clean context boundary.
7. As an 企业成员, I want my 对话 to be saved automatically, so that refreshing or signing in again does not lose my work.
8. As an 企业成员, I want to see my recent 对话 in the left sidebar, so that I can resume earlier work quickly.
9. As an 企业成员, I want to search my 对话历史, so that I can locate an earlier investigation by title.
10. As an 企业成员, I want the first question to generate a useful 对话 title, so that the history list is understandable without manual work.
11. As an 企业成员, I want to rename a 对话 inline, so that I can give it a clearer business name without opening another dialog.
12. As an 企业成员, I want deletion of a 对话 to require confirmation, so that an accidental click does not destroy useful history.
13. As an 企业成员, I want to delete my own 对话, so that obsolete or sensitive working history is no longer shown to me.
14. As an 企业成员, I want other members to be unable to view or modify my 对话历史, so that personal working context remains isolated.
15. As a 知识库维护者, I want the same privacy rules to apply to my 对话, so that maintenance privileges do not expose other members' conversations.
16. As an 企业成员, I want follow-up questions to use the current 对话 context, so that I do not need to repeat the subject and prior conclusions.
17. As an 企业成员, I want the service to control how much history enters the model, so that long conversations remain reliable and affordable.
18. As an 企业成员, I want older context to be summarized when necessary, so that important prior facts remain available without sending the entire history.
19. As an 企业成员, I want each answer to cite original evidence, so that I can verify important banking conclusions.
20. As an 企业成员, I want streaming progress and answers, so that I can see that a complex query is still being processed.
21. As an 企业成员, I want failures to return a safe and actionable message, so that internal exception or credential details are never exposed.
22. As an 企业成员, I want the sidebar to be collapsible, so that I can give more screen space to long answers.
23. As an 企业成员, I want knowledge-base controls to be hidden from me, so that the interface only shows actions I am allowed to use.
24. As a 知识库维护者, I want a 知识库管理 entry in the sidebar, so that I can switch from asking questions to maintaining shared knowledge.
25. As a 知识库维护者, I want to see knowledge-document totals grouped by 成功、进行中 and 失败, so that I understand the current ingestion health.
26. As a 知识库维护者, I want to list knowledge documents with 序号、文件名、大小、入库状态、更新时间 and 操作, so that I can inspect the shared knowledge base efficiently.
27. As a 知识库维护者, I want to search documents by filename, so that I can find a document without scanning the whole list.
28. As a 知识库维护者, I want to filter documents by 成功、进行中 and 失败, so that I can focus on items requiring attention.
29. As a 知识库维护者, I want paginated document results, so that the page remains usable for a large enterprise knowledge base.
30. As a 知识库维护者, I want to open document details, so that I can inspect its original filename, size, uploader, timestamps, current version and latest task result.
31. As a 知识库维护者, I want to upload one supported knowledge document from the browser, so that new enterprise material can enter the shared knowledge base without command-line access.
32. As a 知识库维护者, I want the server to reject unsupported formats and oversized files before queuing work, so that invalid uploads do not consume ingestion capacity.
33. As a 知识库维护者, I want upload acceptance to return immediately with an 入库任务, so that parsing and indexing do not block the browser request.
34. As a 知识库维护者, I want a newly accepted document to display 进行中, so that I can see that background work has started.
35. As a 知识库维护者, I want an 入库任务 to end as either 成功 or 失败, so that there is no ambiguous terminal state.
36. As a 知识库维护者, I want failed ingestion to record a safe failure reason, so that I can understand whether the file or system needs attention.
37. As an 企业成员, I want a document version to remain unsearchable while it is being processed, so that incomplete chunks never influence answers.
38. As an 企业成员, I want the old document version to remain searchable while a replacement is processing, so that updates do not interrupt knowledge availability.
39. As an 企业成员, I want the new version to replace the old version only after all indexes succeed, so that vector and keyword retrieval always agree on the active knowledge.
40. As a 知识库维护者, I want document deletion to require confirmation, so that shared enterprise knowledge is not removed accidentally.
41. As a 知识库维护者, I want deletion to remove a knowledge document from future retrieval immediately, so that withdrawn material no longer supports answers.
42. As a security reviewer, I want every protected API to enforce the Keycloak identity and role on the backend, so that hidden frontend controls cannot be used to bypass authorization.
43. As a security reviewer, I want original files in private MinIO storage, so that documents are not exposed by public object URLs.
44. As a security reviewer, I want upload, activation, deletion and authorization-sensitive operations recorded in audit logs, so that material changes can be traced.
45. As an operator, I want PostgreSQL to be the source of truth for document, version, task, conversation and audit state, so that Redis or an index outage does not erase business state.
46. As an operator, I want ingestion jobs to be idempotent, so that retries or duplicate delivery do not create duplicate active versions or index points.
47. As an operator, I want stale in-progress jobs to be recoverable after a worker restart, so that a crash does not leave permanent ambiguous state.
48. As an operator, I want health information for PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Qdrant and the worker, so that deployment failures can be diagnosed quickly.
49. As a developer, I want a local demonstration realm and two configurable demo identities, so that the member and maintainer flows can be shown without Feishu or WeCom.
50. As a developer, I want the current command-line ingestion and existing question API behavior to remain available during migration, so that enterprise features can be introduced without invalidating the trusted RAG baseline all at once.
51. As a portfolio reviewer, I want documentation to distinguish implemented features from target architecture, so that the public repository makes accurate claims.

## Implementation Decisions

- The product serves one enterprise and one 企业共享知识库. It is not a multi-tenant platform. Knowledge documents are shared across authenticated members; conversations are owned by one member and are not shared.
- Keycloak owns authentication, login sessions and business-role claims. The React application uses OpenID Connect Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. The API validates access-token signature, issuer, audience and expiry using Keycloak metadata/JWKS; it never trusts a role sent in a request body.
- Business roles are `member` and `knowledge_maintainer`. A maintainer inherits member question capabilities and additionally receives document-management permissions. Keycloak system administration is not a business role.
- Local and portfolio demonstrations include a realm/client/role bootstrap and configurable demo identities. Real credentials, tokens and secrets are supplied through local environment configuration and are not committed.
- PostgreSQL is the business source of truth. The application schema includes user references, conversations, messages, rolling summaries, knowledge documents, document versions, ingestion tasks, active BM25 generations and audit events. Keycloak uses a separate database or schema within the PostgreSQL service so that identity internals are not mixed with application tables.
- Database schema changes use Alembic migrations. Application startup must not silently create or mutate production tables outside migrations.
- A 对话 belongs to exactly one authenticated user. A message belongs to exactly one conversation and stores role, content, lifecycle state, timestamps and the evidence metadata needed to render a previous answer.
- The first completed user question generates the default conversation title. Renaming changes only the title. Deletion is logical from the application perspective and must enforce ownership.
- The authenticated application creates a conversation before asking its first question. The streaming ask contract carries a `conversation_id` and question; the server loads and persists history. Browser-supplied arbitrary history is not authoritative for the authenticated flow. The existing history request field may remain temporarily for backward compatibility but is deprecated for the application UI.
- Conversation APIs provide create, list/search, retrieve messages, rename and delete operations. Lists are ordered by latest activity and are paginated.
- Model context is assembled on the server from the current question, system instructions, current-conversation rolling summary, recent messages and retrieved evidence. Full stored history is not sent on every request.
- Normal model input budget is 64K tokens, complex questions may use 128K, and the hard input ceiling is 200K. Each call reserves 8K–16K tokens for output. These are backend settings, not frontend constants.
- Context selection is deterministic before model invocation: reserve system and output space, add retrieved evidence, add the rolling summary, then add recent messages from newest to oldest until the budget is reached. Token counting uses the configured model tokenizer or a documented conservative estimator when an exact tokenizer is unavailable.
- A rolling summary is refreshed when stored messages would exceed the normal recent-history budget. The original messages remain stored; the summary is only a model-context artifact.
- `deepseek-v4-flash` is the target generation model through the existing OpenAI-compatible client boundary. The embedding model remains `BAAI/bge-large-zh-v1.5`, and the reranker remains `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` unless separately changed.
- The existing answer response remains evidence-first: natural-language answer, evidence items, optional refusal reason and latency. `confidence` is not reintroduced, and evaluation-only `choice` does not enter the product API.
- The knowledge-document list API supports search, status filter, stable pagination and latest-update ordering. The frontend maps internal task states to the approved labels 成功、进行中 and 失败.
- The existing single-file upload contract remains supported and accepts the parser formats already supported by the codebase: `.doc`, `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.xls` and `.xlsx`. Format validation uses both the extension and content inspection where available. This release also includes the batch-upload capability tracked in #14; its batch limits, same-name behavior, cancellation boundary and request-orchestration contract must be confirmed in #14 before implementation. Arbitrary file-to-Markdown conversion remains out of scope.
- The default single-file limit is 50 MiB and is configurable on the backend. The API rejects empty, unsupported or oversized files before creating an ingestion job. The frontend displays the server-provided validation message.
- Upload uses multipart form data and returns HTTP 202 with identifiers for the knowledge document, document version and ingestion task. The browser does not wait for parsing or indexing to finish.
- MinIO stores original files and immutable version-scoped processing artifacts in private buckets. PostgreSQL stores object identifiers, checksums and metadata, not the file body. Object access is mediated by the backend.
- Redis provides queue transport, distributed job coordination, short-lived locks and cache invalidation. It is not the final source of task state. The worker writes durable state transitions to PostgreSQL.
- Every ingestion job has a stable idempotency key. Redelivery or worker restart must resume or safely repeat the same version instead of creating another active version.
- Ingestion lifecycle is `queued -> parsing -> indexing -> succeeded` or `failed`. The public UI collapses all non-terminal working states into 进行中. Each transition records timestamps; terminal failures store a sanitized code/message and retain diagnostic details only in server logs.
- The worker reuses the current parser routing and chunk-processing behavior. Online ingestion operates on one immutable document version and must never run the existing whole-manifest routine that truncates global chunk output.
- Parsed chunks and metadata are written as immutable version-scoped artifacts. Qdrant points include document and version identifiers. BM25 is produced as an immutable generation rather than overwriting the only live index in place.
- Activation is coordinated by PostgreSQL. A version becomes current only after the original object, parsed chunks, Qdrant points and candidate BM25 generation have all passed validation. The same transaction records the current document version and active BM25 generation.
- Retrieval enforces the current-version set from PostgreSQL in addition to index metadata. Staged or failed versions remain invisible even if their external artifacts exist. Backend instances atomically reload the active BM25 generation after activation and keep the prior generation until the new one is ready.
- Concurrent activation is serialized with a short Redis lock plus a PostgreSQL consistency check, preventing two workers from publishing conflicting BM25 generations. Database state, not lock existence, determines the final winner.
- Failure before activation leaves the prior current version and prior BM25 generation unchanged. Cleanup of staged Qdrant points and MinIO artifacts is retryable and must not turn a successful old version unavailable.
- Initial upload creates a new knowledge document. The data model supports later versions, but an explicit replace/version-upload interaction and same-name matching policy are deferred until separately specified. The activation invariant is implemented now so future replacement does not require a schema redesign.
- Deleting a knowledge document is an authorized logical withdrawal: it is excluded from the active-version set immediately and recorded in the audit log. Permanent object purge and retention duration are separate policy work.
- Audit events include actor, action, target, request correlation identifier, timestamp and result for upload acceptance, activation, failure, deletion, conversation deletion and authorization-sensitive denials. Audit records must not contain tokens or document bodies.
- Health endpoints distinguish liveness from readiness. Readiness checks required application dependencies without returning credentials or internal exception traces.
- The deployment stack adds PostgreSQL, Keycloak, Redis, MinIO and an ingestion worker alongside the existing Qdrant, backend and frontend services. Persistent volumes are explicit. Startup ordering uses readiness, not only container creation order.
- The React frontend adopts the confirmed prototype: login entry; blue/white bank styling; collapsible sidebar with new conversation, search icon and recent history; inline rename; confirmation deletion; member/maintainer role differences; account menu; knowledge-document table; status filters; upload modal; and evidence-oriented answer layout.
- The prototype-only scene controller is never included in the production frontend. It remains a design inspection aid.
- Frontend authorization controls improve usability but are not security boundaries. Every protected route performs server-side ownership or role checks.
- API errors use stable machine-readable codes plus safe Chinese messages. Authorization failures use 401/403, missing owned resources use 404, validation uses 422 or a documented 4xx contract, accepted ingestion uses 202, and logical deletion is idempotent.
- Existing command-line build and evaluation workflows remain available while online ingestion is introduced. Public documentation must state which path is legacy/bootstrap and which path is the new managed workflow.

## Testing Decisions

- The primary acceptance seam is the FastAPI HTTP boundary using the existing `TestClient` pattern. Tests assert externally observable status codes, response/SSE contracts, persisted outcomes and later retrieval behavior rather than internal method calls.
- API integration tests use a real disposable PostgreSQL database migrated from empty with Alembic. This validates ownership, constraints, transactions, pagination, idempotency and activation semantics against the production database engine rather than SQLite substitutes.
- Keycloak authentication is exercised through an overridable identity-verification dependency that supplies signed/validated test identities and roles. Tests cover missing, expired/invalid, member and maintainer identities without requiring a live Keycloak server for every suite. A smaller deployment smoke test verifies real OIDC configuration.
- Redis, MinIO, Qdrant and model calls use deterministic test adapters at the API acceptance seam. The adapters preserve their public contracts and support injected failure points so the suite can prove that partial ingestion never becomes searchable.
- The highest-value ingestion acceptance journey is: maintainer uploads a small supported fixture; API returns 202 and 进行中; worker orchestration completes; task becomes 成功; the document becomes retrievable with its evidence. A paired failure journey injects a Qdrant or BM25 failure and proves the version remains 失败 and unsearchable.
- Replacement/activation tests create an already-active version, start a candidate version, assert the old version remains searchable during processing, then assert exactly one current version after success. Failure keeps the old version active.
- Authorization tests cover every conversation and document endpoint with both roles, including direct calls to controls hidden in the UI. Ownership tests create two members and prove list, read, rename and delete operations cannot cross users.
- Context-management tests persist a long conversation and assert the model adapter receives content within 64K/128K/200K rules, includes the rolling summary and newest relevant messages, reserves output space and never includes another conversation.
- Streaming tests reuse the existing SSE parsing/order prior art and assert progress, answer and safe-error termination. They also assert that the user and completed assistant answer are persisted exactly once under retries or client disconnects.
- Document validation tests use minimal real fixtures for Word, PDF and Excel parser routes plus invalid extension/content, empty file and over-limit cases. Tests assert behavior and resulting task state, not private parser helper calls.
- Queue/idempotency tests deliver the same job more than once and simulate a worker restart between lifecycle stages. The externally visible result must be one document version, one terminal task and no duplicate active index artifacts.
- Delete tests prove logical withdrawal immediately removes the document from new retrieval results while retaining auditable metadata. Permanent MinIO purge is not asserted because it is outside this specification.
- Frontend client/component tests cover API payload mapping, SSE handling, role-based navigation, conversation selection, inline rename, confirmation deletion, document filters and upload-state rendering. CSS implementation details are not snapshot-tested.
- Visual acceptance compares the implemented React screens with the approved static prototype at representative desktop and responsive widths. Browser screenshot automation is not the primary product test seam; visual review and accessibility checks supplement API acceptance.
- Existing parser, retriever, answer-builder, API history and frontend streaming tests are prior art and remain green. New tests extend these seams instead of creating a parallel test framework.
- A local deployment smoke test starts the full service stack, logs in with configurable demo member and maintainer identities, uploads one small document, observes successful ingestion and asks a question that cites it. This is slower release evidence, not the default unit-test loop.

## Out of Scope

- Multiple enterprises, tenant isolation, per-enterprise databases or tenant-specific knowledge bases.
- Personal knowledge bases or member-specific document visibility; all successful knowledge documents belong to the enterprise shared knowledge base.
- Real Feishu, WeCom, LDAP or corporate identity-provider integration. Keycloak demo identities are sufficient for this release.
- Anonymous public question access. A publicly hosted demonstration still requires an authorized demo login.
- Arbitrary file-to-Markdown conversion, OCR pipelines, images, audio, video, email archives or file formats not already supported by the existing parsers.
- Folder synchronization, external-drive synchronization or scheduled crawling.
- Automatic same-name replacement, explicit version-upload UI, version-history browsing, rollback and manual selection of an older version.
- Manual retry controls and automatic retry-policy UI. Failed tasks are visible; retry behavior requires a later specification.
- Permanent deletion policy, legal hold, retention duration and storage quotas.
- A user/role administration screen. Role assignment remains a Keycloak administrative operation.
- Knowledge-document category, issuer and version columns in the main list; the confirmed prototype intentionally omits them.
- Sharing conversation history between members or allowing maintainers to inspect other members' conversations.
- Replacing Qdrant, changing embedding/reranker models or redesigning the trusted retrieval and evidence-generation algorithms beyond what managed version activation requires.
- Replacing the published evaluation methodology or adding private evaluation workbooks/reports to the public repository.
- Production cloud topology, multi-region disaster recovery, autoscaling targets, enterprise SLA commitments and external penetration certification.
- Pixel-perfect automated screenshot testing as the main acceptance strategy.

## Further Notes

- The confirmed static prototype is the interaction and visual reference, while the current React application and API are the implementation baseline. Development must not copy the prototype scene selector into production.
- The approved domain vocabulary is authoritative: 企业成员、知识库维护者、企业共享知识库、知识文档、文档版本、入库任务、对话、消息、对话历史、模型上下文 and 上下文预算.
- PostgreSQL, Keycloak, Redis, MinIO, Qdrant and BM25 have non-overlapping responsibilities. Redis is coordination, MinIO is object storage, PostgreSQL is business truth, and indexes are derived artifacts.
- The public repository must continue excluding credentials, model caches, raw enterprise material and generated private index artifacts. Example configuration contains placeholders only.
- This specification is intentionally broad and should be decomposed into dependency-ordered implementation tickets before coding. Likely ticket boundaries are platform foundations, authentication, persistence/migrations, conversation APIs/context management, ingestion orchestration, retrieval activation, frontend implementation, and deployment/documentation.

items.title: Decision: is Airbyte still on the roadmap? (ELT/ETL leaves scope under the multi-tenant direction)
items.body:
## Context

The local Airbyte setup uses `abctl`, which provisions Airbyte into a throwaway kind (k8s-in-docker) cluster on its own Docker network. This is a dev/POC convenience, not a production deployment. Several pain points encountered locally are artifacts of `abctl`, not the design:

- The Airbyte kind node must be manually bridged to the `open_epm` Docker network (`docker network connect open_epm airbyte-abctl-control-plane`), and **this bridge drops on every host reboot / Airbyte reinstall** — konsol then can't reach the Airbyte API (all calls fail until re-attached). Documented in `scripts/setup-airbyte.sh` but fragile.
- Airbyte API credentials are random per-install (`abctl local credentials`) and currently hand-pasted into konsol EPM Settings.
- `workspace_id` and `d365_source_definition_id` are found manually via the UI/API.

## What production should look like

Two viable shapes:

**A. Airbyte Cloud (managed SaaS)** — stable API (`api.airbyte.com`), OAuth application client-id/secret created once, stable workspace/source-definition IDs. The ClickHouse **destination** must be reachable from Airbyte Cloud (TLS public endpoint + IP allowlist, or tunnel/PrivateLink). D365 source side is already public HTTPS (Azure OData).

**B. Self-hosted Airbyte on Kubernetes (Helm)** — Airbyte + ClickHouse in the same cluster/VPC, **stable service DNS** (no docker bridge, no reboot-drop). Custom D365 connector image published to a registry (GHCR/ECR), versioned.

## What changes local → prod

| Concern | Local (abctl) | Production |
|---|---|---|
| Networking | manual `docker network connect`, drops on reboot | VPC/cluster service DNS (self-host) or secured endpoint/tunnel (Cloud) |
| Airbyte creds | random per-install, hand-pasted | secret manager (Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / K8s secrets), injected |
| workspace/source-def IDs | hunt in UI/API | set once via IaC (Terraform / Helm values / bootstrap) |
| EPM Settings Airbyte block | clicked in UI | provisioned by config/IaC at deploy time |
| D365 connector | local docker image | published, versioned registry image |
| Stability | reboot breaks it | restart policies, persistence, monitoring, HA |

## What stays the same

The konsol layer is prod-ready as-is: `provision_connector_airbyte` is idempotent (find-or-create), D365 creds stored encrypted in connector password fields, and the config → source → schema-apply → build flow is identical. Productionizing means swapping the Airbyte substrate, not rebuilding konsol.

## Multi-tenant (hosted-clients) notes

- One Airbyte workspace per client (or dedicated instance for isolation); connector → `workspace_id` scopes it.
- Per-tenant D365 creds stay encrypted in each tenant's konsol (never exposed to an LLM/MCP — only a `configured: true` boolean is ever returned).
- Per-tenant ClickHouse target (separate database/schema, e.g. `epm_raw_<tenant>`).
- Onboarding = IaC creating a workspace + connection + calling idempotent `provision_connector_airbyte`, not a human clicking buttons.

## Key decision

The single biggest real design decision is **how Airbyte reaches ClickHouse securely**: in-VPC service DNS (self-host) vs secured endpoint/tunnel (Cloud). Everything konsol-side carries over unchanged.

## Acceptance / next steps

- [ ] Decide Cloud vs self-hosted Helm
- [ ] Define ClickHouse-destination networking for the chosen path
- [ ] Move Airbyte + per-tenant secrets into a secret manager
- [ ] Provision EPM Settings Airbyte block + workspace/source-definition via IaC
- [ ] Publish the `source-d365-fno` custom connector image to a registry

---
_Filed from a working session analyzing the D365 → consolidation wiring on the local stack._

items.title: research: Lakehouse architecture, ownership, and ingestion contract
items.body:
**Parent: #15 — Production lakehouse adapter (BigQuery / ClickHouse Cloud)**

This is one of three deep-research sub-issues spawned from #15. It addresses the *shape of the system* — independent of which backing store we pick. Sister issues cover the BigQuery and ClickHouse Cloud deep dives, and they should make progress in parallel.

## Goal

Produce a research packet that lets us decide where the production `TraceLakehouse` lives, how trace data gets into it, and what the developer-facing eval CLI experience looks like in a control-plane-led world. The packet should give an implementer a clear path forward even before the two backing-store sub-issues land.

## Context

### Existing surface (recap from parent)

- `types/lakehouse.go::TraceLakehouse` — five-method interface (`StoreTrace`, `StoreRecording`, `QueryTraces`, `QueryRecordings`, `Metrics`, `Close`). Used today by `eval/cmd/eval/main.go` for `baseline`, `mine-failures`, `drift`, `compare-to-production`.
- `eval/lakehouse/filestore.go` — file-based dev/CI implementation. Note the `parentOnlyToolCalls` filter (`filestore.go:239`) exists to avoid double-counting forwarded sub-agent tool calls (#55).
- `types/runtrace.go::RunTrace` / `RunRecording` — the persisted shapes. `RunTrace.ToolCalls` carries forwarded sub-agent calls; any aggregation must filter on `RunID`/`ParentRunID`.
- `types/metrics.go::TraceFilter`, `TraceMetrics`, `BaselineMetrics`, `DriftReport` — the read-side contract.
- `harness/internal/trace/otel.go` — the OTel emitter, which already streams spans/metrics over OTLP and is **disjoint** from the lakehouse. The relationship between these two telemetry paths is itself something the research must clarify.
- `harness/internal/transport/grpc.go` and `proto/harness/v1/harness.proto` — the existing harness↔control-plane wire.
- `VERSION1.md` "Lakehouse" + "Eval framework" + "Transport" sections.

### What changed since #15 was filed

1. We are now committing to a **reference control plane** implementation. The harness has always been "a job, not a server" (`VERSION1.md`); the control plane is the long-running counterpart that schedules runs, persists state, and serves operator UIs.
2. We are committing to **managed analytical stores only** (BigQuery, ClickHouse Cloud). Self-managed Postgres is dropped.
3. The OTel emitter has matured (#94 / #98 / #99 / #100) and now ships spans and metrics over OTLP — meaning there is *already* a streaming telemetry path out of the harness that does not flow through `TraceLakehouse`.

### The core question

`TraceLakehouse` was originally designed assuming the harness would write directly to a backing store. With a control plane in the picture, three architectures are possible:

1. **Harness writes directly.** `BigQueryLakehouse` / `ClickHouseLakehouse` adapters live in the harness module, configured per-run. Auth flows through `RunConfig.Provider.Credential`-style federation.
2. **Control plane writes; harness only emits over gRPC.** The harness keeps `Transport` as its only egress for trace data. The control plane consumes the existing event stream and writes to the lakehouse on the harness's behalf. `eval/lakehouse/` ships only the file-backed adapter; production lives in the control plane repo.
3. **OTel-derived lakehouse.** Lean entirely on OTLP — the harness emits OTel spans / metrics; the lakehouse is a SQL view over a span store (BigQuery via OpenTelemetry GCP exporter, or ClickHouse via the official ClickHouse OTel exporter / Tempo). `RunTrace`/`RunRecording` become projection types built on top of spans, not first-class storage shapes.

Each has knock-on effects on the eval CLI, the security model, schema-evolution churn, and how much the harness module is allowed to know.

### Constraints carried in from related work

- **#8 Observability security** — `RunRecording` encryption at rest, `ProductionTrace.classification`, RBAC on lakehouse queries. These are required before multi-tenant deployment.
- **#9 Eval framework security** — eval mining quarantine. Inputs to the lakehouse and consumers of mined tasks both touch user content.
- **#100 Native OTLP/HTTP** — the OTel side is moving to OTLP/HTTP. Whatever we do, we shouldn't reinvent a parallel trace-shipping wire format.
- **#13 Mine first eval suite from real PRs** depends on `QueryRecordings` being usable in production.
- **#30 Eval gate quality** and **#31 Eval runner concurrency** depend on the lakehouse being queryable in CI.
- `RunRecording` payloads can be megabytes (full conversation history including tool I/O) while `RunTrace` is kilobytes. Storing them in the same way is probably wrong.

## Research questions

1. **Ownership.** Which architecture (1/2/3 or hybrid) best fits our constraints — minimal harness deps, control plane as the long-running operator, security model in #8?
2. **OTel duplication.** If the OTel path already carries everything in `RunTrace`, is `TraceLakehouse` redundant — or are the access patterns (offline batch eval, drift, mining failures) sufficiently different from APM queries that we genuinely need a second store? What do other agent platforms do (Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, Helicone, Arize Phoenix, Honeycomb GenAI)?
3. **Recording vs trace separation.** Three live patterns: (a) both in column store (e.g. JSON typed column), (b) structured trace in column store + recording blob in object store with a URL pointer, (c) both columns with one being aggressively partitioned and TTL'd. What's the right default, and what's the migration story between them?
4. **Ingestion contract.** If the control plane is the writer, what does the *interface* between harness and CP look like for trace-completion events vs. recordings? Today `RunTrace` is sent as a single `event_type=trace_completed` over the existing gRPC `Transport`; recordings are file-only. Do we add a new gRPC method, reuse the existing event stream, push to an OTel collector that the CP owns, or write to an intermediary queue? What about backpressure if the lakehouse is slow — does the harness block, drop, or spool to disk?
5. **Eval CLI experience.** Today: `stirrup-eval baseline --lakehouse <local-dir>`. With a CP-owned remote lakehouse, what does the surface become — direct SQL passthrough, a CP "Insights" REST/gRPC API, a read-only CLI auth flow (service account, IAP)? How do disconnected developers / open-source users keep working — do we keep `FileStore` as the OSS escape hatch, or expect everyone to point at a CP?
6. **Schema evolution.** We've already added `RunID`/`ParentRunID` to `ToolCallSummary` (#55). Future additions are likely (multimodal #103, sub-agent budgets, more eval signals). Recommend an evolution policy — JSON-typed columns + projection views, versioned tables, schema registry, or "RunTrace is contractual; we cut new tables for major versions."
7. **PII / secret scrubbing.** `LogScrubber` and `RunConfig.Redact()` cover trace persistence today. With a CP-owned writer, where does scrubbing happen — harness side (defence in depth) or CP-side just before write? How is it enforced as part of the schema (column-level access policies, row policies)?
8. **Multi-tenancy.** What's the per-tenant isolation model? Row-level filters, separate datasets/databases per tenant, or per-tenant projects/services? What does this imply for the schema (`tenant_id` column everywhere) and the read API?
9. **Open-table formats.** Iceberg / Delta give us "the lakehouse" in the literal sense — should we target one explicitly so we can swap engines? BigQuery now reads Iceberg via BigLake; ClickHouse has Iceberg readers. Worth pinning down.
10. **Backwards compatibility & migration.** We have `FileStore` JSON in CI today and possibly local dev recordings. What's the upgrade path — bulk import, parallel-write-then-cutover, or "the file store is dev-only and we accept losing prod data"?

## Deliverables

A research packet that includes:

- **Comparative summary** of the three architectures, with concrete trade-offs scored against: harness dep surface, CP coupling, OTel duplication, eval CLI ergonomics, security/multi-tenancy, schema-evolution cost.
- **A recommended architecture** with reasoning anchored in our constraints.
- **An ingestion-contract sketch** for the recommended path: gRPC method signatures (or OTel attribute conventions), backpressure behaviour, idempotency keys, scrubbing seam.
- **An eval-CLI evolution plan** showing what each subcommand (`baseline`, `mine-failures`, `drift`, `compare-to-production`) becomes; what `FileStore` keeps doing.
- **A schema-evolution policy.**
- **A survey** of how 4–6 named agent observability/analytics products handle the same problem, with concrete observations cited (docs URLs, blog posts, conference talks).
- **A list of open questions** the research couldn't close that should become focused follow-ups.

## Inputs the researcher should pull from

- **In-tree code:** `types/lakehouse.go`, `types/runtrace.go`, `types/metrics.go`, `types/eval.go`, `eval/lakehouse/filestore.go`, `eval/cmd/eval/main.go`, `harness/internal/trace/otel.go`, `harness/internal/transport/grpc.go`, `proto/harness/v1/harness.proto`, `VERSION1.md` ("Lakehouse" + "Eval framework" + "Transport" sections).
- **Related issues:** #8 (observability security), #9 (eval framework security), #13 (mine first eval suite), #30 (eval gate quality), #31 (eval runner concurrency), #55 (sub-agent forwarded calls), #94/#98/#99/#100/#101 (observability productisation), #103 (multimodal — drives recording size).
- **External:** OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions; OTel span store backends (Tempo, BigQuery via the GCP exporter, ClickHouse via the official OTel exporter); Langfuse / LangSmith / Braintrust / Helicone / Arize Phoenix / Honeycomb GenAI architecture write-ups; Iceberg / BigLake / Delta on managed clouds.

## Out of scope

- Concrete BigQuery DDL, partitioning recipes, slot pricing — those go in the BigQuery sub-issue.
- Concrete ClickHouse MergeTree definitions, async insert tuning, materialized views — those go in the ClickHouse Cloud sub-issue.
- Eval suite content (#30) and gate concurrency (#31).
- The OTel side of observability beyond "how does it overlap with the lakehouse" (#94 et al cover that).

items.title: KB Ingestion Phase 4A: Multi-tenant ingestion observability daemon scaffold + telemetry schema
items.body:
## Context

Phase 4A sub-ticket of [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) (Operations + Observability for Cloud-Native KB Deployments). Surfaced 2026-05-20 during nightshift-mode lane-pickup after parallel-track work on #11631 (Phase 0/1C-α write-side stamping by @neo-gpt) + #11660 (Phase 0/1B-β path externalization by @neo-opus-ada) + #11663 (Phase 4 retention policy by @neo-opus-ada).

**Pre-Phase-2-actionable per #11628 body escape clause:**
> *"Operator alerting + dashboard surfacing may begin in parallel once Phase 0/1 #11625 contracts land (daemon-scaffolding can start pre-Phase-2)."*

Phase 0/1A schemas + 0/1B registry are already on `dev`; Phase 0/1B-β paths (PR #11661) + 0/1C-α write-side stamping (PR #11662) are in @tobiu's merge gate. The daemon SHELL + TELEMETRY SCHEMA can land before Phase 2 #11626 ships its ingestion-service hooks — actual live-integration with Phase 2 ingestion calls is deferred to a follow-up sub-ticket.

## The Problem

After Phase 0/1 + Phase 0/1C-α land, cloud Agent OS deployments have:
- Stable `parsed-chunk-v1` + `backup-record-v1` schemas
- Source/Parser registry + per-source path config
- Write-side tenant stamping with `tenantId` / `repoSlug` / `visibility` / `originAgentIdentity`
- Configurable bundle retention

What's still missing for operational visibility:
- **No per-tenant ingestion metrics** — push frequency, error rates, ingestion latency, embedding-budget burn
- **No telemetry schema** for what metrics get persisted
- **No daemon orchestration** that wakes periodically to roll up + persist tenant-scoped metrics

The Phase 4 #11628 ticket's value-prop framing (operational-cost-of-recovery reduction, NOT data-loss prevention) anchors what 4A should collect.

## The Architectural Reality

Per [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) Architectural Substrate Precedent — Phase 4A EXTENDS `KBRecorderService.mjs` rather than introducing a new substrate. KBRecorderService already persists every KB MCP tool invocation into the shared Memory Core SQLite database. Phase 4A adds:

1. **Per-tenant scoping**: extend the existing `kb_query_log` schema with tenant-aware columns (`tenantId`, `repoSlug`, `visibility`) OR add a sibling table `kb_ingestion_metrics` for ingestion-specific counts.
2. **Daemon orchestration**: new daemon at `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` following the `orchestrator-daemon.mjs` / `swarm-heartbeat-daemon.mjs` pattern. Wakes on schedule; rolls up metrics; persists to MC SQLite.
3. **Telemetry-schema doc**: design doc at `learn/agentos/decisions/0NNN-kb-ingestion-telemetry-schema.md` (ADR) defining the persistence contract so Phase 4B reconciliation + Phase 4D alerting consume a stable schema.

## The Fix

### 1. Telemetry-schema ADR

Create `learn/agentos/decisions/0NNN-kb-ingestion-telemetry-schema.md`:

- What metrics are collected (per-tenant)
- Schema shape (column names, types, indexing)
- Retention policy (per-tenant — different from Phase 4 bundle retention)
- Consumer expectations (Phase 4B reconciliation, Phase 4D alerting, operator dashboards)

### 2. SQLite schema extension

Either:
- (a) Extend `kb_query_log` with `tenantId`, `repoSlug`, `visibility` columns (add migration)
- (b) Add sibling `kb_ingestion_metrics` table for ingestion-specific counts

Choice deferred to implementation — extension is simpler if metrics are query-call-shaped; sibling table is cleaner if metrics are roll-up-shaped.

### 3. Daemon shell

`ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs`:

```js
import {KBRecorderService} from '../services/knowledge-base/KBRecorderService.mjs';
import mcConfig from '../mcp/server/memory-core/config.mjs';

// Wake on schedule (default: every 15 minutes).
// Roll up tenant-scoped metrics from kb_query_log (or sibling).
// Persist to a roll-up table for Phase 4D alerting consumption.

export async function runObservabilityDaemon({intervalMs = 15 * 60 * 1000, oneShot = false} = {}) {
    // ... implementation
}

if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
    runObservabilityDaemon({oneShot: process.argv.includes('--once')}).catch(err => {
        console.error('[kb-observability-daemon] failed:', err);
        process.exit(1);
    });
}
```

### 4. Operator-facing CLI

`npm run ai:kb-observability` entry in `package.json` (one-shot mode for operator-driven manual rollup).

### 5. Tests

- Unit: `kb-observability-daemon.spec.mjs` — verifies rollup logic against synthetic `kb_query_log` rows with mixed tenants.
- Integration: synthetic multi-tenant fixture (reuse Phase 5 test fixtures once they land) — deferred to follow-up if Phase 5 fixtures aren't ready.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Telemetry-schema ADR drafted under `learn/agentos/decisions/` (number assigned at file time)
- [ ] SQLite schema extension OR sibling table added (impl decides between extending `kb_query_log` vs creating `kb_ingestion_metrics`)
- [ ] `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` shell exists, follows existing daemon pattern, wakes on schedule
- [ ] Operator CLI `npm run ai:kb-observability -- --once` exists for manual rollup
- [ ] Unit test covers rollup against synthetic per-tenant rows
- [ ] Phase 2 live-integration hooks explicitly deferred to a follow-up sub-ticket (Phase 4A-β or similar)
- [ ] No regression to existing KBRecorderService behavior (manual smoke OR test assertion)

## Out of Scope

- **Phase 2 live-integration hooks** — Phase 2 #11626 doesn't exist yet; integration follows in Phase 4A-β post-Phase-2.
- **Phase 4D alerting surface** — separate sub-ticket. This phase collects + persists telemetry; alerting consumes it.
- **Phase 4B reconciliation daemon** — separate sub-ticket. Different concern (state-drift detection vs metrics rollup).
- **Phase 4C stale-chunk GC daemon** — separate sub-ticket. Different concern.
- **Per-tenant SLA / quota enforcement** — V1 surfaces the data; SLA enforcement is post-V1 commercialization scope per #11628 OOS.
- **Cross-deployment fleet management** — single-deployment scope for V1.

## Avoided Traps

| Trap | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Building before Phase 2 ingestion-service exists | This sub-ticket scopes to scaffolding + schema only; live-integration deferred. The shell + schema ARE pre-Phase-2-actionable per #11628 escape clause. |
| New telemetry database | KBRecorderService already uses Memory Core SQLite; reuse the substrate. |
| Dashboard infrastructure | Out of scope for daemon work; sandman_handoff or portal app extension is Phase 4D territory. |
| Bundling rollup + alerting into one daemon | Separate concerns; testability + future modification budget benefit from separate daemons (per #11628 Avoided Traps). |
| Roll-up cadence baked into the daemon | Cadence becomes `aiConfig.kbObservability.intervalMs` config so operators can tune for high-volume vs low-volume deployments. |

## Related

- **Parent Phase Epic:** [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) (Phase 4: Operations + Observability)
- **Parent meta-Epic:** [#11624](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11624)
- **Substrate-extension target:** `ai/services/knowledge-base/KBRecorderService.mjs` (existing telemetry persistence)
- **Daemon precedents:** `ai/scripts/orchestrator-daemon.mjs`, `swarm-heartbeat-daemon.mjs`, `bridge-daemon.mjs`
- **Sibling parallel lanes** in flight:
  - PR [#11661](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11661) Phase 0/1B-β path-externalization (@neo-opus-ada)
  - PR [#11662](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11662) Phase 0/1C-α write-side stamping (@neo-gpt) — APPROVED, awaiting merge
  - PR [#11664](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11664) Phase 4 retention policy (@neo-opus-ada) — APPROVED, awaiting merge
  - [#11646](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11646) Phase 5C KB unit coverage expansion (@neo-gpt) in progress

## Origin Session ID

`7360e917-1733-4cdd-a6f3-5ac51c34b838`

## Handoff Retrieval Hints

- `query_raw_memories({query: 'Phase 4A KB observability daemon telemetry schema KBRecorderService extension'})`
- `ask_knowledge_base({query: 'KBRecorderService kb_query_log kb_query_faqs Memory Core SQLite telemetry', type: 'src'})`
- Daemon pattern reference: `ai/scripts/orchestrator-daemon.mjs` — proven daemon orchestration shape
- Operator framing 2026-05-19 (#11628 retention sub-ticket context): operational-cost-of-recovery reduction is the value-prop, NOT data-loss prevention

items.title: As a Service, DB schema?
items.body:
<!-- agentloop:waitstate -->
**Current state:** 💤 waiting for human
<!-- /agentloop:waitstate -->

<!-- agentloop:ui-link -->
[Open in AgentLoop UI](https://agentloop.thomas-guettler.de/#/issues/otelhouse/47)
<!-- /agentloop:ui-link -->

<!-- agentloop:plan -->
## Questions

1. How many tenants do you expect (tens, hundreds, thousands)? Above ~1k databases ClickHouse metadata starts to hurt and Option B (shared tables + row policies) becomes more attractive than Option A (database-per-tenant).
2. Do customers bring their own Grafana, or do you host Grafana for them? Hosted Grafana lets us add a second auth layer; BYO Grafana means the ClickHouse credential **is** the only boundary.
3. Per-tenant retention/quotas — uniform across all tenants, or sold as tiers? Determines whether TTL is baked into DDL or made overridable per tenant.
4. Is the Collector hosted by you or by the customer? If customer-hosted, the ingest-token rotation story needs to be designed in v1, not deferred.
5. Tenant-id format and naming rules — confirm short slug (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,30}`) with a reserved-name list (`default`, `system`, `test`, `tenant_admin`)?
6. Is the existing single-tenant `test:test` setup kept as a dev/CI mode, or replaced entirely by a "tenant `test`" in the new model? Affects whether the Dagger pipeline grows a tenancy layer or stays as-is.
7. Scope of this issue: do you want the full v1 (provisioning tool + Collector routing + Dagger isolation test + docs), or just a written design doc this round? The previous code attempt failed and was escalated — knowing whether to ship code or just docs would unblock the next run.

## Goal

Run otelhouse as a multi-tenant service where each customer connects their own Grafana directly to ClickHouse and can only see their own traces, logs, and metrics — with zero risk of cross-tenant reads.

## Constraints driving the design

- Customers connect Grafana **directly** to ClickHouse → the isolation boundary must live inside ClickHouse, not in an app-layer proxy.
- otelhouse today is a Dagger test harness with one shared ClickHouse user (`test:test`) writing to a single `test` database with the upstream `clickhouseexporter` schemas (`otel_traces`, `otel_logs`, `otel_metrics_*`). No tenancy primitives exist yet (see README.md and ci/main.go:42-49).
- Schemas are produced by the upstream Collector exporter, not by us — any tenant marker has to be modelled as an OTel resource attribute or a database boundary, not a custom DDL change to the `otel_*` tables.

## Options considered

**A. Database-per-tenant (recommended)**
One ClickHouse database per customer (`tenant_<id>`), each with its own `otel_traces` / `otel_logs` / `otel_metrics_*` set. One ClickHouse user per customer with `GRANT SELECT ON tenant_<id>.*` only. Grafana datasource per customer points at that user.

- Pros: hardest isolation boundary ClickHouse offers; no row-policy escape hatches; per-tenant retention/TTL/quota knobs; easy to drop a tenant (`DROP DATABASE`).
- Cons: N×7 tables; Collector needs one exporter (or routing pipeline) per tenant; provisioning automation required.

**B. Shared tables + row policies**
Single set of tables, add a `tenant_id` materialized column derived from `ResourceAttributes['tenant.id']`. One ClickHouse user per customer with a row policy on every table.

- Pros: single schema, simpler ingest, lower object count.
- Cons: relies on row policies being correct on every query path Grafana issues; any new table added by a Collector upgrade must get a matching policy or it leaks; harder to defend in a security review.

**C. Cluster-per-tenant** — out of scope for v1; revisit only if a customer demands physical isolation.

**Recommendation: Option A.** "Customer A cannot read customer B" is easier to defend behind a `GRANT` boundary than behind row policies layered over shared tables.

## Implementation plan (Option A)

1. **Tenant provisioning tool (`cmd/tenantctl` or Dagger function)**
   Given a tenant id, the tool runs against ClickHouse as the admin user and:
   - `CREATE DATABASE tenant_<id>`
   - `CREATE USER tenant_<id>_ro IDENTIFIED BY '<generated>'` + `GRANT SELECT ON tenant_<id>.* TO tenant_<id>_ro` (Grafana side — read-only)
   - `CREATE USER tenant_<id>_ingest IDENTIFIED BY '<generated>'` + `GRANT INSERT, CREATE TABLE ON tenant_<id>.* TO tenant_<id>_ingest` (Collector side — lets `create_schema: true` auto-build the `otel_*` tables on first write)
   - Apply the hardened settings profile (step 4) to both users.
   - Emit both credentials + the ingest endpoint to stdout (operator pipes into their secret store).
   - A matching `tenantctl delete <id>` performs `DROP USER` × 2 then `DROP DATABASE tenant_<id> SYNC`.

2. **Ingestion routing**
   Each tenant gets its own OTLP endpoint at the Collector, authenticated with a per-tenant token.
   - **Default (≤ ~50 tenants):** one receiver + one `clickhouse/<tenant>` exporter per tenant in the Collector config, with `database: tenant_<id>` and the ingest user's creds. Generated by `tenantctl` as a config fragment included from the main Collector config.
   - **Scale path:** single OTLP receiver + a `routing` processor keyed on the bearer token or `tenant.id` resource attribute, fanning out to N exporters. Switch when the per-tenant-pipeline config gets unwieldy.
   - Hard rule: writes without a valid tenant credential are rejected. No "default" database fallback.

3. **Grafana wiring**
   - Document the exact datasource JSON for `grafana-clickhouse-datasource`: host, port (9440 / TLS), `username: tenant_<id>_ro`, `defaultDatabase: tenant_<id>`, `secureJsonData.password`.
   - Mark the datasource read-only in Grafana so the UI doesn't offer write actions.
   - Cross-database queries (`FROM tenant_other.otel_traces`) must fail with "Not enough privileges" thanks to the `GRANT`, not return empty rows — verified in tests (step 5).

4. **Defense-in-depth ClickHouse settings**
   Define a `tenant` settings profile applied to all `tenant_*_ro` users:
   - `readonly = 2` (allows `SET` so Grafana works, forbids writes/DDL).
   - `access_management = 0`.
   - `max_concurrent_queries_for_user`, `max_memory_usage_for_user`, `max_execution_time` set to sane defaults.
   - Deny external-data functions (`remote`, `remoteSecure`, `url`, `file`, `s3`, `s3Cluster`, `mysql`, `postgresql`, `mongodb`, `cluster`, `clusterAllReplicas`) via the profile's function restrictions so a compromised tenant credential can't exfiltrate by opening a second connection.
   - Query log stays in `system.query_log`, queryable only by the admin user.

5. **Dagger integration test for isolation**
   New test in the pipeline that:
   - Calls `tenantctl create a` and `tenantctl create b`.
   - Ingests one identifiable span/log into each tenant via the Collector.
   - Asserts:
     - `tenant_a_ro` selecting from `tenant_a.otel_traces` returns its row.
     - `tenant_a_ro` selecting from `tenant_b.otel_traces` → error (not empty result).
     - `tenant_a_ro` calling `remote(...)`, `url(...)`, `file(...)`, `s3(...)` → error.
     - `tenant_a_ro` attempting `INSERT` / `CREATE TABLE` → error.
     - `tenant_a_ingest` attempting `SELECT` → error.
   - This becomes the regression net for every Collector / ClickHouse upgrade.

6. **Docs**
   - New `docs/multi-tenancy.md`: threat model ("Grafana is untrusted from our side; the tenant credential is the only boundary"), provisioning flow, datasource template, explicit non-goals (no PII redaction, no cost attribution, no per-tenant encryption keys in v1).
   - Update `README.md` to link to it and to flag that the existing `test:test` single-tenant setup is dev/CI-only.

## Out of scope for this issue

- Billing / cost attribution per tenant.
- A self-service signup UI (operator runs `tenantctl` for now).
- Cross-tenant aggregate dashboards for the operator (separate issue).
- Migrating an existing single-tenant deployment's data into the new layout.

items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### LLM Evaluation

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| LLM Judge | 用另一個模型依評分規則批改 AI 回答。 | 用另一個模型依評分規準評估回答品質。 | Rubric、pairwise judge、calibration、human agreement。 | 固定prompt與模型版本，抽樣人工複核並監控偏差。 | 大量離線回歸、主觀品質評估。 | judge有偏見與位置效應；不要只依賴單一judge。 |
| Golden Dataset | AI 版本的固定測試案例與標準答案。 | 代表真實使用情境、具標準答案或評分規準的固定案例集。 | Versioned dataset、stratified sampling、edge cases。 | 標記來源、難度、語言與失敗類型，納入CI與變更審查。 | 模型/提示詞版本比較。 | 資料過時會誤導；要避免資料洩漏與只收集簡單案例。 |
| Observability | 把 metrics、logs、traces 串起來，看懂線上系統發生什麼。 | 讓團隊知道系統發生什麼、品質如何、成本多少。 | Metrics、logs、traces、dashboards、alerts。 | 關聯request id、tenant、model、prompt版本與結果指標。 | 線上除錯、SLA與容量規劃。 | 避免記錄原始敏感prompt；指標需能對應行動。 |
| Tracing | 像 distributed tracing，追蹤一次 AI 請求經過的所有步驟。 | 追蹤一次請求跨模型、檢索、工具與服務的完整路徑。 | OpenTelemetry、span、trace ID、Langfuse/Phoenix。 | 每個節點建立span，記錄輸入輸出摘要、耗時、token與錯誤。 | 定位慢點、錯誤與幻覺來源。 | trace資料可能含機密；設採樣、遮罩、保留期限。 |
| Token Cost | 把每次模型呼叫換算成可追蹤、可分攤的成本。 | 量化輸入輸出token帶來的模型使用成本。 | Token counter、pricing table、budget、cost attribution。 | 每次請求記錄token與模型，按租戶/功能聚合並設預算告警。 | 成本最佳化、租戶計費、模型選擇。 | 價格會變；不要只看平均值，要看p95與異常尖峰。 |
| Latency | 拆解使用者等候時間，找出慢在 queue、搜尋、模型或工具。 | 從請求到回應的時間，需拆分各階段觀察。 | p50/p95/p99、TTFT、streaming、timeout。 | 分別量測queue、retrieval、LLM、tool與post-process。 | 互動式聊天、SLA設計。 | 平均值會掩蓋尾延遲；重試與串行工具會放大等待。 |
| Fallback | 主要模型失敗時，自動切到備援模型或簡化流程。 | 主要模型或服務失效時切換到可接受的替代路徑。 | Circuit breaker、model routing、retry、degraded mode。 | 定義觸發條件、替代模型、超時與回復策略並記錄原因。 | 供應商故障、流量尖峰、模型超時。 | fallback品質與成本要測試；避免故障時形成重試風暴。 |
| Prompt Versioning | 把 prompt 當程式碼版本管理、測試與回滾。 | 讓prompt變更可追蹤、可回滾、可比較。 | Git、template registry、semantic version、feature flag。 | 保存版本、變更原因、評測結果與生產流量分配。 | 持續改善提示詞、A/B測試。 | prompt改一字也可能改變行為；不可只靠人工感覺上線。 |

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |
| Row-Level Security | 讓資料庫本身強制每列資料能被哪個租戶看到。 | 由資料庫在每一列層級強制租戶存取政策。 | PostgreSQL RLS、session context、policy。 | 交易開始設定tenant context，並測試直接SQL與服務帳號路徑。 | 共享schema的強制隔離。 | 繞過RLS的管理連線很危險；政策需納入migration與測試。 |
| Tenant-aware API | API 從驗證到查詢都必須知道目前是哪個租戶。 | API在授權、資料查詢與回應中都理解租戶邊界。 | JWT、middleware、OPA、quota。 | middleware解析tenant，服務層拒絕不一致context並套用配額。 | 多租戶REST/GraphQL服務。 | 不要只在controller過濾；內部服務與webhook也要驗證。 |
| Multi-tenant Scaling | 避免單一大租戶吃光資源，並能依租戶分片、限流與擴容。 | 在租戶數、流量與資料量成長時維持隔離與效能。 | Quota、sharding、partition、autoscaling、noisy-neighbor control。 | 依租戶分片/限流，監控單租戶資源與升級路徑。 | SaaS成長與大型租戶加入。 | 平均容量會掩蓋熱租戶；需壓測最壞分布。 |
