items.title: lakehouse: multi-tenant isolation gate — row-level vs per-tenant dataset

milestone.title: production lakehouse
milestone.description: eval/traces need a lakehouse to function correctly, we should have a production implementation sufficient to support stirrup's development, plus something to serve as a reference implementation for deployment.

items.body:
Spawned from #105 deep-dive ([comment](https://github.com/rxbynerd/stirrup/issues/105#issuecomment-4413646429), "Open questions" item 8, §9 multi-tenancy).

## Question

#8.6.3 requires "role-based access to lakehouse queries" before regulated/compliance environments. The #105 packet sketches three multi-tenant strategies for BigQuery:

1. **`tenant_id` column + row-level access policies** on a shared dataset.
2. **Per-tenant dataset** (`recordings_<tenant>`).
3. **Per-tenant project**.

The packet recommends starting with strategy 1 and migrating to strategy 2 at one of three triggers:

- A tenant requires their own CMEK key in their own KMS project (#8 driven).
- Cross-tenant query latency / RLS overhead becomes observable.
- Tenant count crosses ~50 and grant management becomes an ops job.

## Decision needed

Does row-level access on a shared dataset satisfy #8.6.3 RBAC for stirrup's intended multi-tenant deployment, or do we need per-tenant datasets at GA?

This affects:

- The **writer abstraction**: does the destination parameterise by `tenant_id` only (strategy 1), or does it need per-tenant table routing (strategy 2)?
- The **schema**: `tenant_id` as a typed column is non-negotiable either way (RLS does not work on JSON columns), so the schema itself is unblocked.
- The **#106 ClickHouse comparison**: ClickHouse Cloud has a per-service price floor that makes per-tenant-service costly at scale; per-database-on-shared-service is the equivalent of strategy 2.

## Inputs needed

- Stakeholder list: who is the first multi-tenant tenant? What's their isolation posture (BAA / DPA / SOC2 / HIPAA)?
- Threat model: are cross-tenant queries acceptable for ops with the right IAM, or does every read need to be tenant-scoped at the SQL layer?
- Operational ceiling: how many tenants do we expect in year 1?

## References

- #8.6.3 metrics RBAC
- #105 §7 (security posture), §9 (multi-tenancy growth path)
- #15 parent
- Sister: equivalent decision for ClickHouse Cloud belongs in #106's packet

items.title: Integrations: Gmail and Google Contacts sync - two-way email and contact data flow
items.body:
## 1. Executive Summary

Let a rep connect their personal Gmail inbox and Google Contacts (via the OAuth/credential infrastructure built by the sibling issue **"Integrations: Third-party connection hub - admin-managed credentials for Google Workspace and Calendly"**) so that (a) Gmail messages to/from a lead's known contacts are pulled into this app's existing unified activity timeline, and (b) a rep can pull a person from their Google Contacts onto a specific lead as a new contact. This issue is scoped to the **data-sync logic only** — periodic Gmail polling, matching, dedup, and a one-way Contacts import — built entirely on top of the hub issue's credential store. It does not build OAuth, token storage, or any connection-management UI itself.

## 2. Business/Product Context

The repo owner's standing direction for all future roadmap work is to "always consider 3rd party integration opportunities such as google contact, google calendar, gmail, calendly, etc — where the user can add their API/Secret whatever required to connect." Reps already correspond with leads from their own personal Gmail outside this app's dedicated Resend inbound address, and already have lead contacts saved in their personal Google Contacts before those contacts ever reach this CRM. Both are currently invisible to the app. Surfacing that existing activity/contact data — without asking a rep to change how they already work in Gmail — closes a real visibility gap in the per-lead activity history and contact directory this app already invests in (issues #138–#142).

## 3. Current State (verified by direct code read)

- **Unified activity timeline** (issue #140): `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts` defines `ACTIVITY_LOG_COLLECTION = 'activityLog'`, `ActivityEntryType = 'email-outbound' | 'email-inbound' | 'note' | 'system'`, and `ActivitySource = 'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log'` (lines 15–16). `ActivityLogDocument` (lines 48–71) carries an `externalId?: string` field described explicitly as "the originating provider's own message identifier (Resend's email_id)... Only ever set by inbound-webhook writes," backing a **unique, sparse** index (`ensureActivityLogIndexes`, lines 82–92) that makes a provider's webhook retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity/route.ts` (lines 18–24, 48–67) merges `activityLog` docs with `outreach_logs` docs at read time via `mergeActivityTimeline()` — there is only ever one merged timeline, never a second parallel one.
- **UI**: `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx` fetches that same merged endpoint and renders it (lines 51–77, 111–162). Its **local** `ActivityEntry` type (lines 6–14) independently re-declares `source: 'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log'` — this union must be extended in lockstep with `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`'s own `ActivitySource`, or a new source value narrows correctly server-side but fails to type-check / render meaningfully client-side.
- **Contact-reply matching** (issue #142): `lib/contact-reply-matching.ts`'s `matchReplyToLeads(db, brand, tenantId, senderEmail)` (lines 54–80) looks up leads by `contactEmails: email` (an indexed, denormalized array — `contacts.ts`), returning `{kind: 'no-match'} | {kind: 'single-match', leadId} | {kind: 'multi-match', leadIds}`. `findMatchedContact()` (lines 86–107) re-resolves the specific `NormalizedContact` within a matched lead. `generateContactSuggestion()` (lines 140–184) parses a reply's signature block and writes a **pending, human-reviewable** suggestion to a `contactSuggestions` collection — it never writes `contacts[]` directly, matching the repo's established never-auto-merge stance (issue #137, `/admin/duplicates`).
- **Contact model**: `lib/contacts.ts`'s `NormalizedContact` type (lines 17–45), `normalizeContact()` (118–151), `dedupeContacts()` (183–224), and `contactKey()` (158–164: `name+phone` > `name+email` > bare `name`, lowercased) are the single shared normalization/dedup path used identically by every lead write route (POST/PUT/PATCH-MODIFY), replacing three previously-diverging implementations (issue #45). `deriveContactEmails()` (232–238) and `ensureContactEmailsIndex()` (246–254) keep the `contactEmails[]` index in sync on every write.
- **Existing inbound-email path** (issue #141): `lib/resend-webhook.ts` verifies Resend's Svix-signed webhook (`svix-id`/`svix-timestamp`/`svix-signature`) against the real `resend` SDK's runtime behavior, fails closed on any invalid signature, and is the only current writer of `source: 'inbound-webhook'` documents. This is a per-brand **dedicated mailbox address** model — zero rep setup required.
- **Existing periodic-job pattern**: `vercel.json` already declares three real Vercel Cron entries (`/api/admin/forecast-snapshot`, `/api/admin/ticket-size-recalc`, `/api/admin/cadence-tick`). `app/api/admin/cadence-tick/route.ts` demonstrates the established shape: `lib/api-auth.ts`'s `requireCronOrApiKey()` gates the route (fails closed in production if `SLG_API_KEY`/cron header isn't present), `app/lib/brand.ts`'s `getAllBrandConfigs()` iterates every configured brand, and a fixed per-run cap (`MAX_CADENCE_SENDS_PER_TICK = 200`) bounds each invocation so one busy brand can't starve another within a single serverless execution.
- **Admin human-review UI pattern**: `app/admin/duplicates/admin-duplicates-client.tsx` uses `AdminDataTable`/`AdminFormStatus`/`AdminResourceEmptyState` from `@sovereignsquad/gds-admin/client`, plus Mantine `Select`/`SegmentedControl`/`Button`, brand-scoped via `useAuth()`'s `brandLabels` — the established pattern this repo uses whenever a feature needs a rep/admin to review-then-apply rather than auto-apply.
- **Dependencies**: `package.json` (v2.4.188) currently has no Google API client library (`googleapis`, `google-auth-library`, or similar) anywhere in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` — this issue introduces the first one.

## 4. Problem Statement

Real lead-relevant email a rep sends/receives from their own Gmail — outside the brand's dedicated Resend address — never appears in this app's activity timeline, giving an incomplete picture of a lead's actual conversation history. Separately, a rep who already has a lead's contact saved in Google Contacts has no way to pull that person onto the lead record in this CRM except re-typing it by hand, risking drift from `contacts.ts`'s own established dedup/normalization rules if done outside the app's own write paths.

## 5. Goals

**Functional**
- Gmail messages to/from a lead's known contact addresses are ingested automatically (no rep action after connecting) and appear in the existing per-lead Activity tab, not a new/separate view.
- A rep can search their Google Contacts from a lead's detail view and attach a matched person as a new contact on that specific lead.

**Technical**
- Reuse `matchReplyToLeads`, `findMatchedContact`, and `generateContactSuggestion` (`lib/contact-reply-matching.ts`) unmodified for Gmail-sourced messages — no second matching implementation.
- Reuse `contactKey`, `dedupeContacts`, `deriveContactEmails` (`lib/contacts.ts`) unmodified for the Google Contacts import — no second dedup implementation.
- Add exactly one new `ActivitySource` value, `'gmail-sync'`, propagated consistently to every place that union is currently declared (`app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`, `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`).
- A well-defined, collision-resistant dedup key so the same physical email is never logged twice, including across the Resend and Gmail paths when both are active for the same brand.

**UX**
- Gmail-sourced entries render through the exact same `ActivityPanel` list, distinguishable by a labeled badge (not color alone).
- The Google Contacts import affordance follows this repo's established `/admin/duplicates`-style review-then-confirm pattern, not a silent background merge.
- No control implies a capability the rep hasn't actually connected (CLAUDE.md Rule 7) — an "Import from Google Contacts" action is disabled/hidden, never clickable-but-broken, when Google Contacts isn't connected.

## 6. Non-Goals

- **Real-time Gmail push sync** (Gmail API push notifications / Cloud Pub-Sub). v1 is periodic polling only — stated explicitly as a v1 simplification to avoid the added infrastructure (a Pub-Sub subscription, a public push endpoint, watch-renewal bookkeeping) this issue's scope doesn't justify.
- **Automatic, continuous, two-way Google Contacts sync.** v1 is a rep-initiated, one-way (Google → this app) import per contact. Continuous background sync has real conflict-resolution complexity (which side wins on a field disagreement, deletions, merges) that this repo's existing `/admin/duplicates` human-review pattern is a better fit for than an unattended job — not attempted here.
- **Sending email via Gmail.** That belongs to the separate "Outreach: One-off tracked email send" ticket's territory, which already sends via Resend. This issue does not add a second send path from a different identity.
- **Building the OAuth flow, token storage, or connection-management UI.** Entirely the sibling hub issue's scope; this issue only consumes a `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)`-shaped interface from it.
- **Google Calendar and Calendly.** Out of scope for this ticket (title-scoped to Gmail + Google Contacts only); tracked separately if/when picked up.

## 7. Mandatory Technical Constraints

### Design System Requirement (Mandatory)
All UI, UX, and design implementation must use only the Sovereign Squad General Design System (`@sovereignsquad/gds-core`/`gds-admin`/`gds-theme` `^6.5.0`, GitHub release tarballs, per `gds-adoption.json`). Any new sync-status/import UI must use GDS primitives or this repo's established Mantine usage pattern — no new component library.

- Brand/tenant scoping is mandatory on every new read/write, using the existing `resolveBrand()` (`app/lib/brand.ts`) and `getTenantId()`/`tenantFilter()` (`lib/tenant.ts`) helpers — no bespoke scoping logic.
- New periodic work is a Vercel Cron entry added to `vercel.json`, gated by `lib/api-auth.ts`'s `requireCronOrApiKey()`, following `app/api/admin/cadence-tick/route.ts`'s exact shape (per-run cap, per-brand loop via `getAllBrandConfigs()`).
- Any new direct npm dependency (a Google API client) must be checked for deprecation before being added, per CLAUDE.md Rule 1 — run and record the actual `npm view <pkg> deprecated` / install-time warning output, not an assumption.
- No parallel activity timeline, no parallel contact-dedup implementation — both are hard reuse requirements (Rule 5: never guess, verified against the real functions above).

## 8. Architecture

**Coexistence with the existing Resend inbound path (explicit decision):** Resend stays the **default, zero-setup** inbound path per brand's dedicated address. Gmail sync is an **opt-in addition**, not a replacement — a rep can have both active simultaneously for the same brand. Justification: Resend's dedicated address already guarantees every brand has inbound capture with no rep action; Gmail sync exists purely to *also* surface a rep's pre-existing personal-inbox activity for leads they already correspond with outside that address. Making them mutually exclusive would force a rep to give up the zero-setup path to opt into a personal one, which has no benefit. The corollary risk — the same physical email being visible to both paths for the same brand — is handled by the dedup key in §11, not by forcing exclusivity. Gmail sync is **read-only ingestion in v1**: it never sends from the rep's Gmail identity, avoiding two systems both capable of sending as the same brand/rep.

```
                         ┌─────────────────────────┐
 Resend dedicated addr → │ inbound-email webhook    │ → activityLog (source: 'inbound-webhook')
                         │ (issue #141, unchanged)  │
                         └─────────────────────────┘
                                                              \
                                                               ├─→ mergeActivityTimeline() → GET /api/leads/[id]/activity → ActivityPanel
                                                              /
 Rep's own Gmail inbox → ┌─────────────────────────┐
 (opt-in, polled)        │ Vercel Cron: gmail-sync  │ → activityLog (source: 'gmail-sync')
                         │ (this issue, new)        │
                         └─────────────────────────┘

 Rep's Google Contacts → ┌─────────────────────────┐
 (rep-initiated search)  │ Import-from-Contacts     │ → lead.contacts[] + contactEmails[]
                         │ action (this issue, new) │    (via the SAME write path every
                         └─────────────────────────┘     other contact write already uses)
```

Both new flows call into the hub issue's connection store only through a narrow interface this issue treats as a black box: `getValidAccessToken(connectionId): Promise<string | null>` (returns `null` when disconnected/unrefreshable — this issue never handles raw OAuth tokens, refresh logic, or credential storage itself).

## 9. Data Model/Contracts

- `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`: extend `ActivitySource` to `'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log' | 'gmail-sync'`. No other field on `ActivityLogDocument`/`ActivityEntry` changes shape — `externalId` is reused (see §11 for its Gmail-specific value format), not duplicated.
- `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`: extend its local `ActivityEntry['source']` union identically, and add a `'Gmail'` badge label alongside the existing `TYPE_LABEL` map (badge text, not color alone, per §14).
- New collection `gmailSyncCursors`: `{ connectionId: string, brand: string, tenantId: string, lastSyncedAt: Date, lastHistoryId?: string, updatedAt: Date }` — one document per rep-connection-per-brand, indexed on `{ connectionId: 1, brand: 1 }` (unique). Purely an internal bookkeeping collection; never exposed via any API response.
- Google Contacts import introduces **no new persisted collection** — a successful import is a normal `contacts[]`/`contactEmails[]` write through the lead's existing write path.

## 10. API Contracts

- `POST /api/integrations/gmail/sync` — cron-triggered only (`requireCronOrApiKey`), no request body required, iterates every brand (`getAllBrandConfigs()`) and every Gmail-connected rep for that brand (via the hub's connection listing). Returns `{ processed: number, ingested: number, skipped: number, failures: Array<{ connectionId: string, reason: string }> }`, mirroring `cadence-tick`'s `TickSummary` shape. Never called directly by client UI.
- `GET /api/integrations/google-contacts/search?q=<query>&brand=<brand>` — rep-initiated, requires brand access (`requireBrandAccessApi`, same guard `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity` already uses). Returns a bounded list (cap: 25) of `{ resourceName: string, name: string, email?: string, phone?: string, organization?: string }`. Read-only against Google; never writes anything.
- `POST /api/leads/[id]/contacts/import-google` — body `{ resourceName: string }`, brand/tenant-scoped exactly like every other lead-mutating route. Executes the import algorithm in §11 and returns `{ status: 'added' | 'already-exists', contact: NormalizedContact }`. Idempotent: re-posting the same `resourceName` for the same lead after it was already added returns `already-exists`, never a duplicate.

## 11. Algorithm/Processing Logic

The title's "two-way ... data flow" is two distinct one-way ingestion flows (Gmail → activity timeline; Google Contacts → lead contacts), not bidirectional writes back into Gmail or Google Contacts — consistent with §6's explicit non-goals.

**Algorithm A — Gmail periodic poll + cross-source dedup** (runs once per connected rep, per cron tick):

```
function pollGmailForRep(rep, brand, tenantId):
    token = ConnectionHub.getValidAccessToken(rep.gmailConnectionId)
    if token is null:
        record failure "needs reauth" for this connectionId; return   # never aborts the whole cron run

    cursor = gmailSyncCursors.findOne({ connectionId: rep.gmailConnectionId, brand })
    # Safety net even with a cursor: never trust a stale/missing cursor to
    # justify an unbounded fetch — v1 always bounds to a recent window.
    windowStart = cursor?.lastSyncedAt ?? (now - 30 days)   # first-ever sync: 30-day window, not full mailbox history (stated v1 simplification)

    knownEmails = distinct contactEmails[] across every lead for (brand, tenantId)   # one indexed query, reused across every message in this poll

    headersOnly = GmailAPI.listMessageHeaders(token, since: windowStart, max: 50)   # headers-only call first — body is fetched only for a message that already matches
    newCursorMark = windowStart

    for msg in headersOnly (chronological):
        participantEmails = normalizeEmail(msg.from) ∪ normalizeEmail(each of msg.to, msg.cc)
        if participantEmails ∩ knownEmails is empty:
            continue     # not lead-related — never fetch this message's body, never store anything about it

        primaryDedupKey = "gmail:" + msg.messageIdHeader     # RFC 2822 Message-ID, globally unique per email
        if activityLog.exists({ externalId: primaryDedupKey }):
            continue     # already ingested — safe to re-run this poll

        # Cross-source guard: the same message may already be visible via
        # Resend's inbound-webhook path for the same brand when both are active.
        fallbackHash = sha256(normalizeEmail(msg.from) + "|" + sortedJoin(normalizeEmail(msg.to/cc)) + "|" + lower(trim(msg.subject)) + "|" + floorToMinute(msg.date))
        if activityLog.exists({ brand, source in ['inbound-webhook','gmail-sync'], fallbackHash: fallbackHash, createdAt within ±2min of msg.date }):
            continue     # same physical email already logged via the other path

        body = GmailAPI.getMessageBody(token, msg.id)   # fetched only now, only for a matched message
        direction = (normalizeEmail(msg.from) == rep.gmailAddress) ? 'outbound' : 'inbound'
        counterpartyEmail = direction == 'outbound' ? firstMatchOf(msg.to/cc, knownEmails) : msg.from

        matchResult = matchReplyToLeads(db, brand, tenantId, counterpartyEmail)   # UNCHANGED from issue #142
        leadId, matchedContactKey, matchedLeadIds = branch on matchResult.kind exactly as #141's webhook route already does

        insert ActivityLogDocument({
            leadId, tenantId, brand,
            type: direction == 'inbound' ? 'email-inbound' : 'email-outbound',
            direction, fromAddress: msg.from, toAddresses: msg.to, ccAddresses: msg.cc,
            subject: msg.subject, bodyExcerpt: truncateBody(body),   # UNCHANGED truncateBody(), 280 chars
            matchedContactKey, matchedLeadIds,
            source: 'gmail-sync', externalId: primaryDedupKey, fallbackHash,
            createdAt: msg.date,
        })

        if direction == 'inbound' and leadId:
            generateContactSuggestion(db, brand, tenantId, leadId, counterpartyEmail, body, insertedId)   # UNCHANGED from issue #142

        newCursorMark = max(newCursorMark, msg.date)

    gmailSyncCursors.upsert({ connectionId: rep.gmailConnectionId, brand }, { lastSyncedAt: newCursorMark, updatedAt: now })
    # Cursor only committed after the full batch succeeds — an aborted/failed
    # run (rep disconnects mid-poll, API error) leaves the prior cursor intact,
    # so the next run safely re-covers the same window rather than skipping it.
```

**Algorithm B — Google Contacts one-way import** (rep-initiated, synchronous):

```
function importGoogleContact(rep, leadId, brand, tenantId, resourceName):
    token = ConnectionHub.getValidAccessToken(rep.googleContactsConnectionId)
    if token is null: return 409 "Google Contacts not connected"

    person = PeopleAPI.getContact(token, resourceName)
    candidate = normalizeContact({               # UNCHANGED normalizeContact() from lib/contacts.ts
        name: person.name, title: person.organizationTitle,
        email: person.primaryEmail, phone: person.primaryPhone,
    })

    lead = loadLead(leadId, tenantId, brand)      # existing brand/tenant-scoped lookup, unchanged
    existing = dedupeContacts(lead.contacts)      # UNCHANGED dedupeContacts()
    key = contactKey(candidate)                   # UNCHANGED contactKey(): name+phone > name+email > bare name
    if key == '': return 400 "Contact needs at least a name"

    if existing.some(c => contactKey(c) == key):
        return { status: 'already-exists', contact: matchingExisting }   # no write — same identity, per contactKey()'s own definition

    lead.contacts.push(candidate)
    lead.contactEmails = deriveContactEmails(dedupeContacts(lead.contacts))   # UNCHANGED, kept in sync exactly like every other write path
    write lead via the SAME contact-write path PUT /api/leads/[id] already uses   # no new write logic
    return { status: 'added', contact: candidate }
```

## 12. Mathematical/Ranking Logic

N/A — this issue introduces no scoring, ranking, or weighting logic. Matching is exact-identifier (email/contactKey) throughout, reusing existing deterministic functions; no probabilistic or ranked output is produced.

## 13. UX/Operator Behaviour

- **Gmail sync**: fully passive from the rep's point of view once connected via the hub issue's settings UI — no ongoing action required. New entries simply appear in a lead's existing Activity tab (`ActivityPanel`) on next load, labeled with a `Gmail` badge distinct from `Inbound reply`/`Outbound email`.
- **Google Contacts import**: an "Import from Google Contacts" action on the lead detail view (near the existing Contacts section), visible/enabled only when the rep has an active Google Contacts connection (per Rule 7 — never a clickable-but-broken affordance when disconnected). Opens a search field; results render as a selectable list; picking one shows an inline "Already a contact on this lead" (no write) or "Add contact" confirmation before committing, following the same review-then-confirm spirit as `/admin/duplicates`.
- Errors (expired token, API quota, network failure) never crash the panel — same pattern `ActivityPanel.tsx`'s existing suggestions fetch already uses: a failed fetch degrades gracefully to an empty/error state, not a broken UI.

## 14. Accessibility Requirements (mandatory)

- Gmail-sourced activity entries are distinguished by a **text badge label** ("Gmail"), never color alone, matching WCAG 1.4.1 (use of color).
- The Google Contacts search results list is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys / Tab, Enter to select) and exposes results as a proper listbox (`role="listbox"`/`option` or GDS/Mantine's equivalent accessible pattern) with visible focus states.
- Search result count and add/already-exists outcomes are announced via an `aria-live="polite"` region, so a screen-reader user isn't left waiting on a silent async action.
- The "Import from Google Contacts" affordance's disabled state (when not connected) is exposed via `aria-disabled`/`disabled`, not merely styled to look inactive — consistent with Rule 7's affordance-matches-capability requirement applying equally to assistive tech, not just sighted users.
- All new interactive elements meet the same color-contrast and focus-visibility bar the rest of this app's Mantine/GDS-based UI already meets — no bespoke styling introduced.

## 15. Edge Cases

- Both Resend inbound and Gmail sync active for the same brand simultaneously — explicitly supported (§8); the fallback-hash cross-source guard (§11, Algorithm A) prevents the same physical email from appearing twice.
- A rep's OAuth token is expired/revoked mid-poll — that rep's batch is skipped with a recorded failure reason; the cron run continues for every other rep/brand in the same invocation (same "don't let one failure block the batch" precedent `cadence-tick`'s per-brand loop already follows).
- A Gmail message with no `Message-ID` header (rare, malformed/very old mail) — falls back to the hash-based dedup key alone; documented as a known, low-probability v1 limitation, not silently ignored.
- A lead's contact email changes or is removed after Gmail messages were already ingested against it — historical `activityLog` entries keep their original `matchedContactKey`/`leadId` (no retroactive re-matching), identical to the existing Resend-sourced behavior — no new precedent invented.
- Rep disconnects Gmail mid-poll-cycle — the sync cursor is only committed after the full batch succeeds (§11), so a partial/aborted run never corrupts the resume point.
- Multi-match (the same contact email listed on more than one lead) — handled identically to `matchReplyToLeads`'s existing multi-match branch; no new behavior.
- Google Contacts search result has no email/phone (name-only) — `contactKey()` falls back to bare name (existing behavior); the import UI surfaces a "weaker match, review before adding" notice rather than silently treating it the same as an email/phone-backed contact.
- First-ever sync for a newly-connected rep with no cursor — bounded to a 30-day window, never a full historical mailbox backfill (stated v1 simplification, §11).
- Rep's Gmail address itself appears in `contactEmails[]` by coincidence (e.g. they added themselves as a contact by mistake) — out of scope to specially detect; treated the same as any other match, since preventing this is a data-quality issue in `contacts[]`, not a sync-logic concern.

## 16. Performance Expectations

- Poll cadence: every 15–30 minutes via a new `vercel.json` cron entry (final cadence decided at implementation time against Vercel Cron's actual minimum-interval limits for this project's plan) — never real-time (§6).
- Each cron invocation processes brands via `getAllBrandConfigs()` and reps within a bounded per-run cap (mirroring `MAX_CADENCE_SENDS_PER_TICK`'s precedent) so one busy brand/rep can't exhaust a single serverless function's time/memory budget.
- Per-message cost is minimized by a headers-only Gmail API call first; a message body is fetched only after it has already matched `contactEmails[]` — bounds both API quota usage and how much of a rep's unrelated personal mail is ever touched.
- The `contactEmails[]` intersection check is one indexed query per brand/tenant per poll, not a per-message database round-trip.
- Google Contacts search is rep-initiated and synchronous — target p95 response time under 2 seconds, consistent with a live search-as-you-type interaction rather than a batch operation.

## 17. Security/Privacy Requirements (mandatory)

This touches a rep's real personal Gmail inbox and real third-party PII (lead contacts) — scope minimization is the central constraint throughout, not an afterthought:

- **Minimum OAuth scopes**: Gmail — `gmail.readonly` only (never `gmail.modify`, `gmail.send`, or full-mailbox scopes; this issue never sends or mutates the rep's mailbox). Google Contacts — `contacts.readonly` only (never the read-write `contacts` scope; v1 never writes back to Google Contacts, per §6).
- **No token handling in this issue**: OAuth tokens are stored, refreshed, and retrieved exclusively through the sibling hub issue's credential store, accessed only via the narrow `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` interface (§8). This issue's own code never persists a raw access/refresh token.
- **Data-minimization by construction**: the headers-only-then-body-on-match fetch order (§16) means a rep's unrelated personal correspondence is never even fetched into this app's process, let alone stored — only messages whose participants intersect a lead's own `contactEmails[]` are ever touched past the header stage.
- **Body storage is already bounded**: reused `truncateBody()` (`activity-log-store.ts`, 280-char cap) — full email bodies are never persisted, exactly as the existing Resend-sourced entries already behave; this is not a new decision introduced by this issue.
- **Strict brand/tenant isolation**: every read/write goes through the existing `resolveBrand()`/`tenantFilter()` helpers — a rep's Gmail data ingested under one brand's context must never cross-write into another brand/tenant's `activityLog`.
- **Revocation behavior, stated explicitly**: disconnecting Gmail or Google Contacts (owned by the hub issue's UI) immediately stops future polls/imports for that connection. Already-ingested `activityLog` entries are **not** retroactively deleted — this matches how disabling the Resend webhook doesn't purge past inbound activity, and is called out here as an intentional, consistent choice rather than an oversight.
- **No credential or token values in logs**, ever — matching this repo's existing discipline (`activity-log-store.ts`/`contacts.ts` log only structural error context, never payload contents).
- **Rate limiting/backoff**: Gmail API and People API quota errors are caught and backed off per-connection, never allowed to fail an entire cron invocation for every other rep.

## 18. Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ActivitySource` (both `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts` and `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`) includes `'gmail-sync'`, consistently, with no type mismatch between server and client.
- [ ] A real Gmail message from/to an address present in a brand's `contactEmails[]` is ingested into `activityLog` with `source: 'gmail-sync'`, correct `leadId`/`matchedContactKey` (via unmodified `matchReplyToLeads`/`findMatchedContact`), and appears in `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity`'s merged response and in `ActivityPanel`.
- [ ] A Gmail message from an address not in any lead's `contactEmails[]` is never fetched past the headers stage and never stored.
- [ ] Re-running the poll for the same time window never produces a duplicate `activityLog` entry (verified against `externalId`).
- [ ] When both Resend and Gmail sync are active for the same brand and see the same physical email, only one `activityLog` entry results (fallback-hash guard verified).
- [ ] An inbound Gmail-sourced reply with a changed signature-block detail produces a pending `contactSuggestions` entry via unmodified `generateContactSuggestion()`, never an automatic `contacts[]` write.
- [ ] `POST /api/leads/[id]/contacts/import-google` adds a new contact via the existing write path, keeps `contactEmails[]` in sync, and returns `already-exists` (no duplicate write) on a repeat import of the same person.
- [ ] The "Import from Google Contacts" action is disabled/hidden (not merely styled inactive) when the rep has no active Google Contacts connection.
- [ ] An expired/revoked token for one rep does not prevent the same cron run from processing every other connected rep.

## 19. Testing Requirements

- **Unit tests**: dedup-key generation (`externalId`, `fallbackHash`) for representative message shapes; the cross-source dedup guard's window/match logic; the `contactKey()`-based already-exists branch in Algorithm B; the headers-only-then-body-on-match gating logic (asserting a body fetch is never issued for a non-matching message).
- **Integration tests**: a simulated Gmail poll cycle against a mocked Gmail/People API and `mongodb-memory-server` (already a devDependency) producing correct `activityLog` entries, with the same poll run twice producing no duplicates; a simulated `import-google` call verifying the resulting `contacts[]`/`contactEmails[]` state matches every other write path's invariants.
- **Manual verification** (documented, per CLAUDE.md Rule 4): at least one real end-to-end run against a real test Gmail account and a real Google Contacts entry, before this ships, with the actual output recorded — not inferred.
- Full CLAUDE.md Rule 1 gate: `npx tsc --noEmit` zero errors, `npm run lint` zero errors/zero warnings in touched files, `npx vitest run` and the smoke suite (`npm run test:smoke`) 100% passing, `npm run audit:gds-style` clean for any new UI.

## 20. Documentation Requirements

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: document the Gmail-sync and Google-Contacts-import flows, the coexistence decision with Resend (§8), and the dedup-key design (§11).
- `docs/OPERATOR_GUIDE.md`: document how a rep connects Gmail/Contacts (pointing to the hub issue's connection UI) and how to use the "Import from Google Contacts" action.
- `README.md` and/or environment-variable documentation: any new required configuration this issue itself introduces (e.g. the cron schedule entry in `vercel.json`), distinct from the OAuth client credentials themselves (owned by the hub issue).
- `CHANGELOG.md` + version bump, per this repo's existing convention.
- Any newly-added direct dependency's deprecation-check result (per §7) recorded in the commit/PR description, even if the result is "clean."

## 21. Handover Requirements

- Rollback for Gmail sync: disable the `vercel.json` cron entry (or flip a feature flag if one is added at implementation time) — stops all future polling immediately; no destructive action needed, `activityLog` data already written is left as-is (consistent with §17's revocation behavior).
- Rollback for Google Contacts import: remove/disable the UI action and the `import-google` route — no background job to stop, since imports are synchronous and rep-initiated only.
- No production data is touched destructively by either flow: Gmail sync only inserts new `activityLog` documents (never updates/deletes existing ones); Contacts import only appends to `contacts[]` via the same reviewed write path every other contact addition already uses.
- This issue introduces no new auth/session model — it consumes the hub issue's connection store as a black box; a handover reader only needs to understand the `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` contract, not any OAuth internals (those live in the hub issue).

## 22. Delivery Expectations (CLAUDE.md zero-tolerance gate)

Per CLAUDE.md Rule 1, nothing in this issue's implementation reaches `main` with: any `tsc --noEmit` error; any lint error, or any lint warning in a touched file; a failing `vitest run` or smoke-suite test; an undisclosed newly-added direct dependency deprecation. If a new Google API client dependency's deprecation status, or its own transitive deprecation warnings, can't be fully resolved within this issue's scope, that must be stated explicitly in the PR/commit description with a one-line reason, per Rule 1 — never silently shipped unmentioned.

## 23. Final Rule

If implementing this to the full standard above (in particular, achieving a genuinely zero-warning, zero-deprecation dependency addition, or building out the full accessibility surface in §14) turns out to require more scope than this single issue reasonably covers, that must be said explicitly and split into its own separately-tracked follow-up issue — never silently under-delivered against this issue's own Acceptance Criteria.

## 24. Dependencies/Execution Order

- **Depends on**: "Integrations: Third-party connection hub - admin-managed credentials for Google Workspace and Calendly" (sibling issue, filed in the same batch as this one) — this issue's `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` interface and all Google OAuth scopes/consent flow are that issue's deliverable, not this one's. Implementation of this issue should not begin until that interface's contract is at least defined, even if its full UI isn't finished.
- **Builds on** (already shipped, no changes required to their own logic): #140 (`activityLog`/`ActivityPanel`), #141 (Resend inbound webhook — coexistence partner, §8), #142 (`contact-reply-matching.ts` — reused unmodified), and `lib/contacts.ts`'s contact-normalization module (reused unmodified).
- **Explicitly non-blocking, in either direction**, with the "Outreach: One-off tracked email send" ticket — that issue sends via Resend; this issue is read-only ingestion via Gmail; different code paths, no shared state, no ordering requirement between them (§6).

items.title: Pre-canned HyperDX dashboards -- per-team seeding, org-fenced throughput, DFE 2.1 equivalents
items.body:
A DFE deploy currently lands with an empty HyperDX. You log in, you get a search
box, and you build every chart yourself. Every deploy. That is the gap this closes:
the stack should ship knowing how to watch itself.

Full spec, with the live survey it was written off and the DFE 2.1 Grafana
heritage it takes from: `dfe-infra/docs/plans/2026-08-20-otel-dashboards.md`.

This issue is the dfe-hyperdx half (fork seeding + the dashboards themselves).
The collector-side telemetry gaps ride the dfe-infra companion issue.

## What we ship

Three dashboards, seeded per team, working identically on slim, single and scale:

- DFE Throughput - the landing page. Events in, by whom, how fast, how far behind.
- Pipeline Health - Kafka lag and its rate of change, buffer depth, insert latency,
  worker-pool saturation. The "why is throughput wrong" one.
- ClickHouse Health - parts per partition, merges, insert rate and latency, memory.
  The single most likely thing to take a deploy down.

## The bit that makes it work

The ClickHouse row policy already makes the answer role-dependent, so ONE dashboard
serves both audiences. A platform reader (dfe_query_reader) sees every org broken
out by _org_id. An org_viewer sees the identical tiles fenced to their own org.
Nothing in the dashboard JSON knows which is which. DFE 2.1 needed a
customer_name template variable and a database per customer to do this - we do not.

## What we reuse rather than rebuild

Upstream already has file-based dashboard provisioning: `syncDashboards(teamId, dir)`
in `packages/api/src/tasks/provisionDashboards/index.ts`, idempotent, upserts on
name+team+provisioned, never clobbers a user dashboard. Do not write a second one.

The one real blocker is that tile configs reference sources and connections by
Mongo ObjectId, and provisioned JSON cannot know those ids. Upstream's own
AUTO_PROVISION.md example uses a source NAME, which silently does not work because
syncDashboards writes tiles verbatim with no name resolution. So the fork ships
JSON with `{{source:otel_metrics}}` / `{{connection}}` tokens and resolves them at
seed time, in `ensureOrgConnection` where the ids have just been created. That
function already carries the extension-point comment for it.

Platform-only dashboards are seeded only to the platform team, so a tenant never
holds a dashboard with a dangling source reference.

## Landing page

dfe-ui /observe falls through to /search today, and it cannot hard-code a dashboard
id because provisioned ids are per-team ObjectIds. The fork adds a route that
resolves the caller's team's provisioned DFE Throughput and redirects; dfe-ui just
changes its default feature to that route. One path, no id crossing repos.

## Decision needed before the data-quality dashboard

The 2.1 Data Quality dashboards were pure `system.query_log` - insert exceptions
decoded into human causes (missing columns, bad types, invalid JSON, missing table).
Genuinely the best thing in the 2.1 set after throughput. But
`dfe_audit.query_log_archive` carries none of exception_code, exception,
written_rows or tables (checked on the rig). Either extend the archive MV
(recommended - bounded retention, no system-table grant, works against ClickHouse
Cloud) or grant dfe_query_reader read on system.query_log (cheaper, but that table
holds every tenant's query text). Platform-only either way.

## Done when

A freshly created team lands with the dashboards provisioned, all tokens resolved
and nothing dangling; the platform team sees full-stack throughput broken out by
_org_id; an org_viewer driven through Playwright sees only their own org's rows in
every tile; and dfe-ui /observe opens on the throughput dashboard rather than
search.

## Stages

- S2 token resolver + dashboard seeding in ensureOrgConnection
- S3 DFE Throughput + DFE Platform Overview JSON
- S4 default-dashboard route
- S5 dfe-ui landing default (needs a dfe-ui issue, Kay)
- S6 Pipeline Health + ClickHouse Health JSON (needs the dfe-infra companion landed)
- S7 Playwright verification, platform and org_viewer
- S8 query-log schema decision, then Ingest Data Quality

S2/S3 can start now - the throughput tiles need only data that is already flowing.

items.title: [P0] Audit en handhaaf 100% portaalinvoer, externe-data-doorwerking en tenant-readback
items.body:
# Doel
**Werkelijke 100% formulier- en externe-brondekking** in het bestaande klantportaal aantoonbaar maken. Geen parallelle Brain, Heartbeat of scheduler. Gaat verder dan de nu ingediende lossless causal-impact reparatie in PR #4214.

## Traceerbare verplichtingen

1. Inventariseer alle routes/pages uit `portal-v2/page-registry.js`, `portal-v2/page-shell.js`, `portal-next`, legacy en dynamische/integratieformulieren. Verzamel in een automatisch gevalideerde matrix: pagina, veld-ID, eigenaar, tenantcontext, write-endpoint, readback, sourceRevision, Brain-ACK en afhankelijke modellen. Markeer read-only en admin-only apart.
2. Sluit iedere customer write aan op één bestaande canonieke state/BusinessInput writeflow of bewijs een andere authoritative servermutatie met precieze Brain lineage. Verbied parallelle browserstores en orphan inputs.
3. Externe provider-/regulerings-/marktdata: op nieuwe observation via bestaande Source Universe + Company Graph per tenant impact herbeoordelen; alleen daadwerkelijk gewijzigde dependency subgraph, met provenance en freshness. Externe refresh mag customer input niet overschrijven; tenant-impact is nooit globale signaaldata.
4. Voor finance, AI/cloud, governance, proces, marketing, mensen, risico, juridische kaders en CSRD geldt: bij relevante change de juiste modellen herberekenen of expliciet REVIEW_REQUIRED als gegevens/regeldragende bron ontbreken. Geen gefingeerde €-impact/emissies/compliance.
5. Complete durability: transactioneel idempotente outbox/split-batch van >750 KB, restarts/offline, foutretries zonder dubbele Brain-records, monotone versiecontrole en per-batch consumer-ACK.
6. Klant ziet in dezelfde portalweergave: wijziging, bron, tijd, vorige/nieuwe waarde waar geautoriseerd, betrokken pagina's/modellen, actueel/stale/review/pending/applied, reden, voorgestelde actie en readback; alleen eigen tenantinformatie. De bestaande impactmap uit PR #4214 is de eerste UI-draaglaag.
7. CI-contract: auto-gegenereerde route/form-dekking op iedere PR; browser E2E met twee geïsoleerde tenants, 200 velden, 1000 signalen, gelijktijdige writes, fake provider failure, conflict, revocation, GDPR/minimisatie, backfill en bijbehorende evidence.
8. Afsluiten alleen na exact-main Required+CodeQL, Supabase runtime/projection readback, Netlify deployment & authenticated browser readback, en bewezen terugkoppeling naar ONE BRAIN/Heartbeat/Powerhouse. Admin-control-center toont per keten onafhankelijk bewijs, geen kunstmatige green.

## Huidige realiteit
Het bestaande impact engine-contract registreert alle **geregistreerde page IDs**, niet het daadwerkelijke gebruik van iedere DOM-input. PR #4214 sluit enkele bewezen causal-loss/race-gaten en voegt klantzichtbaarheid toe. Dit issue mag niet automatisch sluiten op basis van PR #4214 alleen. Laat eerdere gekoppelde verplichtingen bestaan tot eindbewijs.

## Borgingsconsolidatie — 20 oktober 2026

Fingerprint: `borging-consolidatie-20261020-v1`. Op expliciet verzoek zijn negen bestaande Notion-pagina's bijgewerkt en teruggelezen; drie betrokken database-records hebben daarnaast actuele samenvattende properties gekregen. Geen nieuwe parallelle registers.

- [Master Build, Borging & Go-Live Register](https://app.notion.com/p/3c3da36aac8a81dda3fec4fc12bba5df): geconsolideerde statusmatrix en bronbewijs.
- [Canonical System Map](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a8152be3dedbb32b06239): samenhang en bewijsgrenzen.
- [Error Register & Release Gates](https://app.notion.com/p/3c6da36aac8a81cc9731ea9355881230): bewezen herstel versus open resultaten.
- [Menselijk Handboek](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a81acaad1c88751e9e814): uitleg borging en ondernemerbetekenis.
- [Direct Knowledge Base](https://app.notion.com/p/3c7da36aac8a817a8beff480e45a2aef): learning, herstel en preventie.
- [Dashboard Hub](https://app.notion.com/p/3e4da36aac8a81fbb340daccce80dec8): bestaande vindplaatsen gekoppeld aan actuele waarheid.
- [Engineering Registry](https://app.notion.com/p/3cada36aac8a81199e6cfa9217bf5218): historische Make-snapshots onderscheiden van actuele evidence.
- [Bestaande auditregistratie](https://app.notion.com/p/3ffda36aac8a81ac927fe06346420cb9): ochtendbevindingen behouden, latere bewijzen aangevuld.
- [Portal V2 Current State](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a81deb0f9e516a088939a): inhoud en statusvelden bijgewerkt; fixing/blocked blijft functionele acceptatiestatus.

Documentaire readback: alle negen pagina's bevatten exact eenmaal deze fingerprint; centrale matrix bevat de vier exacte bronlinks en e-mailproductie-event. De drie bijgewerkte recordproperties zijn na schrijven teruggelezen. Dit sluit deze documentaire synchronisatie, niet de volledige systeemacceptatie.

Open borgingsdekking onder dit bestaande issue: volledige vergelijking **capability/route/veld → owner/autoriteit → code/config → logging → test → exacte productie-identiteit → getroffen portaalpagina → resultaat**. Volledigheid is niet aangetoond door deze documentatie-update. Twee echte geautoriseerde klantketens, Brain/Heartbeat ACK, negatieve tenantisolatie, #4558 representatieve 51-veldpariteit, daadwerkelijke connector/model/forecast-output en afzonderlijke providerresultaten blijven nodig.

Bronnen: [laatste portaalacceptatie](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6296290722), [laatste historische telling 11 bewezen/225 open](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6295423181), [#4567 e-mailproductiebewijs](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4478#issuecomment-6296265910), [release/index/HTTP-bewijs](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6295387867).

Geen productiecode, scheduler, autorisatie of portaalweergave veranderd; runtime-consumptie van de nieuwe Notion-tekst en automatische volledige inventarisdekking worden niet als bewezen geregistreerd. Oorspronkelijke acceptatiecriteria en historie hierboven blijven intact; issue blijft open.

items.body:
**Task ID:** `t18176` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~23h`
**Logged:** 2026-07-25
**Tags:** `parent-task` `enhancement` `framework` `knowledge` `security`

## Description

Plan secure personal and shared social knowledge corpora

## Worker Guidance


### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `todo/plans/social-knowledge-corpora.md` — accepted architecture, schemas, boundaries, and phase verification matrix.
- **Then load:** only the existing contracts named by the current phase in the plan's “Relevant existing contracts” section.
- **Load only if:** a phase touches protected storage or remote model routing — `.agents/reference/vault.md` and `.agents/aidevops/knowledge-plane/03-platform-and-policy.md`.
- **Why:** preserve the parent decisions while keeping each worker below a bounded reading budget.
- **Stop when:** the child has verified target files, one complete write surface, focused tests, narrow file scope, and no unresolved cross-phase schema decision.

### Worker Quick-Start

```text
1. Do not implement this parent issue directly; file or execute only the current child.
2. Keep social as knowledge ingress/retrieval, not a new `_social` plane.
3. Use one physical store/index per corpus and derive access from authenticated membership.
4. Raw evidence is authoritative; normalized rows, FTS, embeddings, and Markdown are projections.
5. Official API/archive first; browser capture only for an explicit, tested gap.
6. Likes/bookmarks/reposts/follows are not proof of opinion.
7. No social-platform writes, credentials in AI context, or private data in public Git/GitHub.
```

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: todo/plans/social-knowledge-corpora.md` — parent architecture and phased delivery contract.
- `NEW: todo/tasks/t18176-brief.md` — canonical parent brief and sequential phase declarations.
- `EDIT: TODO.md` — parent task entry and issue reference.
- `CHILD-DEFINED: .agents/aidevops/knowledge-plane/**` — corpus contract and policy documentation where required by a leaf.
- `CHILD-DEFINED: .agents/scripts/**` — corpus, social adapter, query, routine, Vault integration, and focused tests selected by each leaf after discovery.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `TODO.md`, the canonical issue body, `.agents/scripts/shared-phase-filing.sh`, `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`, parent-task worker diagnostics, maintainers, and child issue authors read this plan. Runtime callers are not modified by this planning task.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** This planning PR writes only `todo/plans/social-knowledge-corpora.md`, `todo/tasks/t18176-brief.md`, `TODO.md`, and the canonical issue body. Each child must enumerate its runtime writers before dispatch.

# AEX Web — Developer Onboarding Guide

> This README is a practical, code-verified guide to the `aex-web` codebase (npm package name `bigfixaex`). Every claim below is backed by an exact file path (and line number where useful). Anything that could not be verified from the code is called out explicitly in [Unknowns / Areas Requiring Further Investigation](#unknowns--areas-requiring-further-investigation) instead of being guessed.

---

## Project Overview

**What this project does.** AEX Web is HCL's "Agent Experience" platform: a multi-tenant conversational-AI / chatbot + live-agent-assist web application. A single Node.js/Express server hosts:

- A server-rendered chat widget / bot UI (Handlebars views).
- An **admin/configuration console** (Vue 3 SPA, `src/`) — GenAI agent builder, workflow automation, RBAC, self-heal, learning console, live-agent-console admin, channel configuration, etc.
- A **live-agent console** (Vue 3 SPA, `src-agent/`) — the human-agent chat/dashboard UI used for live chat hand-off.
- A large library of **GenAI/LLM integrations** (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI cloud, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex/Gemini, custom LLM endpoints) plus an **A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol** server/client.
- A **Microsoft Bot Framework** connector layer (Teams, Slack, Telegram, Facebook, SMS, email, IVR/Twilio, Google Chat).
- ~50 pluggable **"tool" connectors** (Slack, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Jira, AWS/Azure/GCP services, databases, etc.) that GenAI agents can call as functions.
- Real-time features (live chat, agent transfer, workflow monitoring) over **Socket.IO**.

**Main purpose.** Let enterprise customers (tenants) configure and run AI-powered chatbots and live-agent-assist workflows across many channels, backed by a common admin console, RBAC, and a large set of external-system connectors.

**Main technologies/frameworks:**
- **Backend:** Node.js 24 (pinned in `package.json:205`, enforced at runtime in `app.js:5-8`), Express 4, Express-Handlebars, Socket.IO 4, Passport (LDAP/SAML/OIDC/IBM AppID), Redis (`redis`/`@redis/client`, standalone or cluster), MongoDB / IBM Cloudant / DynamoDB (pluggable via a "Dispatcher" abstraction), `botbuilder` (MS Bot Framework), `@a2a-js/sdk`.
- **Frontend:** Vue 3 + Vue Router + Pinia, built with Vite; two separate SPAs (`src/`, `src-agent/`) plus legacy jQuery/Materialize-based assets under `public/`.
- **Cloud SDKs:** AWS (`@aws-sdk/*`), Azure (`@azure/*`), IBM Cloud (`ibm-cos-sdk`, `@ibm-cloud/cloudant`, `ibmcloud-appid`).
- **Testing:** Vitest.
- **CI/CD:** Azure DevOps pipelines under `DevOps/` (SonarQube, Mend SCA, AppScan SAST, container security, image signing) — see `DevOps/README.md`.

---

## Project Structure

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app.js` | The entire Express/Socket.IO app bootstrap (see [Application Startup Flow](#application-startup-flow)). |
| `dev.js` / `config-back.js` | `dev.js` hardcodes the local-dev tenant subdomain (`devplayground`). `config-back.js` is a **legacy/unused** Cloudant+Memcache config module, not read by current startup code. |
| `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js` | Loads all configuration and secrets (per-`AEX_ENV`), and creates the global `redisClient`. |
| `lib/corearchitecture.js` | Base class (`CoreArchitecture`) for per-session conversation handling; the canonical example of the `GLOBAL.Dispatcher` service-locator pattern. |
| `lib/scripts/dispatchers/` | The pluggable-backend abstraction layer: DB (`dbServices/`), GenAI (`cognitiveServices/`), object storage (`objectStorageServices/`), key vault, third-party/channel-dependent services. |
| `lib/scripts/` (everything else) | Business-logic modules: live-agent transfer/queueing, bot connectors, A2A protocol, GenAI prompting, workflows, notifications, LDAP client/sync, translation, etc. See [Core Modules](#core-modules). |
| `lib/socket/` | Socket.IO event handlers: `chat.js` (entry point), `liveAgentv2.js` (live-agent broker events), `notification.js`, `workflowMonitor.js`. |
| `routes/` | All HTTP routes, split into `unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js` (mounted in that order — see [Application Architecture](#application-architecture)), plus ~40 feature subfolders (`genAI/`, `liveAgentConsole/`, `rbac/`, `lums/`, `channels/`, `workflows/`, etc.). |
| `middleware/` | `ldapRoleRefresh.js` (background LDAP role sync) and `rbac/` (permission middleware, static role/permission matrix, user-operation guards). |
| `models/` | Data-access classes. Either extend `models/base/index.js` (`BaseModel`, wraps the Dispatcher), call the Dispatcher directly (legacy prototype style, e.g. `models/customer.js`), or are pure-Redis models (e.g. `models/webNotifications.js`). |
| `tools/` | ~50 self-contained connector plugins (Slack, ServiceNow, AWS, databases, etc.) with a uniform `{name, fields, functions[]}` shape, invocable as LLM function-calling tools. |
| `src/` | Vue 3 SPA — the **admin/configuration console**, served at `/admin`. |
| `src-agent/` | Vue 3 SPA — the **live-agent console** (chat + live dashboard), served at `/agents`. |
| `views/` | Handlebars templates — legacy/auth pages, the server-rendered chat widget, login/SSO/OIDC pages. |
| `public/` | Static assets, including the legacy embeddable chat-widget bundle (built by `buildEngine/bundle.js`). |
| `buildEngine/` | Build/post-build tooling: `uiCacher.js` (Brotli-compresses & uploads `dist/` to object storage/CDN after `vite build`), `bundle.js` (legacy chat-widget bundler). |
| `config/` | Only `config/actions.js` exists in this checkout (a small action-name registry). `config/config.js` (the local/dev default config) is referenced by code but **not present** in this checkout — see [Unknowns](#unknowns--areas-requiring-further-investigation). |
| `migrate/` | **Tenant provisioning** scripts (`core.js`, `manage.js`) — not a schema-migration framework; seeds new-tenant data (users, views, default groups, console catalog). |
| `tests/` | Vitest test suite, mirrors `routes/`, `lib/`, `models/`, `middleware/` structure. |
| `tools*/DevOps/deployment` config | `Dockerfile` (root), `deployment/{dev,ibm,onprem}/` (per-environment Dockerfiles/build scripts), `DevOps/` (CI pipeline YAMLs + its own README). |

---

```
                     │  notification.js           │   │          DynamoDB       │
                     │  (@socket.io/redis-adapter │   │  .CGS  → GenAI providers│
                     │   for multi-instance pub/  │   │  .OSS  → object storage │
                     │   sub via redisClient)      │   │  .KP,.TPA,.CDS → more   │

                                    │                         │
                     ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐  ┌───────▼────────────────────┐
                     │  lib/scripts/* business logic│  │  models/* (BaseModel or    │
                     │  agentManager, queueManager, │  │  direct Dispatcher calls)  │
                     │  transferManager, agentTransfer,│└───────┬────────────────────┘
                     │  connectorBots (Bot Framework),│         │
                     │  a2aServer/a2aClient, workflows,│         ▼
                     │  ldapClient/ldapSync, gptPrompter│  MongoDB / Cloudant / DynamoDB
                     └──────────────┬──────────────┘   (system of record, per DB_TYPE)
                                    │
                     ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
                     │        tools/* (~50)         │
                     │  Slack, ServiceNow, AWS, DBs, │
                     │  webhooks... invoked as LLM   │
                     │  function-calling tools        │
                     └───────────────────────────────┘

                     Redis (global `redisClient`, standalone or cluster):
                     sessions (connect-redis) · caching (lib/helper/caching.js) ·
                     rate limiting · Socket.IO adapter pub/sub · agent/queue/transfer
                     state · LDAP connection-pool invalidation · A2A context cache
```

Key architectural traits:
- **Single global service locator** (`GLOBAL.Dispatcher`, set once in `app.js:181`) hides which physical backend (Mongo/Cloudant/DynamoDB, which GenAI provider, which object-storage vendor) answers a given call — see [Database / Storage](#database--storage).
- **Global singletons via bare `GLOBAL`/`config`/`redisClient`/`passport` variables** (declared `writable` via ESLint globals in `.eslintrc.cjs:13-20`), not passed through constructors/DI — an important non-obvious convention for new contributors.
- **Three route "tiers"** (`unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js`) implement a coarse-grained "must be logged in" / "no ACL" / "ACL + RBAC" split, layered with a finer-grained RBAC v2 permission system (`middleware/rbac/`).
- **Two independent Vue SPAs** (`src/` admin console, `src-agent/` agent console) are built as **separate Vite entry points** (`vite.config.js:27-40`: `index.html` → `main`, `agent.html` → `agent`) and served from the same Express server at `/admin` and `/agents` respectively.
- **Redis is load-bearing infrastructure**, not just a cache: sessions, Socket.IO horizontal scaling (via `@socket.io/redis-adapter`), live-agent queue/transfer state, rate limiting, and LDAP pool coordination all depend on it.

## Application Startup Flow

Entry point: `npm start` → `node app.js` (`package.json:12`).

1. **Node version gate** — `app.js:5-8` exits immediately if the running Node isn't v24.x.
2. **`require('module-alias/register')`** (`app.js:9`) activates the `_moduleAliases` map from `package.json:209-219` (`@root`, `@models`, `@lib`, `@libscr`, `@libhlp`, `@helpers`, `@routes`, `@tools`, `@middleware`) so every subsequent `require('@lib/...')`-style import resolves correctly.
3. **`initEnv()`** — `require('@libhlp/envConfiguration').init` (i.e. `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js`) is awaited **before anything else runs**. This:
   - Builds the global `config` object from `process.env.AEX_ENV` (`aks` | `eks` | `onprem` | default) — see [Configuration](#configuration).
   - In production, fetches secrets from the environment's secret store (Azure Key Vault for `aks`, AWS Secrets Manager/IAM for `eks`, OpenBao for `onprem`).
   - Creates the global `redisClient` — a Redis Cluster client (`@redis/client` `createCluster`) or standalone client (`createClient`) depending on `config.IS_REDIS_CLUSTER_MODE`, connects it, and PINGs it before returning.
4. Inside the `.then(async () => {...})` callback (the rest of `app.js`):
   - Express app + `http.createServer(app)` + Socket.IO server (`new IOServer(server, {pingTimeout:15000, serveClient:false})`) are created (`app.js:12-26`).
   - Handlebars view engine registered with custom `json`/`checkif` helpers (`app.js:34-52`).
   - **Session store**: `connect-redis`'s `RedisStore` wraps `redisClient` (`app.js:54-56`); cookie name `app`; secure/`sameSite:'none'`/`partitioned` cookies in production.
   - Body parsers, `passport.initialize()/session()`, `connect-flash`, `lusca` security headers (nosniff, HSTS, CSP, referrer-policy), `morgan` logging (`app.js:99-149`).
   - **`GLOBAL` wiring** (`init()`, `app.js:179-198`): `GLOBAL.TEMP_PATH`, `GLOBAL.Dispatcher = new (require('./lib/scripts/dispatchers'))()`, `GLOBAL.SplitIntent`, and `require('./lib/scripts/translationAgent').translationInit()`.
   - **Tenant/subdomain resolution middleware** (`app.js:202-235`): from `config.SUB_DOMAIN` for on-prem/aks/eks, or parsed from `req.hostname` for multi-tenant SaaS (session destroyed on subdomain mismatch); `dev.js`'s hardcoded subdomain is used outside production.
   - **`@socket.io/redis-adapter` wiring** (`app.js:164-171`): duplicates `redisClient` into a `sub` client, then `io.adapter(createAdapter(redisClient, sub, {...}))` — this is what lets Socket.IO events fan out across multiple app instances.
   - **Route mounting**, strictly in this order (`app.js:238-243`): `unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js` → 404 handler.
   - **`startServer(port, address)`** (`app.js:268-277`) polls `vectorDBs('checkConnection')` every second and only calls `server.listen(...)` once the vector DB connection is confirmed. Production listens on `process.env.PORT` at `0.0.0.0`; non-production hardcodes port `3000` on `localhost`.
   - Graceful-shutdown handlers (`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/etc., production only) decrement Redis-backed agent-queue counters and close Redis/vector-DB connections before `process.exit`.
   - Finally, `lib/socket/chat.js` and `lib/socket/notification.js` are initialized with `io` and the duplicated `sub` Redis client (`app.js:334-335`) — this is where the single `io.on('connection', ...)` handler actually lives (see [Request/API Flow](#requestapi-flow)).

## Request/API Flow

### HTTP request path
```
Client
  → app.js middleware chain (cookies, session/RedisStore, tenant-subdomain resolve,
     body parsers, passport, lusca security headers, morgan)
  → routes/unauthroutes.js   (public: assets, /login, /logout, captcha, webhooks, bot inbound...)
       → ends with a login gate: if !req.session.username → redirect to '/' (unless XHR/API)
  → routes/naclroutes.js     (must be logged in; ldapRoleRefresh middleware; e.g. /agent, /notify, /user_info)
  → routes/aclroutes.js      (admin/management; re-validates customer_credentials; legacy v1 ACL check;
                               RBAC v2 via routes/permissionWrappers.js + middleware/rbac/permissionMiddleware.js)
  → route handler (routes/**/index.js)
       → models/* (BaseModel-backed, legacy-prototype, or pure-Redis)
            → GLOBAL.Dispatcher.service(GLOBAL.Dispatcher.DB, serviceKeys) → Mongo/Cloudant/DynamoDB
       → and/or lib/scripts/* business logic (agentTransfer, workflows, gptPrompter, connectorBots...)
       → and/or redisClient directly (cache, queue counters, rate limiting)
  → res.json(...) / res.render(...) / res.send(...)   (no centralized error-formatting helper — see Error Handling)
```

### Real example — `GET /admin/agentassist/desk/:title` (fetch a live-agent "desk")
1. `app.js:243` mounts `aclroutes.js`.
2. `routes/aclroutes.js:62` — `router.use('/admin', csrfLoginCheck, require('./admin.js'))`.
3. `routes/admin.js:85` — `router.use(adminLogger)` (writes an `AdminLog` audit record for every admin request).
4. `routes/admin.js:113` — `registerRouteWithPermission(router, '/agentassist', require('./liveAgentConsole'))` (from `routes/permissionWrappers.js`) inserts `hasPermission('agentAssist','view')` before mounting.
5. `routes/liveAgentConsole/index.js:11` — `router.use('/desk', require('./desks'))`.
6. `routes/liveAgentConsole/desks/index.js:18-21` — `router.get('/:title', isUserAdmin, async (req,res) => { ... })`; `isUserAdmin` (`desks/index.js:62-69`) restricts to `Admin`/`Viewer` roles via `@libhlp/agentUtility`.
7. Handler calls `new Desk(req.session).get(req.params.title)` (a `BaseModel`-backed model) and responds `res.json({deskDetails})`.

### Real example — `GET /notify/fetchNotifications`
1. `app.js:240` mounts `naclroutes.js`; `naclroutes.js:98` — `router.use('/notify', require('./pushNotification.js').auth)`.
2. `routes/pushNotification.js:40-47` — `router.get('/fetchNotifications', ...)` builds a range key from `req.session.username`, instantiates `new Notification({}, req.session)` (`models/pushNotification.js`), and returns raw DB docs via `res.send(data)`.

### Socket.IO event path (live agent chat)
```
Client socket connects (query.agent=true from src-agent/) 
  → lib/socket/chat.js: single io.on('connection', ...) handler (app.js:334 wires this in)
       → chat.js:492 detects query.agent and skips end-user chatbot listeners
       → chat.js:523 calls AgentTransferSocketEvents(socket)  (== lib/socket/liveAgentv2.js's init())
            → liveAgentv2.js registers 'Transfer Broker' / 'Agent Broker' / 'Peer Broker' / 'disconnect'
            → each Broker event's payload carries an internal `event` name dispatched via switch
            → handlers use QueueManager / AgentManager / TransferManager (all backed by redisClient)
              and lib/scripts/agentTransfer (desk queueing, transfer orchestration, models/agentAssist/*)
```

## Core Modules

### Dispatchers (`lib/scripts/dispatchers/`)
- **Purpose**: single abstraction point ("service locator") that hides which concrete backend (database, GenAI provider, object storage, key vault, third-party API) answers a call.
- **Key files**: `index.js` (the `dispatcher` class — maps short keys `DB`/`CGS`/`OSS`/`KP`/`TPA`/`CDS` to sub-modules; `.service(name, keys)` instantiates the right handler), `dbServices/index.js` (DB backend selection), `cognitiveServices/index.js` (GenAI backend selection), `objectStorageServices/`, `keyVaultServices/`, `thirdPartyAPIServices/`, `channelDependentServices/`.
- **Important functions/classes**: `dispatcher.prototype.service(serviceName, keys, type)` (`dispatchers/index.js:40-42`); `dbDispatcher` methods `find/findById/update/updateById/insert/destroy/searchByMR/bulk/...` (`dbServices/index.js:13-88`).
- **Dependencies**: `mongodb`, `@ibm-cloud/cloudant`, `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb`.
- **Connects to**: instantiated once as `GLOBAL.Dispatcher` (`app.js:181`); called from almost every model and many `lib/scripts/*` modules.

### Live-agent chat backend (`lib/scripts/agentManager`, `queueManager`, `transferManager`, `agentTransfer`, `liveAgentTransfer`)
- **Purpose**: manage human-agent availability, chat queueing, and transferring a conversation from bot to human agent.
- **Key files/classes**: `agentManager/index.js` (`AgentManager` — Redis-backed online/offline/socket-id/active-chats state), `queueManager/index.js` (`QueueManager` — desk queue counters), `transferManager/index.js` (`TransferManager` — per-transfer Redis state), `agentTransfer/index.js` (the orchestrator: `registerTransfer`, `publishToUser/Agent`, `quitUserFromTransfer`, scheduled transfers), `agentTransfer/activeChatsManager.js` (`ActiveChatsManager`, Redis-Set atomic active-chat tracking), `liveAgentTransfer/index.js` (an older, separate rule-driven live-chat bridge used by bot connectors, not the desk/queue system).
- **Dependencies**: global `redisClient`, `models/agentAssist/*` (Desk, DeskSettings, AgentTransfer, AgentConversations), `@libscr/notifications`, `@lib/scheduler`.
- **Connects to**: instantiated throughout `lib/socket/liveAgentv2.js`; `agentTransfer` calls `GLOBAL.ConnectorBotTriggers.transferAgentMessage` (from `connectorBots`) to reach bot-channel users.

### Bot Framework connectors (`lib/scripts/connectorBots/`)
- **Purpose**: integrate with Microsoft Teams, Slack, Telegram, Facebook, SMS, email, IVR/Twilio, Google Chat via the Microsoft Bot Framework SDK.
- **Key files**: `index.js` (current, `CloudAdapter`-based, builds/caches per-channel connectors, publishes `GLOBAL.ConnectorBotTriggers`), `indexV1.js` (legacy `BotFrameworkAdapter`-based), `botbuilder-redis-storage/` (Redis-backed Bot Framework `Storage` implementation for conversation/user state).
- **Dependencies**: `botbuilder`, `botframework-connector`, global `redisClient`.
- **Connects to**: `routes/connector_bots.js`; `GLOBAL.ConnectorBotTriggers` is called by `agentTransfer`, `notifications`, `chatMessages`.

### A2A protocol (`lib/scripts/a2aServer/`, `lib/scripts/a2aClient/`)
- **Purpose**: expose AEX GenAI agents as Agent-to-Agent (A2A) servers, and let AEX call out to external A2A agents.
- **Key files**: `a2aServer/index.js` (AgentCard building, channel resolution), `a2aServer/executor.js` (`runCGSTurn` — wraps the CGS conversation pipeline in a Promise with a timeout), `a2aServer/taskStore.js` (`ChannelTaskStore`), `a2aServer/contextCache.js` (Redis-backed conversation context, 15-minute TTL), `a2aClient/index.js` (`sendMessage`, `sendMessageStream`, auth-header building for API key/Basic/Bearer/OAuth2).
- **Dependencies**: `@a2a-js/sdk`, `models/externalAgents`, global `redisClient`.
- **Connects to**: `routes/external/a2a.js`, `routes/a2aClient/index.js`, `routes/connector_bots.js`, `lib/scripts/dispatchers/cognitiveServices/openai/externalAgentTool/`.

### GenAI / cognitive services (`lib/scripts/dispatchers/cognitiveServices/openai/`)
- **Purpose**: unify multiple LLM providers behind one interface (the "openai" dispatcher key is used as an umbrella name for all providers).
- **Key files**: `openai.js` (Azure OpenAI), `openaicloud.js` (OpenAI public cloud), `bedrock.js` (AWS Bedrock, Titan/Nova), `vertex.js` (Google Vertex/Gemini), `customllm.js` (customer-configured LLM via a workflow), `gptCaller.js` (unifying caller), `agents.js` (agentic tool-calling loop — this is what actually calls `tools/*`), `guardrail.js`, `callMCP.js` (Model Context Protocol client), `contextManagement/` (planning, sliding-window context, user-preference injection).
- **Dependencies**: `@azure/identity`, `jsonwebtoken` (for GCP service-account JWTs), AWS SigV4 signing (`crypto`).
- **Connects to**: `routes/genAI/*`, `lib/scripts/gptPrompter`, `tools/*` (function-calling), `a2aClient` (external-agent-as-tool).

### GenAI prompting & language utilities (`lib/scripts/gptPrompter`, `interpreters`, `translationAgent`)
- **`gptPrompter/index.js`**: `prompt({...})` — generic one-off LLM question helper with named prompt templates per "console"/use-case (`ucd/`, `ow/`, `translator/`, `functions/`, `pg/`). Called by `routes/genAI/index.js`.
- **`interpreters/slack/index.js`**: converts internal "MCT" markup + Markdown into Slack Block Kit.
- **`translationAgent/index.js`**: dispatch table for translation providers (`watson`, `openwhisk`, `google`, `microsoft`) plus spell-check via a configurable endpoint.

### Workflows, notifications, PWA (`lib/scripts/workflows`, `notifications`, `pwaSubscription`, `chatMessages`)
- **`workflows/index.js`**: `traverseFlow`/`initiateWorkflow` — walks a workflow node graph (`models/workflow`), injects per-node-type credentials (e.g. ServiceNow), integrates with the external scheduler service (`config.SCHEDULER_API`).
- **`notifications/index.js`**: `sendNotifications({channel,...})` — routes to web push (`models/webNotifications`), channel bots (`GLOBAL.ConnectorBotTriggers.proactiveMessage`), or email.
- **`pwaSubscription/index.js`**: Web Push (VAPID) subscription management.
- **`chatMessages/index.js`**: a generic "chat message mode" bridge (separate feature from live-agent transfer), used by `connectorBots`.

### LDAP integration (`lib/scripts/ldapClient`, `lib/scripts/ldapSync`, `middleware/ldapRoleRefresh.js`)
- **`ldapClient/index.js`**: low-level LDAP connectivity (`ldapts`), a **per-tenant connection pool** (size 5) with Redis pub/sub pool-invalidation (`aex:ldap:pool-invalidate`), RFC-4515 filter escaping, configurable search/attribute/lockout policy.
- **`ldapSync/index.js`**: `resolveGroups` maps a user's LDAP group DNs to AEX `AccessGroup` roles; upserts LDAP profile fields; invalidates the Redis role-TTL cache (`aex:role_ttl`).
- **`middleware/ldapRoleRefresh.js`**: applied globally in `naclroutes.js:28`; non-blocking background role refresh keyed off a Redis TTL per user.

### Tool connectors (`tools/`)
- **Purpose**: ~50 pluggable integrations (Slack, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Jira, AWS/Azure/GCP services, databases, webhooks, etc.) that GenAI agents can invoke as function-calling tools.
- **Key files**: `tools/index.js` (`getAllToolFunctions()` flattens every tool's `functions[]` into one registry keyed by function name; `getToolDescription(toolName)`), `tools/example.tools.js` (the template every tool follows).
- **Plugin shape** (every `tools/<name>/index.js`): `{ name, fields: { secrets, config }, functions: [{ name, description, parameters, function }] }`.
- **Invocation path**: `cognitiveServices/openai/agents.js` loads the registry once, presents `functions[].parameters` (OpenAI-function-calling JSON Schema) to the LLM, and on a tool call executes `TOOLS[toolName].function(toolArgs)`.

### Frontend apps (`src/`, `src-agent/`)
- **`src/`** — admin/configuration console (Vue 3 + Pinia + Vue Router, `createWebHashHistory('/admin#')`). Pages: GenAI agent builder, workflows, RBAC, self-heal, learning console, live-agent-console admin views, master config, UI management, channel configuration.
- **`src-agent/`** — live-agent console (`Home.vue`, `Chat.vue`, `LiveDashboard.vue`). Connects to `lib/socket/liveAgentv2.js` via `socket.io-client` with `query: { agent: true }` (`src-agent/helpers/chat/socket-events.js:59`).
- Both call the backend via plain `axios` on **relative, same-origin paths** (no central API client) — a CSRF token from `GET /user_info` is applied globally to `axios.defaults.headers.common['x-aex-ad-client']`.
