items.title: SRD-R1B: GHL Two-Way Commercial Operations + Stitchi CRM Tools
items.body:
# GHL Two-Way Commercial Operations + Stitchi CRM Tools

Parent issues: #126, #124
Related: #128, #131, #140, #145, #214

## Purpose

Deliver the customer requirement that commercial and sales users operate their normal GoHighLevel workflows from Tanaghum instead of repeatedly switching to GHL. GoHighLevel remains the external CRM source of truth; Tanaghum becomes the governed operating surface, approval layer, AI assistant, audit ledger and reporting layer.

The current controlled acceptance proves GHL -> Tanaghum read sync. This sprint adds the missing Tanaghum -> GHL command path and provider reconciliation.

## Current Implementation Truth

- Customer-owned GHL credentials and location are stored in the tenant vault.
- Read-only validation, mapping, preview, sync, idempotent lead mirrors, Event Operations, Historical Assessment and read-only Stitchi summaries are proven for controlled purchase/partial-payment and meeting/no-show scenarios.
- Existing write-back is a narrow, disabled `/contacts/upsert` call for already-linked leads. It does not provide complete CRM operation.
- Tanaghum does not currently create/update opportunities, move stages, create/update appointments, manage payment/ticket fields, send GHL WhatsApp messages, or expose those actions through Stitchi.
- The current private integration token is read-only. Production execution remains blocked until the customer grants and approves exact write scopes.

## Product Outcome

A permitted user can remain in Tanaghum to:

1. Create or update a GHL contact.
2. Add or remove approved GHL tags.
3. Create or update an opportunity.
4. Move an opportunity between approved pipeline stages and statuses.
5. Set total sale value and approved opportunity custom fields for amount paid, payment status, payment date and ticket quantity.
6. Book, reschedule or cancel an appointment.
7. Record Showed/Completed/No Show outcomes.
8. Draft, approve and send an authorized WhatsApp message through the customer GHL provider.
9. See the provider-confirmed result, reconciliation status and audit evidence without raw credentials or unnecessary PII.
10. Ask Stitchi to prepare the same work in natural language; Stitchi must ask for missing critical fields, show a structured preview, require approval and then execute only through governed Tanaghum services.

## Architecture

```text
Hybrid UI / Stitchi
  -> structured command draft
  -> tenant + RBAC + business validation
  -> immutable preview
  -> human approval
  -> idempotent GHL command job
  -> HighLevel API
  -> sanitized provider result
  -> webhook/read-back reconciliation
  -> Tanaghum mirror refresh
  -> audit and user-visible outcome
```

GHL remains CRM source of truth. Tanaghum never silently overwrites provider state and never reports a write as successful until provider confirmation is recorded.

## Backend Scope

### Governed Command API

Add a dedicated `ghl-operations` module with preview/approve/execute/read endpoints for:

- contact upsert
- contact tag add/remove
- opportunity create/update
- opportunity stage/status/value/custom-field update
- appointment create/update/cancel/status
- WhatsApp message send

Every command must include:

- tenant key
- actor user and role
- command type
- target GHL location
- linked Tanaghum lead/event/commercial plan when applicable
- sanitized structured payload
- provider endpoint family
- idempotency key
- preview hash/version
- approval state and approver
- execution state
- provider object IDs
- attempts and timestamps
- sanitized error/result summary
- reconciliation state

### Required State Machine

`draft -> previewed -> pending_approval -> approved -> executing -> provider_accepted -> reconciled`

Terminal/exception states:

- rejected
- cancelled
- blocked
- failed
- reconciliation_failed
- expired

No state may skip required approval. Repeated execute calls with the same idempotency key must not create duplicate contacts, opportunities, appointments or messages.

### HighLevel Adapter

Implement typed client methods for:

- `POST /contacts/upsert`
- contact tag add/remove endpoints
- opportunity create/upsert/update/status endpoints supported by current HighLevel API version
- `POST /calendars/events/appointments`
- `PUT /calendars/events/appointments/:eventId`
- `POST /conversations/messages` for authorized WhatsApp sends
- read-back endpoints required to verify provider state

Use tenant-owned sub-account/private integration credentials only. No global credential fallback.

### Reconciliation

- Add signed/verified GHL webhook ingress where supported.
- Store provider event IDs and deduplicate webhook deliveries.
- Reconcile contact, opportunity, appointment and message outcomes.
- When webhook coverage is unavailable, perform bounded read-back verification.
- Never trust client-supplied provider success.
- Surface stale, pending, failed and drifted states honestly.

## Permissions And Approval

- Read: commercial/sales roles permitted by existing tenant policy.
- Prepare/preview: marketing manager, sales manager, lead qualification manager, department head, CCO, admin according to action type.
- Approve external CRM mutation: CCO, department head or admin by default; customer policy may narrow this.
- Execute: system service only after a valid approved command.
- WhatsApp send requires message approval, consent/DND checks and customer provider readiness.
- No role receives broad provider access merely because it can read GHL data.

## Stitchi Scope

Add governed executable Stitchi actions for:

- prepare GHL contact
- prepare/apply tags
- prepare opportunity
- prepare stage/status/value/payment update
- prepare appointment
- prepare appointment outcome
- prepare WhatsApp follow-up

Stitchi must:

- know tenant/user/role context
- resolve event, commercial plan, lead and GHL mapping context
- ask one concise follow-up when critical data is missing
- never invent provider IDs, pipeline stages, payment amounts, ticket quantities or consent
- show a structured action card with effects and warnings
- require approval
- execute through the same backend command service as the UI
- report provider-confirmed outcome and refresh relevant views
- never expose raw PII in AI prompts beyond the minimum approved context

## Hybrid UI Scope

Provide task-first controls in Sales & Leads / Event Operations:

- Create/update CRM contact
- Create opportunity
- Change stage/status
- Book/update meeting
- Record outcome
- Update payment/ticket evidence
- Draft/approve/send WhatsApp
- Command history and reconciliation status

Use business wording. Hide API endpoints, flags and raw provider data from customer-facing views. Keep advanced connector diagnostics under Settings/Integrations.

## Security And Reliability

- Secrets never returned, logged or placed in command payload records.
- Strict tenant isolation on commands, approvals, provider IDs, webhook events and mirrors.
- Validate all GHL IDs against the tenant location and approved mapping.
- Prevent arbitrary endpoint or field injection.
- Respect GHL DND/consent and WhatsApp template/provider rules.
- Apply retry with bounded exponential backoff only to retry-safe operations.
- Add correlation/request IDs and idempotency keys.
- Encrypt any sensitive command metadata at rest where required.
- Redact provider errors before returning them to clients.

## Tests

### Unit/Contract

- request schemas and allowed field lists
- RBAC and approval boundaries
- state machine
- idempotency and duplicate prevention
- preview hash/version mismatch
- tenant isolation
- provider error sanitization
- contact/opportunity/appointment/message client contracts
- payment/ticket custom-field mapping
- consent/DND/no-send rules
- webhook signature/deduplication
- read-back reconciliation

### Integration

- create contact -> provider accepted -> mirror reconciled
- create opportunity -> stage/value/custom fields -> reconciled
- appointment create -> showed/no-show update -> dashboard refresh
- WhatsApp draft -> approval -> send -> message status reconciliation
- provider timeout/retry/failure paths
- command rejected/expired/cancelled paths
- no raw secrets or unnecessary PII in API, logs, audit or Stitchi prompts

### Browser/E2E

- sales manager prepares a contact/opportunity but cannot self-approve when policy forbids it
- CCO approves and the command executes once
- UI shows provider-confirmed result and refreshed lead/event state
- Stitchi performs the same governed flow
- no hidden 401/403/500 or console errors
- responsive layout at desktop and mobile widths

## Definition Of Done

- All listed CRM command types have preview, approval, execution, audit, idempotency and reconciliation.
- Hybrid users can complete the controlled attended, fully-paid and lost scenarios without opening GHL after initial provider administration.
- Stitchi can prepare and execute those same scenarios after approval.
- GHL remains source of truth and Tanaghum reflects provider-confirmed state.
- WhatsApp send remains blocked unless the customer GHL WhatsApp provider, required write scope, consent policy and execution authorization are present.
- Full backend/frontend test suites, focused GHL contract tests and Playwright customer workflow pass.
- CI is green and deployment evidence is attached.
- Controlled live acceptance is performed with customer-approved write scopes before production write capability is claimed complete.

## Customer Dependencies

The customer must provide/approve:

- a GHL sub-account Private Integration Token with the exact required write scopes
- location, calendar, pipeline, stage, tag and custom-field mappings
- roles allowed to approve each mutation type
- WhatsApp channel/provider readiness, templates and consent rules
- whether Tanaghum may trigger GHL workflows or send messages directly

These dependencies do not block implementing and testing the production adapter with contract fixtures; they block only live write acceptance.

## Non-Goals

- Replacing GHL as CRM source of truth
- Exposing full GHL administration in Tanaghum
- Creating customer pipelines/calendars/phone providers without explicit scope
- Autonomous external writes without approval
- Storing provider credentials outside the tenant vault

items.title: Performance, Stability, & Horizontal Scaling Review
items.body:
# Performance, Stability, & Horizontal Scaling Review

## Background & Motivation
As CircuitBreaker expands to support multiple teams and a vast array of hardware/software integrations, the architecture must transition from a "snappy single-server" model to a horizontally scalable foundation. This review analyzes the current state of Multi-Tenancy, Error Handling, Telemetry Data Ingestion, and Integration Extensibility to identify architectural bottlenecks and propose paths for horizontal expansion.

## 1. Multi-Tenancy (Team Support)
### Current State
- The application implements multi-tenancy at the database level using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS). A `TenantMiddleware` extracts the tenant ID from the session/JWT and sets a Postgres configuration variable (`app.current_tenant`) for every request.
### Bottlenecks & Risks
- **Noisy Neighbors & Connection Limits:** While RLS provides strong logical isolation, all tenants share the same physical database compute, memory, and connection pool. A heavy analytical query from one team will degrade performance for others.
- **Index Bloat:** As data grows, shared B-Tree indexes become massive and less efficient to update.
### Horizontal Scaling Path
- **Near-term:** Implement a robust connection pooler (like PgBouncer, which is already present in docker but must be tuned for multi-tenant workloads) and implement per-tenant API rate limiting to prevent "noisy neighbor" abuse.
- **Long-term (Enterprise Scale):** Transition from a single shared-schema RLS model to a **Database-per-Tenant** or **Sharded** architecture (e.g., using Citus). This allows true horizontal scaling where tenant databases can be physically distributed across different database clusters.

## 2. Telemetry Ingestion & Long-Term Uptime Data
### Current State
- High-frequency telemetry is ingested into standard relational PostgreSQL tables (`HardwareLiveMetric`, `TelemetryTimeseries`) with standard B-Tree indexes.
- To prevent database collapse, a cleanup worker (`purge_old_hardware_live_metrics`) deletes raw telemetry data older than 7 days. Uptime is aggregated daily by `rollup_worker.py`.
### Bottlenecks & Risks
- **Write Thrashing:** Standard Postgres tables are not optimized for massive, constant append-only time-series data. Writing millions of rows will cause severe table bloat, heavy WAL generation, and disk I/O bottlenecks.
- **Data Loss:** Users cannot currently view long-term historical telemetry because it is actively destroyed to protect database stability.
### Horizontal Scaling Path
- **TimescaleDB Migration:** Convert the `hardware_live_metrics` and `telemetry_timeseries` tables into **TimescaleDB hypertables**. This allows you to keep PostgreSQL as your primary datastore while gaining automatic time-based partitioning, columnar compression (up to 90% disk space savings), and hyper-fast continuous aggregations.
- **Message Queue Buffering:** The current `poll_hardware` worker publishes directly to Redis. For massive scale, telemetry payloads should be buffered through the existing **NATS JetStream** message bus before being batch-inserted into TimescaleDB.

## 3. Integrations Architecture
### Current State
- Integrations are tightly coupled to the monolithic backend. The `app/integrations/dispatcher.py` file uses a hardcoded `PROFILE_MAP` dictionary (e.g., `"idrac9": IDRACClient`, `"ilo6": ILOClient`).
### Bottlenecks & Risks
- **Monolithic Deployment:** Adding a new hardware or software integration requires modifying core application code, rebuilding, and deploying the entire monolith.
- **Dependency Hell:** As more complex integrations are added, their specific Python dependencies (e.g., heavy SDKs) will bloat the main application container.
### Horizontal Scaling Path
- **Dynamic Plugin Registry:** Refactor the dispatcher to use Python's `entry_points` or a dynamic module loader so integrations can self-register without hardcoded maps.
- **Sidecar / Microservice Integrations:** Decouple integrations entirely. Move them into lightweight, isolated containers that communicate with the main CircuitBreaker core over **NATS**. The core simply broadcasts "Poll Hardware X", and the specific integration microservice picks up the job, executes it, and replies with the normalized JSON payload.

## 4. Stability & Error Handling
### Current State
- The API layer handles exceptions well via centralized handlers (`app_error_handler`, etc.) in `main.py`.
- Background workers (`telemetry_collector.py`, `discovery.py`, `webhook_worker.py`) rely on localized `try/except` blocks that print to standard Python `logger.warning` or `logger.error`.
### Bottlenecks & Risks
- **Silent Failures:** Worker errors buried in text logs are difficult to track across a distributed multi-node deployment, leading to silent integration failures or missed telemetry.
### Horizontal Scaling Path
- **Centralized APM:** Integrate an Application Performance Monitoring (APM) and error tracking tool (e.g., Sentry, OpenTelemetry). Wrap worker execution loops in APM transaction contexts to automatically capture stack traces, local variables, and execution duration.
- **Dead Letter Queues (DLQ):** Implement DLQs in NATS for failed webhook deliveries or telemetry parsing errors, allowing administrators to inspect and replay failed events.

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Spec completo, listo para que un agente lo implemente

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Una instalación de Wacrm solo puede representar una configuración de WhatsApp por Account y todavía no puede convertir de forma segura los webhooks globales de una Meta App en mensajes y estados aislados por tenant. El ingreso actual valida firmas y conserva el cuerpo recibido, pero no resuelve `phone_number_id`, no deduplica eventos, marca la entrega como procesada antes de procesarla y limita el cuerpo por debajo de los 3 MB admitidos por Meta.

Como resultado, una empresa no puede usar números separados para ventas, soporte o sucursales sin mezclar conversaciones, escoger accidentalmente un remitente incorrecto o arriesgar efectos duplicados cuando Meta reintenta una entrega. La pantalla de configuración tampoco ofrece un proceso persistente y verificable que lleve al administrador desde credenciales hasta una recepción real.

## Solution

Wacrm ofrecerá un MVP de integración directa donde cada instalación opera su propia Meta App y un endpoint global de webhooks. Cada Account tendrá una WhatsApp Integration capaz de agrupar varios WABA y WhatsApp Phone Number Connections. Las entregas se autenticarán y persistirán antes del acuse; después, una cola las dividirá en eventos idempotentes, resolverá el tenant mediante `phone_number_id` y aplicará mensajes o estados sin cruzar Accounts.

Un asistente guiado permitirá a Owner y Admin validar credenciales, suscribir WABA, registrar números, conservar avances parciales y comprobar una entrega real antes de declarar una conexión Active. La operación del MVP incluirá reintentos internos, inspección y replay por Artisan, retención limitada del cuerpo crudo y estados comprensibles, sin exigir Embedded Signup, mTLS ni un dashboard especializado.

## User Stories

1. As an Instance Operator, I want to configure one Meta App for my Wacrm installation, so that every tenant can use a common, maintainable webhook endpoint.
2. As an Instance Operator, I want the Meta App Secret to remain outside tenant-facing screens, so that Account administrators cannot access an installation-wide secret.
3. As an Instance Operator, I want a verify token and callback URL that I can copy into Meta, so that I can complete endpoint verification without editing application code.
4. As an Instance Operator, I want webhook signatures to be mandatory, so that forged requests cannot create messages or alter delivery statuses.
5. As an Instance Operator, I want Wacrm to accept Meta's documented payload size, so that legitimate deliveries up to 3 MB are not rejected.
6. As an Instance Operator, I want a temporary persistence failure to return a retryable response, so that Meta can redeliver data Wacrm could not durably record.
7. As an Instance Operator, I want valid persisted deliveries acknowledged quickly, so that internal processing latency does not trigger external duplicates.
8. As an Instance Operator, I want invalid signatures rejected without persistence, so that unauthenticated payloads do not enter the processing pipeline.
9. As an Instance Operator, I want raw webhook deliveries retained for a bounded period, so that I can diagnose and replay problems without retaining sensitive payloads indefinitely.
10. As an Instance Operator, I want structured logs without secrets, so that operational diagnostics do not expose access tokens or App Secret material.
11. As an Instance Operator, I want to list failed and unresolved events from Artisan, so that the MVP remains operable without a dedicated webhook dashboard.
12. As an Instance Operator, I want to replay selected events safely, so that corrected configuration or transient failures can be recovered without duplicating CRM effects.
13. As an Instance Operator, I want unsupported event types recorded separately from failures, so that future Meta fields do not generate misleading incidents.
14. As an Account Owner, I want to connect multiple WhatsApp numbers, so that sales, support and branches can operate independently in one Account.
15. As an Account Admin, I want to connect numbers from more than one WABA, so that my organization is not constrained to a single Meta container.
16. As an Account Admin, I want Wacrm to verify that a number belongs to the declared WABA, so that incorrect identifiers are caught during setup.
17. As an Account Admin, I want Wacrm to validate the access token and required permissions, so that I receive an actionable error before relying on the integration.
18. As an Account Admin, I want Wacrm to subscribe the Meta App to the WABA, so that I do not have to execute Graph API requests manually.
19. As an Account Admin, I want Wacrm to register a phone number when required, so that inbound events can start flowing.
20. As an Account Admin, I want partial setup progress preserved, so that a failed subscription or registration can be retried without re-entering all credentials.
21. As an Account Admin, I want setup retries to be idempotent, so that pressing retry cannot create duplicate subscriptions or connections.
22. As an Account Admin, I want distinct connection readiness states, so that valid credentials are not confused with a working webhook.
23. As an Account Admin, I want a guided real-message test, so that a connection becomes Active only after Wacrm receives and routes an event for that number.
24. As an Account Admin, I want to replace an access token without seeing the stored token, so that credential rotation is possible without disclosing secrets.
25. As an Account Admin, I want to designate at most one active default connection, so that initiating a conversation can be convenient but deterministic.
26. As an Account Admin, I want the first connection proposed as default with an explicit confirmation, so that setup is convenient without making a silent sender choice.
27. As an Account Admin, I want a number already claimed by another Account to be rejected without revealing the other tenant, so that tenant privacy is maintained.
28. As an Account Admin, I want to disconnect one number without deleting its CRM history, so that temporary or permanent channel changes do not erase customer records.
29. As an Account Admin, I want disconnecting one number to leave its WABA subscribed while other numbers still use it, so that sibling connections keep receiving events.
30. As an Account Admin, I want disconnecting the default number to clear the default rather than silently choosing another, so that outbound messages never switch senders unexpectedly.
31. As an Account Admin, I want connection health and the latest actionable failure visible in Settings, so that common problems can be resolved without server access.
32. As an Account Member, I want to view connection status without being able to change credentials, so that I understand channel availability without receiving administrative privileges.
33. As an Account Viewer, I want tenant-safe status visibility without raw webhook payloads, so that monitoring cannot expose global or cross-tenant data.
34. As an agent replying to a conversation, I want the reply to use the connection that received the conversation, so that the customer sees the expected business number.
35. As an agent initiating a conversation, I want to choose a sender when no default exists, so that Wacrm never uses an arbitrary number.
36. As an automation author, I want an inbound automation to support “same connection as trigger”, so that automated replies remain on the original channel.
37. As an automation author, I want outbound automations to pin an explicit connection, so that later default changes cannot alter their sender.
38. As a broadcast author, I want every broadcast to pin an active connection, so that all recipients receive messages from the intended number.
39. As a broadcast author, I want execution paused when its connection is disconnected, so that Wacrm does not fall back to another number.
40. As a CRM user, I want one Contact per `wa_id` within my Account, so that the same customer is not duplicated when contacting multiple business numbers.
41. As a CRM user, I want separate conversations for the same Contact on sales and support numbers, so that assignments, unread counts, AI behavior and histories do not mix.
42. As a CRM user, I want inbound messages deduplicated by Meta message ID, so that webhook retries cannot create duplicate timeline entries.
43. As a CRM user, I want outgoing status transitions applied monotonically, so that a late `sent` event cannot regress a message already marked `delivered` or `read`.
44. As a CRM user, I want statuses for unknown messages retained without creating fictional messages, so that later synchronization or replay can correlate them safely.
45. As an Account Admin, I want events for disconnected connections preserved but blocked, so that reconnecting can recover them without mutating the CRM while the channel is disabled.
46. As an Account Admin, I want events for an unknown `phone_number_id` preserved as unresolved, so that completing the missing connection can recover them.
47. As an Account Owner, I want deleting the Account to disable routing and remove encrypted tokens, so that deleted tenants cannot continue sending or processing WhatsApp traffic.
48. As an Account Owner, I want number transfer to require an explicit disconnect and reconnect, so that historical CRM data is never silently moved between tenants.

## Implementation Decisions

- The design follows ADR 0008 and uses the domain vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`: Meta App, WhatsApp Integration, WABA Subscription, WhatsApp Phone Number Connection, Webhook Delivery and Webhook Event.
- The MVP is for direct installations. One Wacrm installation owns one Meta App and one global callback. The design must not assume Solution Partner onboarding.
- Installation-wide App Secret and verify token remain configuration owned by the Instance Operator. They are not tenant records and are never exposed through tenant-facing props or responses.
- Each Account has one WhatsApp Integration containing its encrypted operational access token and connection health. The plaintext token is accepted only on creation or replacement and is never returned.
- An Account may own multiple WABA Subscriptions. Within one installation, a WABA belongs to exactly one Account.
- A WABA Subscription may own multiple WhatsApp Phone Number Connections. `phone_number_id` is globally unique across the installation.
- A normal connection attempt must not take over an existing `phone_number_id`. The conflict response must not disclose the owning Account. Administrative recovery is reserved for the Instance Operator.
- At most one active connection per Account may be the Default WhatsApp Phone Number Connection. Removing or disabling it clears the default without assigning a replacement.
- Connection readiness is represented explicitly as Credentials Verified, Subscribed, Webhook Waiting, Active, Attention Required or Disconnected. Partial setup is durable and resumable.
- The guided setup validates token usability and both required permission families, verifies WABA/number ownership, subscribes the Meta App to the WABA, registers the number when required and waits for an actual routed event before marking Active.
- Repeating a completed or partially completed setup step is idempotent. A failure preserves previous successful steps and an actionable, sanitized error.
- Owner and Admin may create, update, retry and disconnect integrations and connections. Member and Viewer may only receive tenant-safe read projections permitted by the existing Account policy.
- Disconnecting a phone connection disables outbound use and blocks inbound operational effects while preserving historical data. It does not unsubscribe a WABA with remaining connections.
- Deleting an entire integration removes encrypted token material and disables its connections. Account deletion must disable routing immediately and then follow the application's retention/deletion policy.
- The webhook verification GET validates `hub.mode`, verify token and challenge and returns the challenge as plain text on success.
- The webhook POST reads and signs the exact raw bytes. It never verifies a re-encoded JSON representation.
- The effective payload limit is 3 MB and is enforced against actual body bytes in both application and deployment guidance. `Content-Length` may be used for early rejection but is not trusted as the only check.
- Invalid or missing HMAC returns `401` and creates no Delivery. A body over 3 MB returns `413`. A temporary failure to persist returns `503`. Once a valid delivery is durable, the endpoint returns `200` even when its content is malformed, unsupported, unresolved or later fails internally.
- A rigid per-IP throttle must not be the availability boundary for authenticated Meta traffic. Abuse protection uses the body limit, HMAC, short request timeout, infrastructure controls and observability of invalid signatures; any emergency request limit must be generous enough not to reject shared Meta infrastructure.
- A Webhook Delivery is installation-level and may contain events for multiple tenants. It stores the exact raw body, signature metadata, receive time, processing state and sanitized diagnostics, but does not receive an Account global scope.
- Raw JSON decoding is deferred until after signature verification. A valid signed body that cannot be decoded is retained and classified rather than discarded into Meta's seven-day retry loop.
- Delivery ingestion performs only authentication, durable persistence and after-commit queue dispatch before returning `200`.
- Processing splits every supported entry/change/item into independently classifiable Webhook Events. Events reference their Delivery and carry a deterministic identity/fingerprint sufficient for idempotency.
- Event routing resolves `metadata.phone_number_id` without relying on a pre-bound tenant, then binds the owning Account before any tenant-scoped model access.
- An unknown number produces an Unresolved Webhook Event. A known disconnected number produces a Blocked Webhook Event. An unimplemented field produces an Unsupported Webhook Event. None is retried as an internal technical failure.
- A supported event that exhausts transient retries becomes a Failed Webhook Event and remains replayable. A message status whose message is absent becomes an Uncorrelated Message Status and remains available for later correlation.
- Inbound messages use Meta's message ID as their idempotency key. Status updates use the message ID plus their stable transition identity. Other event types use official identifiers when available and otherwise a deterministic normalized fingerprint.
- Duplicate Deliveries may be retained as separate delivery attempts, but the same Event can modify CRM state only once.
- Events for different conversations may process concurrently. Events for the same conversation are serialized or protected by equivalent concurrency control.
- Outgoing status changes are monotonic and resilient to out-of-order delivery. Older or lower-rank statuses cannot regress terminal or later states.
- A Contact is unique by Account and canonical `wa_id`. Manually entered numbers are normalized before matching; ambiguous candidates are never auto-merged.
- A Conversation belongs to an Account, Contact and WhatsApp Phone Number Connection. Its uniqueness includes the connection, allowing one Contact to have separate sales and support threads.
- Replies always inherit the Conversation connection. New conversations require an explicit connection unless an active default exists.
- Broadcasts pin a connection at creation. Outbound automations pin a connection; inbound-triggered automations may explicitly use the trigger's connection. A disabled connection pauses execution rather than selecting another.
- Message records must be traceable to the sending/receiving connection directly or immutably through their Conversation.
- Delivery processing starts as received, becomes queued, and is marked processed only when every extracted Event has a classified outcome. A delivery with exhausted event failures is distinguishable from a fully successful one. `processed_at` is never set during ingress.
- Raw Delivery bodies are retained for 30 days. Pending unresolved or failed work must not be pruned before resolution. Operational Contacts, Conversations and Messages follow normal CRM retention. A compact idempotency record is retained at least beyond Meta's seven-day retry window, with 30 days as the MVP baseline.
- Raw global Deliveries are not exposed in tenant UI or tenant API responses. Tenant users see only normalized records and connection/event health belonging to their Account. Instance Operator diagnostics must minimize or mask personal data where practical.
- Artisan operations support listing failed/unresolved work and replaying selected work. Replay uses the same idempotent processor and cannot duplicate an already applied effect.
- Structured logs include delivery/event identifiers, processing state and tenant identifier only after routing. They exclude access tokens, App Secret, full authorization headers and unnecessary raw message content.
- The existing single-row WhatsApp configuration must migrate non-destructively into Integration, WABA Subscription and Phone Number Connection records. Existing conversations can be assigned automatically only where a unique legacy connection is known; ambiguous rows must be reported for explicit remediation instead of silently assigned.
- The current uniqueness of Conversation by Account and Contact is replaced with uniqueness that also includes the connection.
- Database constraints must enforce tenant ownership and cross-record consistency wherever practical, including unique WABA ownership, unique `phone_number_id`, one default per Account and connection-aware conversation identity.
- The active Settings experience must persist through authenticated backend boundaries and generated route helpers; the archived application remains reference-only.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests observe behavior at the highest public seam and each behavior is asserted once, following ADR 0004. Internal class structure, private helpers and queue implementation details are not test contracts.
- The primary seam is the public webhook HTTP endpoint using the test environment's synchronous queue execution. It covers verification, exact-body HMAC, actual 3 MB limit, response semantics, durable Delivery creation, event extraction, tenant routing, idempotency, disconnected/unknown/unsupported outcomes and resulting CRM records.
- The webhook Feature suite extends the existing Meta webhook tests rather than creating a parallel low-level suite. It uses signed payload fixtures representing multiple entries, multiple Accounts, duplicate deliveries, malformed signed bodies, inbound messages and out-of-order statuses.
- Tenant isolation is asserted through observable webhook results: a `phone_number_id` may affect only its owning Account, global Deliveries cannot leak through tenant projections and cross-Account WABA/number claims are rejected. Reusable model-level tenant assertions remain supplemental for new tenant-scoped records.
- The authenticated Settings HTTP seam uses a fake Meta Graph boundary. It covers authorization, token redaction/encryption behavior, permission validation, resumable partial setup, WABA subscription reuse, registration, uniqueness conflicts, default selection, token rotation, disconnect and health projections.
- Meta Graph tests assert requests and externally meaningful outcomes, not the internal HTTP client implementation. Error fixtures include invalid credentials, missing permissions, WABA/number mismatch, already-subscribed success and transient Meta failures.
- The Artisan Feature seam covers listing and replaying Failed, Unresolved, Blocked and Uncorrelated work. It proves replay is idempotent and becomes effective after correcting the relevant configuration.
- One Browser test covers the critical user journey from Settings: an Owner/Admin enters credentials, progresses through explicit setup states, sends the instructed real/test message represented by the controlled test backend, observes the detected Contact/message and sees Active. It also verifies that the token is no longer displayed.
- Browser tests do not duplicate Graph error matrices, webhook signature cases, event state transitions or policy permutations already proven at Feature seams.
- Existing Account policy prior art is used for role behavior. Existing tenant-isolation helpers are extended for new tenant-scoped models. Existing Meta webhook Feature tests provide the baseline for route and signature behavior.
- Migration verification covers preserving a legacy single-number configuration and conversation assignment when unambiguous, plus a safe failure/report when historical rows cannot be mapped.
- Retention tests prove ordinary old raw Deliveries are pruned while unresolved/failed work remains. Logs and serialized responses are checked for secret leakage at their public boundaries.
- The verification gate is the repository's normal fast test gate plus the focused Browser gate; no new independent test suite is introduced.

## Out of Scope

- Embedded Signup.
- Operating Wacrm as a Meta Solution Partner or Tech Provider.
- Advanced Access/App Review automation for onboarding third-party businesses.
- Per-customer or per-number webhook overrides.
- mTLS configuration.
- Static Meta IP allowlists.
- A full webhook Delivery/dead-letter dashboard.
- Functional processing of webhook fields other than `messages`; such fields are retained as Unsupported.
- WhatsApp Business App history synchronization.
- Automatic transfer of Contacts, Conversations or Messages between Accounts when moving a number.
- Automatic sender fallback when a connection is disconnected or unhealthy.
- Automatic Contact merges based on ambiguous phone representations.
- Tenant access to raw global Delivery payloads.
- Database-per-tenant architecture, a third-party tenancy package or PostgreSQL RLS.
- Changing the project into a hosted multi-customer Solution Partner platform.

## Further Notes

- This specification implements the accepted decisions in ADR 0008 and uses the domain definitions in `CONTEXT.md`.
- Meta's documented contract allows webhook payloads up to 3 MB and retries non-`200` deliveries for up to seven days, potentially producing duplicates.
- Meta's `messages` webhook carries the receiving `phone_number_id` in `metadata`, making a single callback with tenant routing the simplest MVP topology.
- Subscribing the Meta App is a WABA-level operation; number registration and runtime connection state remain number-level concerns.
- The current code already provides useful prior art for GET verification, HMAC validation, exact raw-body persistence and webhook Feature tests. Delivery/event processing, tenant routing, multinumber schema and persistent onboarding are the principal missing capabilities.
- Before implementation is handed to agents, this specification should be decomposed into independently deliverable tracer-bullet tickets with explicit dependency edges.

items.title: RFC: Datalevin as Talon's fact store and query engine
items.body:
## Context

Talon rules need to reason over live inventory data (items, tickets, activities, stock levels). The original spec says "compiles to Prolog" but Prolog's built-in database is RAM-only — facts disappear on restart, there's no clustering, and no real persistence. We explored building our own storage layer (WAL, snapshots, LMDB) but that's reinventing a database.

**Datalevin** is an open-source Datalog database that already solves this: persistent storage (LMDB), Raft consensus clustering, RBAC, and native Datalog queries. Instead of building a storage layer around a Prolog engine, we use a database that speaks Datalog natively.

## Why Datalevin

| Requirement | Datalevin | Prolog + custom storage |
|---|---|---|
| Fact persistence | LMDB, crash-safe, zero-config | We'd build WAL/snapshots ourselves |
| Restart recovery | Reopen LMDB file, instant | Replay WAL or reload from MCP (slow) |
| Clustering / HA | Built-in Raft consensus | We'd build replication ourselves |
| Per-tenant isolation | RBAC built in | We'd manage separate engine instances |
| Datalog queries | Native, optimized, cost-based | Prolog can do it but with runtime footguns |
| Recursion (tree walking) | Native recursive rules | Yes (Prolog's strength too) |
| Negation | Stratified, safe | Prolog's negation-as-failure (trickier) |
| Guaranteed termination | Yes (Datalog property) | No (Prolog can infinite loop) |
| Aggregation (avg, count) | Built-in | Libraries, manual findall |
| Full-text search | Built in | No |
| Vector search | Built in | No |

Additional Datalevin features relevant to Talon:
- **Datomic-style Datalog** — the most mature Datalog dialect, large community
- **Transaction log** — every fact change is recorded, enabling time-travel queries ("what was true last week?")
- **Schema-flexible** — accepts documents with nested data, no rigid table definitions
- **Client/server mode** — TCP port 8898, any language can connect
- **Java, Python, Node.js bindings** — Go would talk via TCP client protocol

## Why Datalog over Prolog

See also: [Wikipedia: Datalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datalog)

Datalog is a subset of Prolog designed specifically for databases. It keeps what matters for Talon (unification, recursion, negation, backward reasoning) and drops what hurts (infinite loops, side effects, cut). Key differences:

| | Prolog | Datalog |
|---|---|---|
| Designed for | General logic programming | Database queries |
| Termination | Not guaranteed | **Always terminates** |
| Side effects | assert/retract mutate state | Pure queries, explicit transactions |
| Storage | RAM only | **Persistent by design** |
| Recursion | Yes (but can loop) | Yes (safe, guaranteed to finish) |
| Negation | Negation-as-failure (subtle) | Stratified negation (well-defined) |
| Aggregation | Manual (findall + compute) | Built-in (count, avg, sum, min, max) |

Talon's `detect`, `rule`, and `recommend` blocks map naturally to Datalog. The `combine` block (optimization) would still need a constraint solver on top.

## Architecture

\`\`\`
OpenTalon pod:
  ├── opentalon (Go)           ← existing, unchanged
  ├── weaviate-plugin (Go)     ← existing, unchanged
  ├── mcp-plugin (Go)          ← existing, unchanged
  └── talon-plugin (Go)        ← NEW
      └── connects to Datalevin via TCP

Datalevin (sidecar or separate pod):
  └── JVM process
      ├── LMDB on PVC (persistent volume)
      ├── Raft for HA (multi-node)
      ├── RBAC (per-tenant isolation)
      └── TCP :8898
\`\`\`

## Data flow

### 1. Facts enter Datalevin from MCP tool results

\`\`\`
User asks "show me my items"
  → LLM calls timly.list-items via MCP
  → MCP returns structured JSON (items, pagination)
  → talon-plugin transacts facts into Datalevin:

    [:db/add item-501 :record/type :item]
    [:db/add item-501 :record/category "Vehicles"]
    [:db/add item-501 :record/status :active]
    [:db/add item-501 :attr/km 45000]
    [:db/add item-501 :attr/last-service-km 20000]
    [:db/add item-501 :attr/name "VW Transporter"]
\`\`\`

Every MCP tool result enriches the fact base. Over time, Datalevin accumulates a complete picture of the tenant's inventory.

### 2. Talon rules compile to Datalevin Datalog queries

\`\`\`talon
detect "Service overdue" {
  for records where type == "item"
    and category in category_tree("Vehicles")
    and attr "km" > attr "last_service_km" + 20000
    and status == "active"
  flag matching items
  priority HIGH
}
\`\`\`

Compiles to Datalevin Datalog:

\`\`\`clojure
[:find ?item ?name ?km ?gap
 :where
 [?item :record/type :item]
 [?item :record/status :active]
 [?item :record/category ?cat]
 [?item :attr/name ?name]
 [?item :attr/km ?km]
 [?item :attr/last-service-km ?last-km]
 [(ancestor ?cat "Vehicles")]       ;; recursive rule
 [(- ?km ?last-km) ?gap]
 [(> ?gap 20000)]]
\`\`\`

### 3. Learned thresholds live in Datalevin too

\`\`\`clojure
;; "What's the average service interval for this tenant?"
;; Not a hardcoded 20,000 — computed from their actual ticket history.

[:find (avg ?gap) .
 :where
 [?ticket :ticket/status :done]
 [?ticket :ticket/item ?item]
 [?ticket :attr/km-at-service ?km]
 [?ticket :attr/prev-service-km ?prev-km]
 [(- ?km ?prev-km) ?gap]]
\`\`\`

This query runs over persisted facts. No separate "learning database" needed — the same Datalevin instance holds both live facts and historical data for threshold computation.

### 4. Feedback stored as facts

\`\`\`clojure
;; User confirmed a detection
[:db/add feedback-1 :feedback/rule "service-overdue"]
[:db/add feedback-1 :feedback/reaction :confirmed]
[:db/add feedback-1 :feedback/timestamp #inst "2025-05-06"]

;; Query confidence
[:find (avg ?score) .
 :where
 [?f :feedback/rule "service-overdue"]
 [?f :feedback/reaction ?r]
 [(if (= ?r :confirmed) 1.0 0.0) ?score]]
\`\`\`

### 5. Time-travel for pattern discovery

Datalevin records every transaction. This enables:

\`\`\`clojure
;; "What items were active 90 days ago but are now defective?"
;; Query the database AS OF 90 days ago vs now.
;; No separate history table needed — Datalevin is immutable.

[:find ?item ?name
 :where
 [?item :record/status :active :as-of 90-days-ago]
 [?item :record/status :defective :as-of :now]
 [?item :attr/name ?name]]
\`\`\`

This is exactly what pattern discovery needs: comparing past state to current state to find degradation patterns.

## Restart and persistence

| Scenario | What happens |
|---|---|
| Pod restart | Datalevin reopens LMDB file. All facts intact. Instant. |
| Pod migration | PVC follows the pod (Kubernetes). No data loss. |
| Node failure (with Raft) | Other Raft nodes have the data. New pod syncs from cluster. |
| Datalevin process crash | LMDB is crash-safe (memory-mapped, copy-on-write). No corruption. |
| Cold start (new tenant) | First MCP tool results transact facts into empty database. |
| Data freshness | Background sync job periodically re-fetches from MCP and updates Datalevin. |

No WAL hacks. No snapshot management. No "reload from MCP on restart." Datalevin is a real database.

## The Talon compilation pipeline (updated)

\`\`\`
.talon source
  → Lexer → Parser → AST → Validator
  → Datalevin Datalog emitter (not Prolog)
  → Datalevin query execution
  → Results back to talon-plugin
  → Surfaced as detections, recommendations, policy blocks
\`\`\`

The spec says "compiles to Prolog" — this RFC proposes changing the target to **Datalevin Datalog**. The language syntax stays the same. Only the backend changes.

## What stays from the Prolog design

- Backward reasoning (Datalog does this)
- Recursive rules (Datalog does this, safely)
- Negation (Datalog does this, with stratification)
- Unification-based pattern matching (Datalog does this)
- The `.talon` surface syntax (unchanged)

## What improves

- **Persistence is native** — facts survive restarts, no custom code
- **Clustering is built in** — Raft consensus, HA out of the box
- **Termination is guaranteed** — no infinite loops, ever
- **Aggregation is built in** — avg, count, sum, min, max in queries
- **Time-travel** — query historical state for pattern discovery
- **Full-text + vector search** — already in Datalevin, bonus features

## What we lose

- **Prolog's full generality** — Datalog is a subset, can't do everything Prolog can
- **The `combine` block** — constraint satisfaction / optimization needs something on top of Datalog (but this was true for Prolog too — `findall + sort` is not a real optimizer)
- **Go-native embedding** — Datalevin is JVM, requires a sidecar process

## Open questions

1. **Go ↔ Datalevin protocol.** Datalevin has a TCP client/server mode. We need a Go client library. Options: implement the wire protocol, use gRPC adapter, or HTTP bridge.
2. **Per-tenant isolation in Datalevin.** Options: separate LMDB files per tenant (cleanest isolation), or shared database with entity_id attribute on every fact (simpler ops, use RBAC for access control).
3. **Fact schema.** Datalevin is schema-flexible but benefits from schema declarations. We need a standard schema for Timly facts (record, attr, activity, ticket, person, container).
4. **Sync frequency.** How often do we re-fetch facts from MCP to keep Datalevin current? On every user request? Every 5 minutes? Event-driven via webhooks from Rails?
5. **The `combine` block.** Constraint satisfaction is not Datalog's strength. Options: compile `combine` to a different engine (Z3, OR-tools), or express it as ranked Datalog queries with aggregation.

## References

- [Datalevin GitHub](https://github.com/datalevin/datalevin)
- [Datalog (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datalog)
- [Talon Spec v0.1](https://github.com/opentalon/talon-language/issues/1)
- [RFC: Talon for MCP Tool Calling](https://github.com/opentalon/talon-language/issues/2)
- [RFC: Learning from Data](https://github.com/opentalon/talon-language/issues/3)
- [SWI-Prolog Database Docs](https://www.swi-prolog.org/pldoc/man?section=db)

items.title: RFC: Enterprise index storage — three orthogonal axes (version / snapshot / tenancy), git-content-addressed graph

labels.name: scope/graph
labels.description: Code graph, igraph, ROI subgraph, SCIP decode

items.body:
## Summary

Reframes enterprise index storage around **three orthogonal problems** that were previously conflated, and proposes mirroring git's content-addressed model rather than inventing our own versioning:

1. **Multi-version** — as-of-commit graph queries as a repo evolves across commits/branches.
2. **Snapshot isolation** — one query sees a consistent view of a version, not a half-mutated graph racing a concurrent indexer.
3. **Multi-tenancy** — isolation between users/tenants. **Decided (this RFC): single-org self-hosted, weak isolation** (one deployment ≈ one tenant; row-level filtering; `tenant_id` reserved nullable for a future SaaS RFC).

**Central finding (the pivot):** cross-file reference edges are today *materialized at index time into a single mutable igraph, and eagerly cross-coupled* — an incremental patch to file F re-runs LSP `references()` to rebuild inbound edges living in *other, unchanged* files. This single fact is what breaks both axis 1 (clean per-file dedup) and axis 2 (free MVCC). The highest-leverage move is therefore **not** building version storage first, but **de-materializing cross-file edges**: keep SCIP monikers unresolved per-blob and resolve them lazily at query time + a hot-edge cache. SCIP/LSP already emit the monikers; today's code eagerly resolves and discards them.

## Motivation

The three axes have different solutions and different cost centers; bundling them produced a muddy design (see the prior revision of this issue). Separating them:

**Axis 1 — multi-version.** A code graph's defining property is that *most files are unchanged between commits*, and git is already a content-addressed version system. Mirror it:

- **Content-address per-file symbol subgraphs by file blob hash.** SCIP/LSP produce symbols per-document, so store `file_content_hash → that file's symbol subgraph`. Two commits that don't touch file F share F's subgraph automatically. Storage is `O(unique file versions)`, not `O(commits × repo size)`.
- **A "version" degenerates to a manifest:** `(repo, commit) → {file_blob_hash...}` — literally a mirror of git's tree. Snapshotting a new version = writing one manifest, O(1), copies no graph data. The graph as-of a commit = the union of those blob subgraphs.
- **Incremental indexing:** a new commit only re-runs SCIP/LSP on *changed* files; everything else reuses its blob hash. This reuse is the precondition for the whole scheme.

So a "snapshot" is not a thing to materialize — it's a logical view of `(commit manifest + version predicate)`.

**Axis 2 — snapshot isolation, basically free *if* the base is immutable.** Store edges in an append-only/immutable table keyed by blob hash; a reader pins `(commit, overlay)` and filters `blob_hash ∈ manifest`. A concurrent indexer writes *new* blobs/manifest rows and never touches the rows an old reader sees — that's MVCC, no hand-rolled locks. (This is a concrete instance of the temporal-ordering / fixed-logical-timepoint idea from MemConsist.)

**The catch — cross-file edges.** Per-file dedup is clean for intra-file edges. But call-graph / cross-file references belong to *no single blob*. This is the one genuinely expensive part — and today it is implemented in the worst possible form for versioning:

- Cross-file reference edges are fully materialized as real igraph edges with both endpoints resolved to vertex IDs at build time (`codeminer/graph/code_graph.py:195-229`; C++ backend emits resolved `(src_id,tgt_id,type,anchor_file,anchor_line)` in `scip_decode_core.py:99-123`). No unresolved-moniker / query-time path exists.
- An incremental patch to file F **rebuilds inbound cross-file edges from other files** via LSP `references()` (`patcher_base.py:488` → `subgraph_mgr.py:717-770` `reconnect_incoming()`; outbound via `reconnect_outgoing()`; deletes record severed in/out edges in `delete_file_subgraph()`).

Consequences: (1) "G unchanged ⇒ reuse G's subgraph" is violated, because changing F mutates edges attached to unchanged G; (2) MVCC is *not* free, because the concurrent indexer mutates the very graph a reader is traversing.

**Axis 3 — multi-tenancy. Decided: single-org self-hosted, weak isolation.** One deployment ≈ one tenant. Users within the org share one committed graph + each their own branch/commit + their own small mutable overlay. Row-level filtering suffices; no per-tenant database. Schema reserves a nullable `tenant_id` so a future multi-org SaaS RFC is an additive migration, not a rewrite. (Repo/docs/roadmap contain no SaaS/tenant requirement today — only a self-hosted CI runner.)

## Detailed Design

### The pivot: de-materialize cross-file edges

Stop resolving monikers at build time. Per blob, store:

- **intra-file edges** (CONTAIN + intra-file references) — immutable, travel with the blob.
- **unresolved cross-file references** — `(src_local_symbol, target_moniker, anchor_line)`, immutable, travel with the blob. The moniker is SCIP's global stable symbol id.
- **definitions index** — `moniker → (blob_hash, local_symbol)` for blobs that *define* a moniker.

Query-time resolution (bounded k-hop neighborhood, not whole-graph): given the active manifest's blob set, resolve each `target_moniker` to the defining blob *within that manifest*, with a hot-edge materialized cache for frequently traversed cross-file edges. This matches the workload (limited-hop retrieval, not global analysis) and removes the eager `reconnect_incoming` LSP pass from the incremental path entirely.

Net effect: axis 1 dedup becomes clean for *all* edges; axis 2 MVCC returns to free; incremental indexing gets cheaper.

### Storage substrate — boring and unkillable

Versioning/snapshot logic lives in **our** layer (blob-hash addressing + manifest + version-range predicates), over a dull, durable substrate — DuckDB/Postgres edge tables, conceptually reusing git's object store. Explicitly **do not** outsource version/time-travel semantics to a niche versioned DB (Datomic, TerminusDB, Dolt). The Kuzu lesson: a niche store can go unmaintained; TerminusDB is in the same ecosystem-size risk band. Keeping versioning in our layer makes swapping the substrate a local change, not another architecture-level migration.

Sketch (single-org, weak isolation; `tenant_id` nullable, reserved):

```
blobs(blob_hash PK, ...)                                  -- immutable, content-addressed
intra_edges(blob_hash, src_local, dst_local, edge_type)  -- immutable, follows blob
xref_unresolved(blob_hash, src_local, target_moniker, anchor_line)  -- immutable
defs(moniker, blob_hash, local_symbol)                   -- resolution index
versions(version_id PK, repo_id, commit_sha, schema_ver, model, status, tenant_id NULL)
manifest(version_id, blob_hash)                          -- (repo,commit) -> blob set; mirrors git tree
refs(repo_id, name, version_id, tenant_id NULL)          -- main / release-x / branch -> version
overlays(overlay_id, user_id, base_version_id)           -- per-user dirty workspace
overlay_blobs(overlay_id, blob_hash)                     -- only the user's changed-file subgraphs
```

A reader pins `(version_id, overlay_id?)`; every read filters `blob_hash ∈ manifest(version) ∪ overlay_blobs(overlay)`.

### Pluggable interface (the "hybrid" decision, unchanged)

A minimal backend-agnostic `IndexStore` contract: catalog/refs/version lifecycle + content-addressed blob put/get/has. Embedded default = SQLite/DuckDB catalog + content-addressed blob dir + FAISS files kept as blobs. A future server backend (Postgres + object store + a real vector DB) implements the same surface with no call-site changes. Validate the surface against the embedded impl only — don't pre-build for the server.

### Per-user overlay (axis 3, weak isolation)

A user's uncommitted edits = a small mutable overlay layered on a committed snapshot. Query view = `base-as-of-commit ∪ user overlay`. The overlay holds only that user's changed-file subgraphs (reuses the existing incremental delta machinery, emitting blobs instead of mutating the shared graph). Dropped on session end.

## Trade-offs & Risks

- **Query-time resolution cost.** k-hop traversal now does moniker→blob resolution. Mitigated by hot-edge cache and the limited-hop workload. This is the deliberate trade for clean versioning + free MVCC.
- **De-materialization is invasive.** Touches the graph build path, the SCIP/LSP decode (stop eager-resolving monikers, keep them), the incremental patcher (drop `reconnect_incoming` LSP pass), and the retrieval ops (add resolution + cache). Biggest single chunk of work — but it's the unlock for everything else.
- **Storage growth across versions.** Bounded by blob dedup (huge cross-commit overlap) + GC of unreffed versions/blobs past a grace window.
- **Migration.** Import the existing `.codeminer_cache/` + `repo_manifest.json` as one initial version (`ref=main`); compat shim so old manifest paths still load.
- **Substrate discipline.** Resist re-coupling cross-file edges into a mutable shared graph "for query speed" — that reintroduces the axis-2 break.

## Implementation Plan

- **Phase A — de-materialize cross-file edges (the pivot, do first).** Keep SCIP monikers unresolved per-blob; add `defs` index; resolve lazily at query time + hot-edge cache; remove eager `reconnect_incoming` from the incremental path. Validate graph-query parity against today's materialized graph.
- **Phase B — content-addressed blob store + manifests (axis 1).** Per-file blob subgraphs keyed by file content hash; `versions`/`manifest`/`refs` tables; incremental index reuses unchanged blobs. Multi-commit coexistence + rollback.
- **Phase C — snapshot isolation (axis 2).** Reader pins `(version, overlay)`; append-only base; MVCC reads; GC of unreffed versions/blobs.
- **Phase D — per-user overlay (axis 3, weak isolation).** Mutable overlay layer over a committed snapshot; row-level filtering; `tenant_id` reserved nullable.
- **(Deferred RFCs)** server substrate (Postgres + object store), vector-DB swap (Milvus partition-key / Qdrant / LanceDB), multi-org SaaS strong isolation.

## Effort

effort/large

items.title: [PO ACCEPTED / BUSINESS SCOPE CLOSED] Core Module 9.1–9.6/B – infrastructure TCO and technical proof OPEN
items.body:
# Shoperation Core 9.1 — Skálázhatóság, infrastruktúra- és költséghatékonysági döntés

**Keltezés:** 2026-10-13 (Europe/Budapest). **Hatályos PO scope zárás: 2026-10-14 (M9.1–9.6/B BUSINESS CLOSED; 9.7 visszavonva, technikai és pénzügyi kapuk OPEN).**
**Business state:** **9.1 PO ACCEPTED WITH BINDING CONDITIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE/TCO REVIEW BEFORE FINAL PLATFORM READINESS**.
**Technical state:** **NOT FULLY ASSESSED / MEASUREMENT & VENDOR COMPARISON DEFERRED TO MANDATORY GATE**. This is an agreed business architecture principle, NOT a claim that Vercel, Supabase, Resend or any alternative are demonstrably optimal, a technology migration decision, or a development kickoff.
**Roadmap anchor:** `quality/knowledge/living-roadmap.v2.json` → `SCALE-COST-ARCHITECTURE` (core capability, order 285) and then `CORE-SECURITY-PRIVACY-RESILIENCE` (290), `SHOPERATION-CORE-CAPABILITY-COMPLETE` (300), mandatory `CORE-OPERATIONAL-ADVERSARIAL-PROOF` (400). Existing Core Modules 1–8 business requirements and the Core-first / no early Builder path remain authoritative.

## Product Owner döntés, pontosan
1. **MOST nincs szükség 100%-os infrastruktúra-benchmarkra vagy azonnali provider-váltásra.** Az üzleti/architekturális követelményt és végrehajtási kaput most rögzítjük, a fejlesztés során csak a későbbi összehasonlíthatóságot és költségmérést alapozzuk meg. Ne tereljük el a Core megvalósítását korai, drága újraírással.
2. **A webshop teljes végleges üzemi késznek minősítése / Market Ready / éles skálázhatóság elfogadása ELŐTT KÖTELEZŐ valós, reprodukálható, teljes körű infrastruktúra- és szolgáltatóválasztási vizsgálat**. Ez blocking business + Capability/Dependency Closure gate: az aktuális **Vercel + Supabase + e-mail sending provider (jelenlegi Resend)** architektúra pénzügyi és műszaki racionalitását **más elérhető és reálisan megvalósítható alternatívákkal** össze kell vetni.
3. **No provider lock-in by inertia.** Vercel, Supabase és Resend jelenleg használatban lévő eszközök, nem végleges márkahűségi döntések. Bármelyik maradhat, cserélhető vagy szolgáltatási határ mentén vegyes infrastruktúra alakulhat ki, de csak mért költség/teljesítmény/stabilitás/kockázat és kontrollált PO döntés szerint. A meglévő Supabase Postgres, Auth/RLS, transactional RPC, storage, scheduled jobs/queues és tenant identity/security migrációs kockázata külön bizonyítandó; e-mailnél külön provider adapter, suppression, consent, webhooks, bounce, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, transactional vs marketing és később M6.3 tarifascope. Nem építünk új e-mail/DB/hosting domaint kézzel másolatként.
4. **Nem csak a legolcsóbb kell.** A cél a műszakilag megbízható, gyors, biztonságos, jól skálázódó és fenntarthatóan nyereséges webshopmotor. **Megtakarított például ~1000 Ft/webshop/hó nem indokol elfogadhatatlan checkout-lassulást, ár/készlet inkonzisztenciát, gyakori rendelkezésreállási hibát, adatvesztést vagy gyenge hibatűrést.** A fizetőképesség és a valós teljes életciklusköltség egyszerre döntési tényező.
5. **Cost transparency required.** Meg kell mérni a platform összes közvetlen fix és változó havidíját, de a marzs-számításban a költségek számlázási scope-ját, multi-tenant megoszlását és a teljes tulajdonlási költséget is. ## 9.2/A — A monitorozás saját költsége és terhelése — kötelező költség-haszon és önterhelési kapu (2026-10-13 PO KIEGÉSZÍTÉS, ELFOGADVA)

**Product Owner-követelmény:** „Nehogy a költség- és egészségfigyelő rendszer maga dobja meg jelentősen az infrastruktúra-költségvetést, vagy terhelje annyira a webshopokat, hogy éppen az akadozást okozza.” Analógia: egy jármű akkumulátorát felügyelő eszköz fogyasztása is lehet káros, ha túlzottan terheli az akkumulátort. Ez az **erőforrás-önterhelés / observer effect / monitoring overhead** önálló, blokkoló nemfunkcionális minőségi követelmény a **9.1 TCO-gate és 9.2 telemetry/estimated-vs-invoice rendszerben**; nem pusztán megjegyzés vagy posztlaunch optimalizáció.

### Üzleti működési és gazdasági szabályok
1. **A figyelő saját költsége is teljes körűen mérendő és elszámolandó.** A metrikák/logok/traces létrehozása, mintavétele, tárolása/retention-je, event bus/queue, címkekardinalitás, per-tenant aggregáció, dashboard query, riasztásküldés, költségmodellezés, számlafeldolgozás, havi reconciliáció, opciókénti külső monitoring/SaaS vagy AI-tokenszámítás ugyanúgy compute, IOPS/DB, CPU/RAM, hálózati egress/CDN, storage, invokáció és mérnöki üzemeltetési költséget jelent. Ez a platform számlájából és a 9.2 becsült költségmodellből **NEM hagyható ki**; ahol pontosan nem mérhető, megalapozottan becsült, külön jelölt.
2. **Nem lehet végtelen „a monitorozást is monitorozó” lánc.** A monitor overhead alapvető accountingja egyszerű, alacsony költségű, külső provider-billing/aggregate + ritka belső self-health számlálókból történjen; ne építsünk második teljes megfigyelőgépet az elsőre, amely önmagában egy harmadikat igényel. Sentinel/Control Plane és meglévő admin incident/attention felületek újrafelhasználása kötelező, duplikált monitoring authority tilos.
3. **Gazdasági kapu:** a 9.1, 9.2 és végső Core audit mutassa külön az *alkalmazás normál erőforrásköltsége*, *monitorozás hozzáadott direkt+mérnöki költsége*, *monitorozás nélküli / csökkentett telemetriás, azonos terhelésű kontroll összehasonlítás* és *mérhetően elhárított vagy korán felismert kockázat/incidens értéke* bontást. Az elkerült veszteség csak **bizonyítható, vagy bizonytalansággal jelölt** becslés lehet; nem számolhatunk találomra „a monitoring 10× megtérül” állítást. Egy drága funkció csak érdemi, igazolt hibamegelőzési vagy diagnosztikai értékkel és PO jóváhagyással maradhat.
4. **Adaptív mérési mélység:** preferált a szolgáltatói natív aggregált usage, batch/scheduled feldolgozás, olcsó sampling és kis címkekardinalitás, csak szükségesnél rövid idejű mély tracing. A ritka, egyszerű üzletek monitorozása ne legyen aránytalanul drágább, mint az üzletek normál működése. Fontos checkout/payment/stock-integrity/security és tenant-isolációs audit **soha nem tűnhet el**, ha a mély, nem kritikus trace-k gyűjtése költségkorlát miatt csökken. Erőforrás-terhelésnél kontrollált **degradation**: elsőként részletes diagnosztikai minták/retention csökkentése, nem maguk a kereskedelmi funkciók, kritikus bizonyítékok vagy riasztások kikapcsolása.
5. **Noisy neighbor és self-induced regressions:** egy tenant, hibás importer, bot, videófeltöltés vagy hibás riasztási ciklus ne hozzon létre egész platformra kiterjedő „log storm”-ot, high-cardinality tag-explosiont, végtelen retry/e-mail riasztás-sorozatot vagy számlázható polling-vihart. Limit, bulkhead/backpressure/queue, sampled logging, dedup és metering cost budget kötelező. A figyelő endpoint/process failure a webshop core checkout útját alaphelyzetben **ne blokkolja**, ugyanakkor a jogi és biztonsági audit események tartós, külön védett megőrzése kötelező.
6. **Teljesítmény-kapu:** production-like reprezentatív teszten szét kell választani a webshop terhelését a 9.2 measurement middleware/logging overheadjétől p50/p95/p99 fő requestek (külön checkout/search/PDP), DB kapcsolat és lock, háttérqueue, memória, forgalom és compute szempontjából. Külön peak-drop, kampány, súlyos hibafolyamat és 1/10/100/1000 tenant scenario; a vizsgálat eredménye alapján **PO-val jóváhagyott konkrét monitoring-overhead és operating-budget küszöbértékeket** kell megállapítani, nem most kitalált „maximum 1%” eredményeket. Túlzott mért overhead esetén a megfigyelőrendszer **nem TECHNICALLY DONE**.
7. **Cost awareness nem költségvakság:** ne válasszunk olyan olcsó monitorozást, amelyből hiányzik a súlyos checkout/payment hibák, adatvesztés, jogsértő adatkezelés, cross-tenant biztonsági probléma vagy perzisztens performance degradáció felismerése. A minőségi/safety coverage és a monitor-teljes költség **együttes optimalizálása** a cél, nem minimális megfigyelés minden áron.
8. **A becslő becslésénél a saját overhead is bekerül a tényleges havi számlával összevetendő költségledgerekbe** (`observability_direct`, `observability_shared_allocated`, `monitor_estimate_processing` megfelelő versioned accounting definícióként, nem előírt implementációs kulcsnévként). Minden kalibráció és korrekció auditált, számla megőrzött, owner-reviewed, nulla kötelező AI vagy fizetős provider aktiválás.

## 9.3 — Kapacitáskezelés, forgalomhoz illeszkedő erőforrás-allokáció és terhelés alatti üzembiztonság — PO ELFOGADVA, architektúraválasztás MÉG NYITOTT (2026-10-13)

**Előző PO jóváhagyás:** 500 webshop / egy hirtelen nagy akció példája; egy webshop túlterhelése nem ronthatja le más tenantok checkoutját, vásárlásait, alap sebességét vagy biztonságát. Alap és Pro ugyanazon alapvető megbízhatósági, érdemi oldalbetöltési és ügyletkonzisztencia-színvonal; Pro nem jelent általános sebességi paywallt. Peak-burst, pénzügyi tranzakció, készlet és biztonság prioritás; nagy CSV/import, tömeges feladatok hátrasorolhatók; autoscaling/capacity használat ellenőrzött költségbudget és bizonyítható terhelési teszt alapján. **Ez üzleti scope elfogadás, még nem tuning vagy cloud provider-módosítás.**

**A felhasználó új, világos példákkal bemutatott kiegészítése (elfogadott vizsgálati követelmény):** A Vercel által választható nagyobb „gépméretek” és a Supabase-adatbázis közötti szűk keresztmetszetet, a webshopok aktuális fogyasztását és a játékipari progresszív/preloading megközelítés webes megfelelőit vizsgáljuk meg. **Ha 500 webshopból például 100-nál nincs aktív kérés, ne égessenek szükségtelen dinamikus számítási kapacitást; a ténylegesen forgalmasak kapjanak a tényleges szükséglet szerinti kapacitást** – de a csendes webshop is legyen azonnal elérhető, használható, rendelhető, ne legyen „alvó üzlet” vagy érezhető ébresztési büntetés. Ez **cél és feasibility-gate**, nem előre jóváhagyott tenant-hibernálás, fix erőforrás-hozzárendelés vagy provider-automatikus átkonfigurálás.

### Fontos technikai tények (forrásellenőrzés 2026-10-13)
- Vercel Functions / Fluid Compute dokumentáltan **automatikusan skálázódik a kérelmekhez**, forgalommentes időszakban a funkciópéldányok leállhatnak, és több I/O-bound kérés ugyanazon példányban futhat; a projekt beállításainál Standard 2 GB/1 vCPU és Pro/Enterprise esetén Performance 4 GB/2 vCPU konfiguráció választható, azonban ez **nem a merchant tenantonként fel/le kapcsolható gép kiválasztása**, és a drágább CPU nem garantál automatikusan gyorsabb Supabase-t. [Vercel Functions](https://vercel.com/docs/functions); [Fluid Compute](https://vercel.com/docs/fluid-compute); [Memory/CPU](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/memory).
- A hálózati/CDN cache, ISR és háttér-újragenerálás sok statikus vagy kevésbé dinamikus termék/kollekció tartalmat válaszolhat meg a backend teljes futtatása nélkül. **Személyes/cross-tenant/B2B protected/fiscal/order/cart/payment válaszra közös, ellenőrizetlen cache TILOS**; a termékár, készlet/variáns/checkout a canonical authorityból a kritikus végpontnál újraellenőrzött. [Vercel CDN cache](https://vercel.com/docs/caching/cdn-cache); [ISR](https://vercel.com/docs/incremental-static-regeneration).
- A gyakori párhuzamos vásárlás **Vercel és PostgreSQL/Supabase oldalát is** terheli; a bottleneck lehet CDN miss/SSR CPU, megugró invokáció, felhő–DB régió késleltetése, adatbázis-connection pool, lock/transaction/slow query, stock/race és PSP/provider bottleneck. A Supabase serverless esetekre transaction pooler és erőforrásmérés lehetőségeket dokumentál. A Function régiót a DB-hez közel tartani alapesetben indokolt; a Supabase aktív adatbázis projekt resource cost nem tűnik el attól, hogy az adott merchant csendes. [Supabase connection docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres); [Supabase pool limits](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres/pooling-and-limits).
- A gaming „ajtó/lift loading” **szelleme alkalmazható**, de a webes buyer UX célja nem mesterségesen elnyújtott animáció. Valódi hasznos optimalizáció: statikus/ritkán változó tartalom előre-készítése (prerender/ISR), CDN cache, kliens oldali intelligens prefetch/loading, képek méretezése/lazy load, szándékos UI progression, párhuzamosítható read-only adatlekérés és nem tranzakciókritikus feladat aszinkron queue-ba mozgatása. Nem hamis stock/ár, nem elrejtett valódi 10s késleltetés; a végső user-perceived latency mérése dönt.

| 1. Multi-tenant isolation | Egy nagy akció/rossz bot/import/heavy search tenantja nem teheti tönkre a többi merchant PDP/cart/checkout/DB hozzáférést: tenant-scope fairness/isolated queue, rate/burst, bulkhead és backpressure, de a normál, jogosult vevői vásárlás szándékos elfojtása nélkül |

A korábban 9.7-ként felvetett **önálló emberi ügyeleti/incidenskezelési motor nem kapott PO-elfogadást, a javaslatot az átfedő 9.4/9.5/A és meglévő Control Plane/Sentinel authority miatt visszavontuk**. Nem indítunk mesterséges 9.7 funkciót, új ticket/shift/incident párhuzamos motort vagy új funkcionális döntéskört. Ez felülírja a dokumentum korábbi köztes „9.7+ üzleti felülvizsgálat nyitott” megjegyzéseit.

**Üzletileg elfogadott elvek:** (1) vevő-, kereskedő- és tenant-biztonság; (2) üzemszerű helyes működés, stabil minőség; (3) tényszerűen alátámasztott, méretarányos TCO-optimalizálás — ebben a sorrendben. Alap és Pro közös üzemi biztonsági minimum; Pro nem jelent kivételt veszélyes éles módosításokra. Központi kötelező Core-security frissítések a 9.6/A szerinti, kockázatalapú, tenant-specifikus preflighttal; kereskedői örök verziókihagyás és per-tenant Core fragmentáció nélkül.

**Kifejezetten nyitva maradó, kötelező végrehajtási és elfogadási kapuk:**
- **9.1 infrastruktúra/TCO kapu:** teljes Vercel/Supabase/e-mail provider és releváns reális alternatívák számlákkal, mért usage-zsal, teljesítménnyel, security/DR-rel, per-tenant/order egységköltséggel és 1/12/24/36 havi TCO-val történő reprodukálható összevetése a végső Core / Market Ready elfogadás ELŐTT. Az infrastruktúra/provider végleges kiválasztása NINCS elfogadva; az explicit fizetős szolgáltatói aktiválás vagy átváltás PO engedélyt igényel.
- **9.2–9.6 műszaki bizonyíték:** valós tenantonkénti erőforrás-/monitoring-overhead adatok; load/soak, concurrency/noisy-neighbor, kritikus order/payment/stock correctness; mentés/restore, RTO/RPO/SLO, GDPR/security, riasztások, központi változáskezelés és per-tenant előellenőrzés teljes E2E/negatív, exact-head CI, Completion Truth, Lifecycle, Core Operational/Adversarial Audit. **TECHNICALLY OPEN / NOT VERIFIED**; forráskód vagy issue szöveg nem tekinthető teljesítési bizonyítéknak.
- **Külön üzleti ár/limit döntések:** [M6.3 e-mailküldési tarifa #1264](https://github.com/infowaterk-max/water-K-/issues/1264), M1 tárhelybővítés díjazása, plusz csak valós költségvizsgálat után felmerülő infrastruktúra/provider pénzügyi döntés. Ezek nem kerülnek hallgatólagosan elfogadásra, nem aktiválhatnak új költséget.
- **Meglévő végrehajtási authority:** [Living Roadmap v2](https://github.com/infowaterk-max/water-K-/blob/main/quality/knowledge/living-roadmap.v2.json) `SCALE-COST-ARCHITECTURE` (285) → `CORE-SECURITY-PRIVACY-RESILIENCE` (290) → `SHOPERATION-CORE-CAPABILITY-COMPLETE` (300) → `CORE-OPERATIONAL-ADVERSARIAL-PROOF` (400); az elfogadott Core-funkciók owner-operable E2E hiányainak [#1284](https://github.com/infowaterk-max/water-K-/issues/1284) felülvizsgálata. A technikai feladatok végrehajtása dependency-order, Plan Before Code és a meglévő closure gate szerint történhet; **Core first → audit → product experience → Builder → sablon**.
  
**Állapot és változtatási határ:** M9 PO BUSINESS ACCEPTED / BUSINESS SCOPE CLOSED; M9.1 TCO/provider commercial selection OPEN; technical implementation/proof OPEN. Ez a bejegyzés docs-only issue-módosítás; **nincs kód, PR, CI, új fizetős provider, staging/production környezetmódosítás vagy korai Builder/Template kickoff**.
