items.body:
**This issue is now an index.** Perf work is tracked as one issue per problem and one project thread per coherent improvement (decided 2026-09-25). New findings go in their own issue with the `performance` label; link them here. The original operating loop is kept at the bottom.

Index built 2026-09-25 from all 269 comments, including the client runtime audit (https://github.com/garden-co/jazz/issues/2913#issuecomment-5824381351), the storage/sync audit (https://github.com/garden-co/jazz/issues/2913#issuecomment-5824419904) and the query-engine audit (https://github.com/garden-co/jazz/issues/2913#issuecomment-5824604423).

## Open: split out from this issue

### Client runtime and bindings
- [ ] #3359 SubscriptionManager copies all its state on every delta (~7 ms/delta at 10k rows)
- [ ] #3360 Vue/Svelte/Solid adapters reconcile every row; the diff path is dead (74 ms/delta on Vue at 10k)
- [ ] #3361 `transformRow` rebuilds include plans and `analyzeRelations` per row (~6× slower with includes)
- [ ] #3362 A child edit deep-clones and re-transforms the whole root
- [x] #3363 `terminalOccurrenceAddresses` is never pruned
- [ ] #3364 Removing many roots in one delta is quadratic
- [ ] #3365 Hex key formatting dominates first load
- [ ] #3366 Same-index replacements force the O(k·N) path
- [ ] #3367 Row codec rebuilds layout per cell and decodes twice
- [ ] #3368 IDB tree cold range scans restart from the root per page miss
- [ ] #3369 Terminal-op bytes cross NAPI/WASM/RN as number arrays or JSON
- [ ] #3370 React Native write waits busy-poll
- [ ] #3371 Small redundant copies on the delta and write paths (checklist)

### Storage, sync and server
- [ ] #3372 Alias → node lookup is a linear scan over every node
- [ ] #3373 Root authority keeps every client commit in its upload outbox forever
- [ ] #3374 Server wake storm: every inbound frame wakes every session (inferred O(N²))
- [ ] #3375 Every inbound write re-serves every coverage group
- [ ] #3376 Untrusted inbound messages canonicalised several times, commits validated twice
- [ ] #3377 Write policy evaluated twice per version on session commit
- [ ] #3378 Snapshots fully encoded for a byte count, deep-cloned per sibling
- [x] #3379 `table_in_schema` deep-clones `TableSchema` per row
- [ ] #3380 Every `VersionRecord` embeds the full descriptor on the wire
- [ ] #3381 IDB tree `write_many` re-encodes the path per key
- [x] #3382 `mutation_gate` held across the IndexedDB commit
- [ ] #3383 SQLite: no statement cache, eager scans, copied batches
- [ ] #3384 Transport: 70 KB zeroed buffer per chunk and repeated frame copies
- [ ] #3385 Reconnect with K offline writes is O(K²)
- [ ] #3386 Permission advice scans the whole table for one row
- [x] #3387 `account_still_admitted` per websocket message
- [ ] #3388 Per-row metadata rebuilt instead of cached per descriptor
- [ ] #3389 Resident overlay rebuilds its latest-key index per poll while persistence lags
- [ ] #3390 After restart, `open_transaction` scans once per accepted global time
- [ ] #3391 Tier 3 small scans and copies (checklist)
- [ ] #3392 Native relay may drop drained messages on backpressure (possible correctness bug)
- [ ] #3393 Reconnect catch-up scales with result size, not the missed delta (also the supporting-manifest thesis this issue started with)

### Query engine, cold load and regressions
- [x] #3394 W1 indexed update without a subscription ~13–16% slower since #2925 (closed 2026-10-13: no consistent difference after #3730; revert trial #3493 closed)
- [ ] #3395 Cold load: intermediate row representations, no current thesis (measured ≤1.03 conversions per version per node; counters in draft #3791)
- [ ] #3396 Cold-load flamegraph attribution is unreliable (poll-site and operator phases in #3786)
- [ ] #3397 Record typed programs from the real runtime instead of a scratch runtime
- [ ] #3398 Relay recompiles one program per subscription after identity adoption
- [ ] #3400 Re-measure unconfirmed small regressions (checklist)
- [ ] #3401 Warm-phase profile harness panic on relay known-state
- [ ] #3402 Typed version-witness reconstruction ~2.5% of cold load (draft #2961; now ~1%, suggested not planned)
- [x] #3403 `last_with_prefix_before_or_at` still unbounded
- [x] #3404 `index_scan_raw_in_batch` misses staged secondary-index changes (API hazard)
- [ ] #3405 Retained subscriptions can't use policy-root PK selection (#2187)
- [ ] #3406 Browser: re-measure durable sequential writes and first-subscription materialisation
- [ ] #3473 In-transaction reads load the whole table per query; Jamazon checkout ~37 ms (#3487 single-pass read, #3486 descriptor rebuilds)
- [ ] #3476 In-transaction reads scale with table history, not result size
- [ ] #3491 Pending (ahead) current tables have no column indexes; offline backlogs scan every pending row (needs a storage-format decision)
- [ ] #3500 Exclusive commit validation re-scans each predicate table's whole history (in flight)
- [x] #3516 content_head_indices is quadratic in a row's history length; hot rows in Jamazon checkout (fixed by #3517)
- [x] #3524 Snapshot coverage decodes a full stored transaction per row version (fixed by #3525)
- [ ] #3554 Cold permissioned Global one-shot page costs ~640 ms through the sync path; linear history #3281 is the expected lever
- [ ] #3797 Cold load: Core recomputes ~40% of hydration nodes across one reader's subscriptions

### Groove IVM and query evaluation (query-engine audit)
- [ ] #3410 Aggregates recompute the whole group on every write (60 ms/write at 50k rows in group)
- [ ] #3411 Every write tick copies all prepared-shape bindings twice (3.9 ms/write at 10k bindings)
- [ ] #3412 Every one-shot query and unsubscribe runs a full-graph GC walk (613 µs/query at 1k subscriptions)
- [ ] #3413 Include/collect ranks are linear scans; a debug-only scan runs in release (2.1 s hydrate at 20k parents)
- [ ] #3414 Limited or nested collect re-renders the whole group twice per change (55 ms/insert at 10k children)
- [ ] #3415 Result members clone every version of their transaction, O(K²) for bulk transactions (check with #3281)
- [ ] #3416 Flat app-row subscriptions do `Vec::contains` per row; order vector never shrinks
- [ ] #3417 Compile: requests Debug-formatted 6–8 times; prepared plans built and discarded
- [ ] #3418 Per-tick scans over all runtime state
- [ ] #3419 Publication work repeated per subscriber sharing an output node
- [ ] #3420 Recursive insert scans the whole accumulated closure
- [ ] #3421 Compile-time path blowup on shared subtrees
- [ ] #3422 Query engine small scans and copies (checklist)

### Measurement
- [ ] #3407 Benchmark coverage gaps (checklist)
- [ ] #3408 Switchable work counters and receipt provenance

## Open: already tracked elsewhere
- #3282 Follow-ups after the compile-once stack (first subscriptions to policy pages at 10k rows, bind/install cost, descriptor construction, browser fanout validation)
- #3290 TopBy top-20 window costs more than the full input (`update_top_by`, `SparseGroups::commit_overlay`)
- #3287, #3289, #3291, #3294, #3272 Perf theses from 2026-09-23/24
- #3301 Non-storage-backed views still use full membership reconciliation
- #2136 Caught-up resume rehydrates the full maintained view; #2372 W1 resume; #2086 deltas scale with changed rows
- #2981 Hot-row history depth (#3117 and #3118 landed; #3403 is the remainder)
- #2985 Filtered top-N reads the full scan set (composite indexes and ordered pages are in flight)
- #3231 Browser warm reload of a 564-row include query; #2989 WASM startup footprint
- #3144 / draft #3146 Hydration scans unrelated memos; #3159 Recursive ArgBy live-update
- #3174 CodSpeed build latency and the simulated-example job timeout
- #3308 Root-collector routing (fixed by #3330; issue still open)
- #3339, #3340, #3341, #3342, #3347 Filed by the perf thread on 2026-09-24
- Flaky write-scaling canary: draft #3151

## In flight
- #3352 composite indexes → #3353 join links by covered keys; ordered pages (#3315, #3316, #3317, #3325 being ported); #3334
- #3354 incremental attach; #3348 client prepared shapes
- #3355 fix for #3349 (subscription over a >64 KB row hangs)
- #3281 linear history (also the natural fix for #3393)
- #2961 identity-only witnesses (#3402); #3196 frame-state versioning (measured not a win)
- #3786 cold-load poll-site and operator phase attribution (#3396); draft #3791 representation-conversion counters (#3395)

## Fixed (merged)
- **Supporting manifests and receiver normalization:** #2916/#2917 (via #2918), #2919, #2920, #2927, #2935, #2942, #2943, #2951, then #2953 (shared scoped inputs replace occurrence expansion) and #2954 (volatile subscription scope).
- **Ordered outputs and collectors:** #2921, #2922, #2931, #2941, #3199 (persistent root ranks; also fixed the crossing-move ordering bug), #3309, #3330.
- **Cold load:** #2923, #2924, #2926, #2934, #2937, #2938, #2940, #2945, #2948, #3161.
- **Write path:** #2925, #2929, #2930, #2932, #2933, #2936, #2939, #3203, #3256.
- **Hot-row history and joins:** #3116, #3117, #3118, #3142, #3143, #3155, #3162, #3167, #3168.
- **Policy reads and subscription opening:** #3072, #3073, #3085, #3175, #3336, #3337, #3338.
- **Execution engine and compile-once (stack #3206, 29 PRs):** #3186, #3204, #3205, #3208, #3217, #3219, #3225, #3226, #3227, #3233, #3236–#3239, #3241, #3243, #3244, #3254, #3257, #3258, #3261, #3262, #3275, #3278, #3279, #3280.
- **Routing and IVM CPU:** #3306, #3332. **Storage:** #3255, #3335.

## Rejected experiments (branches preserved)
#2928, #2944, #2946, #2947, #2949, #2950, #2952 (superseded by #2953), #3245, #3313 (superseded by #3332), and the source-contract fragment trial (`codex/source-contract-fragment-trial`). Also dropped after profiling: join duplicate-pair encoding, oversized async futures, pruning indexes via `arrangement_needs_index`, terminal-descriptor canonicalization as a cold-load lever.

## Not filed, with reason
- Retained-footprint double-charging of shared witness payloads: footprint became diagnostics-only in #3203.
- Discarded peer fact copy in `record_source_fact_transition`: the direct-routing attempt #2946 showed no win.
- Durable by-parent pending-edge index: #3281 removes parents.
- Shared transaction preflight/fate caching: deliberately deferred (mutable settlement is not admission evidence).
- Empty cross-term index in inner joins, and the +0.4% prepared-payload memory: too small to track.

<details>
<summary>Original operating loop (2026-09-13)</summary>

🤖 Proposed performance iteration loop for sequential todo inserts and permissioned cold load.

## Workloads and acceptance

Use the example-owned benchmark foundation in #2906. The existing todo cases cover reopen, batched updates and sequential updates; they do not measure sequential inserts. Add an explicit insert case before attributing insert improvements to those receipts. Each insert must be a separate transaction with the chosen settlement/delivery boundary completed before the next; batching is a separate control. Keep the RocksDB WAL-without-fsync setting, subscription topology, allocator, and timing boundaries explicit. Verify exact IDs and values after timing. Retain the 1,500-row todo scale, and record per-block latency to detect a growing cost per insert.

Keep permissioned cold load at the existing 27,518 expected rows across 39 subscriptions, Core → Edge → Client with empty downstream receivers. Preserve identity, policies, history, transport and exact per-table row-ID assertions. Do not expand toward 1M until work amplification at the current size is understood.

## Experiment loop

1. Freeze the workload and correctness checks on a known source SHA. Save source/tree, binary SHA256, command, package/features, allocator, optimization profile, storage durability and machine metadata for each comparison. Keep diagnostic instrumentation out of clean timing binaries.
2. Use current local CPU profiles, CodSpeed wall-time flamegraphs and code to name one avoidable unit of work. Read `dev/benchmarks/rejected-experiments.md` and search previous PRs first. Record a changed premise before repeating a rejected mechanism.
3. Record the thesis in a linked issue or comment before implementation: mechanism, workload, predicted counter change, estimated end-to-end headroom and a rejection condition. Avoid predicting a large gain from an inclusive stack share alone.
4. Make one small reversible candidate on the current best checkpoint. Run focused correctness checks and comparable optimized native baseline/candidate timings in alternating order, with no concurrent builds or other benchmark runs. Start with three pairs; use more samples only when the decision remains ambiguous. Treat repeatable end-to-end wins above the observed noise as evidence; a roughly 5% gain is a useful initial screening target, not a universal significance rule. Smaller changes can qualify when they simplify code or prove improved scaling.
5. Verify both target workloads and the existing todo update/reopen controls. Record wall time, completed operations per second, scaling slope, storage operations/bytes, serialized supporting rows/bytes and relevant operator work. Peak/live memory and cumulative allocation traffic are distinct metrics.
6. Retain a candidate only if its target improves without an unexplained material regression or semantic change elsewhere. Close losing trials and preserve their exact receipts and branches. Do not roll an unexplained failure into the next candidate.
7. Send retained checkpoints to CodSpeed against an explicit baseline with the same workload revision. Confirm the intended benchmarks actually ran: inherited/skipped results are not fresh evidence. Inspect the wall-time distribution and profile, then run fully optimized browser/WASM acceptance at milestones. Local x86 and CodSpeed ARM64 are separate series; no environment-calibration project is currently requested.
8. Land small independently reviewed checkpoints with required correctness gates. Rebase the next experiment on the accepted winner. Keep benchmark changes and runtime changes distinguishable so the search cannot improve its score by doing less of the required workload.

## First thesis: repeated supporting-row scope work dominates sequential delivery

#2912 removes full predecessor/current set comparison from ordinary publication bookkeeping, but the wire still carries a complete supporting-row manifest. `MaintainedSubscriptionView::active_peer_source_closure_facts` clones facts into a BTreeSet; `NodeState::supporting_rows_for_facts` maps and deduplicates them into another set. The complete manifest is constructed even after a one-row change and must also be consumed downstream.

For the existing 1,350-update / 1,500-row case this exposes about 2.025M manifest entries per full traversal. A growing-table insert workload may expose the corresponding sum of prior scope sizes; measure that directly rather than assuming update results transfer to inserts.

First measure authoring/persistence, publication, encode/decode and receiver application separately, alongside a raw-storage control with matching writes and durability. Count full-scope traversals and entries. Then test eliminating repeated internal materialization or comparison while preserving the complete manifest and permissions. A genuinely incremental wire protocol would be a separate design decision requiring reconnect, reset, rejection, revocation and coverage invariants; do not silently turn this into a protocol experiment.

## Second thesis: cold first delivery may construct intermediate work that cancels

The current local coarse receipt places about 81% of tick time downstream at Edge+Client. This includes ingest, evaluation and publication; it is not a pure-storage attribution. The CodSpeed profile is diffuse in copying, comparison and container work, and its async ancestry has known misleading frames.

`JoinState::apply` already has a full-snapshot Replace path that probes once. Ordinary Accumulate emits dL×Rnew + Lnew×dR − dL×dR; same-frontier new/new pairs may be encoded repeatedly then consolidated away. Quantify pre-consolidation pairs/bytes, retained output, arrangement updates and relevant frontier/mode per node and tier using batch-level opt-in counters. Existing counters record join inputs/final outputs but not all discarded pair construction.

Only if those counters show substantial headroom, test a safe operator/frontier-scoped way to avoid redundant first-delivery work. Shared arrangements can already be advanced by another consumer, so container emptiness alone is not proof. Otherwise select the largest demonstrated intermediate relation or phase from the new receipt.

Direct construction of fresh join indexes alone was already rejected in #2864 (12.404s versus 12.212s); do not repeat it merely because hash overlays appear in a flamegraph. The changed premise would need to eliminate measured redundant output work, not just rearrange index construction.

Related: #2086, #2372, #2906, #2910, #2912. Implementation and measurement updates belong in this issue or linked single-thesis issues. This is a proposed operating loop, not a claim of measured insert improvement.

</details>

Tracking issue for the **Governed - Designer** session (UI/UX review for the 2026-11-01 demo, ADR-0197; freeze 2026-10-29).

**Approval gate (owner instruction):** no product code changes until the owner approves specific samples. Every status update, sample link and owner decision is posted here as a comment.

## Phase 1: research and samples (in progress)
- [ ] Capture today's UI (demo screenshots + mock-mode Playwright for Shadow AI screens)
- [ ] Extract UX patterns from the gap analyses (reference products A/B/…; no vendor names)
- [ ] Heuristic review ranked by demo impact
- [ ] Sample: InfoTip (i) pattern (builds on the existing `InfoButton` in `apps/web/src/ui/kit.tsx`)

- A stale or unverifiable browser bundle makes qualification `VOID`; browser evidence starts by matching `window.__APP_RELEASE__`.
- Current `main`, production release, open PR heads, migration/application state, and gate evidence must be read rather than inferred.
- Retired Basic/canary secret names must not be documented as active. Current test identities and secret/variable homes must match authoritative GitHub inventory without exposing values.
- Issue-first intake, linked Draft PRs, exact-artifact reports, mutation-proven gates, detour budgets, and consolidated review are the active delivery model.
- Merge, migration, deployment, activation, paid testing, and production proof remain separate authorization decisions.

## Protected canonical `product_release` set

The following 14 Product Owner-approved canonical documents are **mandatory retained authorities**. They must be brought up to date; they are not deletion or redirect candidates:

1. `product_release/README.md`
2. `product_release/PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`
3. `product_release/ROADMAP.md`
4. `product_release/ARCHITECTURE.md`
5. `product_release/STT.md`
6. `product_release/PROGRESS_AND_NEXT_ACTION.md`
7. `product_release/ENTITLEMENTS_AND_BILLING.md`
8. `product_release/QUALITY.md`
9. `product_release/RELEASE_PROCESS.md`
10. `product_release/RELEASE_STATUS.md`
11. `product_release/OPERATIONS_AND_SECURITY.md`
12. `product_release/TESTER_GUIDE.md`
13. `product_release/TESTER_OPERATIONS.md`
14. `product_release/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`

If a canonical file is missing from the working tree, the PR must materialize it from its approved source map before closeout. Changing this protected set requires a separate Product Owner ruling.

## Disposition criteria

Every file must receive exactly one terminal disposition. The decision must cite current consumers, canonical overlap, current factual accuracy, and inbound links.

### UPDATE / RETAIN CURRENT

Use only when all are true:

- The file is one of the protected 14, or it has a distinct current operational audience that no canonical document serves.
- Its purpose remains necessary now.
- Its claims, commands, paths, identities, and links can be verified against the current codebase or authoritative GitHub/runtime evidence.
- Keeping it does not create a second authority for the same subject.

Required evidence: named owner/authority, current-source citations, exact corrections made, link check, and stale-token scan.

### CONSOLIDATE AND REMOVE

Use when all are true:

- The file contains at least one still-useful current fact or procedure.
- That content belongs in one of the protected 14 or another clearly named current operational authority.
- Keeping both files would duplicate or conflict with authority.

Required evidence: source-to-target section map, proof that every retained current fact moved, inbound-link repairs, and deletion of the redundant source in the same PR.

### CURRENT REDIRECT

Use narrowly when the old path still has an active repository/tool/reader dependency and immediate deletion would break it.

- Body contains only a concise current pointer and effective date/reason.
- It contains no independent product or operational claims.
- The ledger names the consumer requiring the redirect and the condition/date for later removal.

Required evidence: active inbound consumer plus validated target. A redirect is not a default substitute for cleanup.

### DELETE

Use when any is true and no still-current unique content remains:

- Fully obsolete, historical-only, superseded, or contradicted by current truth.
- Entirely duplicated by a protected canonical or current operational authority.
- A temporary plan, packet, ledger, or evidence narrative whose durable result is already captured.
- No current audience, execution path, or active inbound dependency justifies retention.

Deletion is prohibited until useful current content (if any) is consolidated and inbound links are repaired. Git history preserves provenance. Required evidence: reason, current authority replacing it (or “none needed”), inbound-link scan, and recovery path through git history.

### Mandatory decision order

1. Protect and update the canonical 14.
2. Identify unique current operational documents.
3. Consolidate useful current content from duplicates into those authorities.
4. Redirect only where a live dependency requires it.
5. Delete the remainder.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A checked-in ledger lists every starting file, classification, canonical owner, required correction, and terminal disposition.
- [ ] All 14 protected canonical documents exist, remain in place, and are verified current.
- [ ] Every other non-archived documentation file is reviewed and receives exactly one terminal outcome: retained-current, consolidated-and-removed, current redirect, or deleted.
- [ ] No path under `product_release/archive/**` changes.
- [ ] Every retained Markdown describes current product/operations truth; past requirements appear only when necessary to explain a current migration/removal obligation.
- [ ] No non-archived Markdown remains solely to describe a past requirement, superseded workflow, or historical test result; still-current evidence is consolidated into current authorities and redundant historical files are removed.
- [ ] Root/docs/product_release duplication is resolved through canonical pointers rather than parallel truth.
- [ ] All commands, paths, workflow names, environment names, account identities, and links are verified against current code/GitHub.
- [ ] Stale dynamic SHAs/run IDs are removed from durable documents or placed only in RELEASE_STATUS/evidence with exact provenance.
- [ ] Markdown internal links pass.
- [ ] Product/documentation contract checks pass.
- [ ] Exact-head CI passes.
- [ ] Final PR report contains zero unreviewed inventory entries and `Evidence pending: None.`.

## Required evidence

- Exact changed-file list against the 92-file starting inventory plus the new ledger.
- Mechanical assertion that `product_release/archive/**` has zero changes.
- Stale-token scan covering AssemblyAI/Cloud-STT-as-current, Native/Web-Speech-as-current, Basic identities, obsolete transcript-retention claims, obsolete release SHAs, and superseded authorities.
- A terminal disposition for every non-archived Cloud-STT and Native-STT evidence/runbook filename: consolidate current Private-STT facts into a canonical authority, repair inbound links, then delete or reduce to a dependency-required redirect.
- Link/path validation and current workflow/script existence checks.
- Mutation proof that the documentation guard fails on at least one stale-current claim and one archive modification.
- Exact-head CI and documentation/product contract results.
- Deletion/consolidation ledger including removed paths, retained current content, repaired inbound links, and recovery through git history.

## Sequencing

This documentation PR remains queued until functional MVP facts and #1304's final technical disposition are frozen. Then rebase/retarget to current `main`, regenerate the inventory once, and qualify the exact final head. The delay is sequencing—not a missing PM matrix or unresolved product ruling.

## Implementation PR gate

- [x] Issue created before the documentation branch.
- [x] Implementation must occur in a linked Draft PR.
- [x] No archive edits.
- [x] No review until the 92-file ledger is terminal and exact-head evidence is complete.

Status: **OPEN — inventory captured; implementation not yet qualified.**

</details>

items.title: [DOCS] Canonical docs relay queue — Khế MVP
items.body:
## Purpose

Đây là **single pinned queue** cho mọi report cần fold vào canonical docs (BRD / SRS / Glossary / PROJECT_PLAN / CLAUDE.md / Mockup).

**Owner:** ERP_Docs session (branch `claude/edit-git-docs-Khe01`). Single-owner. Reads queue → folds canonical → replies `✅ Folded — <version>`.

**Posters:** All session leads after PR merge (post-merge rule).

---

## Post-merge rule (BẮT BUỘC)

Trong vòng **24h** sau khi PR merge vào `main` (hoặc `staging` nếu spec-impact cần frontend sync sớm), session author MUST comment vào issue này với template dưới đây.

Bỏ qua = rule violation, ERP_Docs sẽ flag trong Weekly Review.

Áp dụng khi PR ảnh hưởng tới: **business rule, schema, API contract, UI, deploy info, hoặc known bug**.

---

## Comment template

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD> — <session_name / branch>
- **PR / trigger:** #<số PR> → `<base branch: main hoặc staging>`
- **Đã đụng:** <file / module / area, vd backend/modules/ingest, frontend/src/pages/admin/Documents.jsx>
- **Thay đổi:** <1-3 dòng tóm tắt cái gì thay đổi và tại sao>
- **Docs cần cập nhật:**
  - BRD §<x> (vd §4 nguyên tắc / §7 functional)
  - SRS §<y>
  - Glossary (terms cần thêm/sửa)
  - PROJECT_PLAN (milestone update)
  - CLAUDE.md (bug pattern / business rule / API field mapping)
  - "chưa rõ" nếu uncertain
- **Ambiguity / cần PM xác nhận:** <nếu có spec conflict hoặc cần ratify, hoặc "none">
```

---

## ERP_Docs workflow

### Session kickoff

1. Read this issue's comments (sort newest first).
2. Categorize comments by status:
   - **Pending** — chưa fold
   - **Processed** — đã fold (reply marked ✅)
3. Process pending in chronological order.

### Cascade fold order

**BRD → SRS → Glossary → PROJECT_PLAN → CLAUDE.md → Mockup**

Reasoning: business rule (BRD) drives spec (SRS) drives terminology (Glossary) drives planning (PROJECT_PLAN) drives operational notes (CLAUDE.md). Mockup last (UI follows spec).

### Per-fold actions

For each canonical doc updated:
- Bump version number trong header
- Add changelog entry (đầu file hoặc separate changelog section)
- Cross-check references to other docs (no broken §x links)
- Reply DOCS_INBOX comment với: `✅ Folded — BRD v0.2 + SRS v0.3 + CLAUDE.md v0.5`

### Pre-commit check (BẮT BUỘC)

Trước khi `git commit` cho thay đổi BRD/SRS/GLOSSARY/PROJECT_PLAN:
- Verify cascade consistency (no stale cross-references)
- Verify version bumps
- Verify DOCS_INBOX comments reply marked

### Weekly Review (Monday)

Đầu mỗi session docs-editor Monday, run 8-item checklist:

- [ ] DOCS_INBOX có pending comments > 7 ngày? Process immediately.
- [ ] BRD version cao hơn SRS version → sanity check cross-ref
- [ ] Glossary terms còn match BRD/SRS use cases?
- [ ] PROJECT_PLAN milestone status đồng bộ với GitHub issue status?
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "Common Bug Patterns" có entries mới từ INC trong tuần?
- [ ] Mockup files version match current spec?
- [ ] No "TBD" / "TODO" entries trong canonical docs > 2 sprints? File issue.
- [ ] PM_Assistant STATE file recent updates? Cross-check decisions ratified vs draft.

Append findings vào `## Weekly Review Log` section dưới đây.

---

## Section: Pending

*(ERP_Docs ngầm: keep this section ordered newest-first; move processed entries to ## Processed below.)*

<!-- Posters: post new comments BELOW this section header (chronological). -->

---

## Section: Processed

*(ERP_Docs: move entries here sau khi fold xong + reply ✅.)*

---

## Section: Weekly Review Log

*(ERP_Docs: append weekly Monday review findings here.)*

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD> Weekly Review

- 8-item checklist results: <pass/fail summary>
- Pending count: <N>
- Issues filed: <list>
- Next review: <YYYY-MM-DD>
```

---

## Notes

- Owner is single ERP_Docs session — không spawn parallel docs-editor sessions (sẽ conflict).
- ERP_PM_Assistant có thể post initial comments cho bootstrap (e.g., relay BRD v0.1 → fold sau ratify).
- Sessions không có write permission lên `docs/` — bắt buộc qua queue này.
- Issue này luôn `status:in-progress` (long-lived). Comments là work units, not issue lifecycle.

# Phase26 — Support Hub & Conversation Management

**Implementation-ready specification. All D1–D40 decisions and amendments are ratified; the founder confirmed the testing approach.**

Support Hub is one cohesive Asym surface with shared native CRM context and correctly authorized owner actions. This specification preserves the complete email/intake/work lifecycle, private collaboration, drafts and reading preferences, contextual guidance, safe file reading and recoverable Unwanted/future-mail holding journeys.

**Start with the user-story book**, then follow its stable US26/REQ26/AC26 identifiers into the detailed requirement volumes. The glossary fixes domain language; OpenSpec carries observable behavior, design and the unchecked implementation/qualification checklist. The source trace records every captured section's authority and disposition.

The full package contains **217 independently verifiable user stories, 2,210 detailed requirement definitions, 717 main OpenSpec scenarios, and all additional exact proof/operating-control suites**. It covers **all 40 ratified decisions**, including D27-C, D29-X01 and every accepted correction. Numerical limits, state/audience/source rules, failure recovery and release gates remain binding.

**Email Studio/P17** owns governed reusable content, canonical authoring and whole-message preparation. **P6** owns actual communication, provider evidence and recovery. **Support** owns human work, source-specific intent and private drafting; canonical intake owns receiving and held-mail decisions. CRM and giving/care domains retain their own truth, permissions and mutations. These seams are specified throughout the requirements, not left as integration assumptions.

**Confirmed proof approach:** real authenticated Support/API and canonical intake/job boundaries on disposable local Supabase; focused actual database permission/concurrency/migration proof; and full Playwright journeys on that same backend. Existing frameworks are reused and real-provider qualification stays separate.

No feature implementation or implementation-ticket graph is included. Specification/documentary validation has passed; product runtime, provider, accessibility, intended-user and release evidence remains required before activation. Local formal/OpenSpec mirrors are validated; this publication is the complete issue-tracker specification and does not claim a source PR.

items.title: Launch QA tracker: Eliza app + Eliza Cloud all-surface QA/UX ([qa-agent] × [cloud-agent])

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: Blocked on a human decision/action; agent work complete

items.body:
# Launch QA tracker — Eliza app + Eliza Cloud, all surfaces

**Status as of 2026-07-05:** this issue is now tracker/history and high-signal launch context. It is no longer the single onboarding link for agents.

## Start Here

1. **Live kanban state:** https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/12
2. **Coordination room:** https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14292
3. **Agent/project workflow:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/docs/AGENT_COORDINATION.md
4. **Evidence standard:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/PR_EVIDENCE.md

Merged setup PR: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/14297

## Source-of-truth split

- **Project board = state and ownership.** Keep `Status` and `Claimed by` accurate.
- **Focused issues = work cards.** Scope, acceptance criteria, blockers, and durable evidence live on the work issue.
- **Pull requests = code plus proof.** Link the work issue/card and attach evidence per `PR_EVIDENCE.md`.
- **Discussion = coordination.** New agent intros, handoffs, blockers, multi-card status, and noisy chat move to Discussion #14292.
- **This tracker = launch rollup/history.** Keep only high-signal summaries here. Convert unresolved findings into focused issues/cards.

## Agent loop summary

1. Read root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, package-local agent docs, `PR_EVIDENCE.md`, the Project readme, and the relevant issue/card.
2. Pick an unclaimed `Todo` card or create a focused issue/card for new real work.
3. Comment `CLAIMING: <scope>` on the work issue with your lane tag, set Project `Status = Claimed`, and set `Claimed by = <tag>`.
4. Move to `In progress` when actively mutating code, config, deploys, or shared resources.
5. Post evidence on the issue and PR, then move the card to `Needs-agent-verify` or `needs-human-verify` per the board rules.
6. Do not move cards to `Done` or close this tracker unless nubs/a maintainer explicitly delegates that authority.

## Definition of done for the whole push

Every board card is `Done`; every launch finding is fixed-and-verified or explicitly deferred with a written reason; and nubs/maintainers have personally approved the required surfaces: browser console, app.elizacloud.ai, desktop app, phone APK, and relevant connector/cloud flows.

## Legacy note

The original issue body embedded the standing goal and board conventions directly in this tracker. Those durable rules moved into repo docs in PR #14297 so future agents do not need to scrape this issue comment history. Existing comments remain useful context and evidence history.

- **governed 审计锚（第 47 场续场 2 实跑后的下轮起点）**：`--since-ref objectstack=6251f59051c0 --since-ref objectui=56cf4d8e89b7 --since-ref hotcrm=cc0608c0700b --since-ref cloud=eca60c38bc15`（hotcrm 与 cloud 沿用第 43 场续场 5 块 L 6267842465 的锚，第 45、47 场皆不可达未审；objectos 未附着、无锚）。续场 2 窗口（自 `e3aa111ad979` / `56cf4d8e89b7`，11 + 0 主线提交）：0 笔受管、0 笔超线，读数见块 B 6335394324。此前：续场 1 窗口（自 `abc25a3536e2` / `7e9708e63216`，15 + 1 主线提交）：2 笔受管（#25149、#25127，皆 docs/adr，皆有 os-zhuang APPROVED），只记台账，读数见 6333015375。此前：第 47 场窗口（自 `eddffc3390cf` / `c8f8b10ad9b5`，51 + 11 主线提交）：6 笔受管 + 1 笔超线（#24940），七笔皆有 os-zhuang APPROVED，只记台账，读数见开轮标记 6327973881 与块 A 6329411583。此前窗口：第 45 场续场 3 窗口（自 `e4d604efd39f` / `53dea27afab5`，32 + 5 主线提交）：4 笔受管 + 2 笔超线（#25023、#24918、objectui#11600 有 os-zhuang APPROVED；#25025、#24917 Tier S 在达档 PASS 上落地，objectui#13290 超线无 APPROVED，三行认定闭），读数见开轮标记 6307898127 与块 F 6308518208。续场 2 窗口见 6303458266 / 块 E 6304450595；续场 1 窗口见 6285413947；本场窗口见 6279597228。

items.title: Cloud 10-user launch — tracker
items.body:
# 🛰️ Cloud launch — live coordination board

> **3 NubsCarson agents** coordinate here. Post with your role prefix (`[cloud-agent]` / `[vps-agent]` / `[phone-agent]`). **Claim shared zones before mutating.** This top section is the living status; comments are the chronological log. Launch-cutover tracker (Stan's lane) is preserved below the divider.

> **STATUS — 2026-06-28: the dedicated-agent 10-user launch is CODE-COMPLETE and green on prod.** Chat works end-to-end (TTFT ~2–4s), the provisioning chain is verified green end-to-end on staging, the monetized money-path is live, and apps-deploy (Product-2) is proven on prod. **The terse/imperative-prompt blocker (`Say PONG` → "I'm not sure how to answer that.") is FIXED + LIVE-VERIFIED on prod (#9807, merged).** Root cause was core's `isUnusableStage1Reply` discarding non-allowlisted all-caps replies (`PONG`/`HELLO`) — NOT the streaming doubling first suspected in #9766 (a harmless, unrelated change). Prod `ELIZA_AGENT_IMAGE` pinned to `sha-7032a6a` (prod base + #9807); live hammer on a fresh agent = `Say PONG` 20/20, `Say HELLO` 5/5, NL 3/3, **0 fallbacks**. **The 10-user launch is fully LIVE on prod (06-27): console→prod promote DONE + validated** — apex `elizacloud.ai` serves the migrated Steward sign-in (Passkey/Magic-link/Google/GitHub/Discord), API Worker current, watchdog retired, rollback hatches kept. Dedicated-agent chat + terse prompts verified live post-promote (`Say PONG` clean). **Apps-deploy is open to all orgs (#9789 merged).** Active follow-on workstream = **pre-GA Apps-platform hardening (#9853, 9 PRs, all independently reviewed SOUND/merge-ready 06-28)** — awaiting maintainer merge + staging daemon arm for the apps e2e.

### 👥 Lanes
| Agent | Owns | Current focus |
|---|---|---|
| 🟦 **cloud** | cloud-api (Worker), cloud-shared, plugin-elizacloud, packages/agent runtime, agent-image **builds**, Worker deploys, provisioning **logic** | ✅ console→prod promote DONE + watchdog retired (06-27); now driving **apps-platform pre-GA hardening (#9853, 9 PRs)** — needs maintainer batch-merge |
| 🟩 **vps** | Hetzner boxes (CP `eliza-production-1` + nodes), daemon **service** (`/opt/eliza`, systemctl), networking/headscale/disk/scaling, core reasoning loop | provisioning chain GREEN; **arm the staging daemon** for the apps-GA create→build→isolated-DB→live-URL e2e (cloud-agent's ask #2); preauth-TTL durability |
| 🟪 **phone** | packages/app (web/desktop/mobile), packages/ui, Capacitor, on-device chat UI, SSE consumption, keyboard, plugin-elizacloud streaming client | app/UI/chat shipped + green; **terse-prompt blocker FIXED + live-verified on prod (#9807 merged; prod pinned `sha-7032a6a`)**; Gate B (#9737) merged + staging-host #9760; deepscan #9743/#9745 merged; UI gestures via @desktop-codex #9725. All phone-lane PRs merged. |

### ✅ Done — live / verified on prod
- **Dedicated-agent chat latency: 24–34s → ~2–4s** — #9354 (cerebras streaming double-emit), #9491 (reasoning_effort suppression), on top of the earlier #8768 crash / #8771 DB-locality / #8769 embeddings / #8759 billing / #8757 concurrency wins.
- **Cerebras pricing-404 prod outage** (all gpt-oss completions were 500ing) — fail-soft pricing fetch **#9539**, deployed + verified live (Worker 200 / "PONG").
- **Duplicate-agent provisioning blocker** — **#9493** (reuse the one existing agent; never mint a duplicate on a failed lookup).
- **Token-by-token streaming** — landed on develop (lalalune `0929e26929` + the abort-cancel fast-follow); on-device SSE verified.
- **Provisioning chain GREEN end-to-end on staging** (🟩 @standujar) — fresh Dedicated Sandbox → `headscale_ip` → `running` → reachable over tailnet → `/pair`, on the robot node (`e2e-dedicated-test`, `100.64.0.37`). The preauth-TTL crash-loop was root-caused + fixed (10→60min).
- **Apps-deploy (Product-2) — ARMED + PROVEN end-to-end on prod** (🟦) — real API key → `POST /apps/:id/deploy` → 202 BUILDING → daemon → container → `production_url` → **200**, cleaned up. Money-path + provisioning held 10/10 throughout.
- **Monetized money path + profits-pay-hosting** — live ($0 new-org default, Cerebras defaults, no `:nitro`).

### 🔧 In flight / remaining
- ✅ **Terse-prompt dead-end — FIXED + LIVE-VERIFIED on prod, MERGED (#9807).** Real cause: core `isUnusableStage1Reply` discards non-allowlisted 2–8 char all-caps replies (`PONG`/`HELLO`) as enum/scaffold leakage, and the terse-keep rescue only handled numbers + "reply with exactly N words: X" — so the model's good `PONG` was thrown away → fallback. Fix adds `parseSayLiteralInstruction` + rescues a reply matching a token the user explicitly asked the agent to "say". Unit `80/80`. Prod `ELIZA_AGENT_IMAGE` pinned `sha-7032a6a` (prod base + #9807); live hammer = `Say PONG` 20/20, `Say HELLO` 5/5, 0 fallbacks. NOTE: the earlier #9766 (streaming de-double) was a misdiagnosis — harmless, unrelated, stays merged.
- ✅ **Console → prod promote — DONE + VALIDATED (06-27).** cloud-agent retired the watchdog + dispatched `cloud-cf-deploy production` (3/3 jobs green: API Worker + apex console + app). #9813 (apex login) + #9789 (apps open) rode along. Validated both lanes: apex renders Steward sign-in (not blank-tab), API healthy no-500s, dedicated-agent chat `Say PONG` clean on `sha-7032a6a`. Rollback hatches kept (console→`d2957c23`, Worker→`138a1e7b`). The ~2,000-commit prod gap is closed; prod is current with develop.
- 🟦 **Apps-platform pre-GA hardening (#9853) — 9 PRs, reviewed merge-ready.** P1 security gate (#9858/9859/9862/9863/9864/9865) + P3 (#9866/9867/9868). Independently reviewed (phone-agent, 06-28): **all 9 SOUND, no blockers** (#9865 + #9867 green CI; rest sound-diff + flaky-base). Remaining: maintainer batch-merge + vps arms the **staging** daemon to run the create→build→isolated-DB→live-URL e2e. Ops gates held (coordinated): `REDIS_RATE_LIMITING`, `CONTAINER_IMAGE_REQUIRE_DIGEST`.
- 🟩 **Gate A durability** — preauth-TTL env-overridable (`97dfde2`, default 60min) so the on-box fix survives a daemon redeploy.
- ⚠️ **Minor (phone-flagged 06-27, awaiting cloud-agent):** a dedicated agent's *injected* inference key can be revoked while its container keeps running (it 401s blind instead of self-healing). Isolated to one stale validation agent (deleted); whole fleet healthy (agents up 11 days). Worth a 401→re-key/error guard so it can't bite a long-lived real agent later.
- **Phone-lane PRs — all MERGED:** #9807 (core — terse "Say X" keep; the real blocker fix), #9766 (plugin-elizacloud — streaming de-double; harmless/unrelated), #9760 (ui — staging control-plane host), #9743 (ui — story mock TranslationProvider), #9745 (cloud — ai-pricing outage-resilience test). Still open elsewhere: #9725 (app — desktop shell QA, @desktop-codex draft).

### ⚠️ Notes
- **Console watchdog: RETIRED (06-27)** — the migrated `packages/app` console is live on prod and supersedes the `d2957c23` rollback. Rollback hatches kept handy (console→`d2957c23`, Worker→`138a1e7b`) in case anything surfaces.
- **`cloud-cf-deploy` deploys Worker + console together;** `ref=develop` ships develop-tip for both — coordinate before any prod dispatch. Prod is current with develop as of the 06-27 promote; it re-drifts as develop moves (periodic re-promote keeps it fresh).

### 🤝 Protocol
Stay in lane · claim shared zones first (daemon code=cloud-PR, deploy/restart=vps; `ELIZA_AGENT_IMAGE` pin; CP root SSH=vps; prod Worker + console=cloud) · **never do another agent's work unasked — offer and defer.**

---

> 📋 **LATEST STATE (2026-06-28):** dedicated-agent 10-user launch is **fully LIVE on prod** — chat + terse fix verified, console promoted (Steward sign-in live), apps-deploy open. Active workstream = **Apps-platform pre-GA hardening (#9853, 9 PRs reviewed merge-ready)** awaiting maintainer merge + staging daemon arm. Newest per-lane detail in the recent comments below.

---

> ⚠️ **The section below is the 06-16 launch-cutover snapshot (Stan's lane). Most of it is now DONE** — staging provision E2E is **green** (see @standujar's pinned comment) and apps-deploy is **armed + proven on prod**. Kept for history; the live status is the board above.

Single tracker for the cloud 10-user launch. **Core works + verified; gated on staging-green → prod cutover.** Detailed writeup: #8321 (comment).

> **Update 06-16:** Stan cleared the staging blocker (cert + secrets); `develop`→`main` promoted so the quality fixes are **live on prod**; the apps deploy + tenant-DB E2E **passed in CI**. Down to two operator actions.

## ✅ Done — verified live on prod
- [x] SDK provisions cloud agents (shaw's launch gate) — `/api/v1/eliza/agents` + `/provisioning-agent` → 200
- [x] Monetized money path — elocute + council both earn real $ (live test)
- [x] Profits-pay-hosting loop wired + verified
- [x] #8422 — arm `APPS_DEPLOY_ENABLED` — merged + live on prod
- [x] #8426 — recommend Cerebras defaults, drop flaky `:nitro` — merged + **live on prod** (recommended now = `zai-glm-4.7` + `gpt-oss-120b`)
- [x] #8427 — new orgs default `$0` not `$100` (footgun) — merged + live on prod
- [x] #8430 — apps deploy + tenant-DB E2E — **CI green**
- [x] `develop`→`main` promotion — prod now carries all the above

## ✅ Staging blocker cleared (@standujar, 06-16)
- [x] headscale-staging cert → issued → `/health` = 200
- [x] headscale bootstrap — `agent` + `tunnel` users + admin key
- [x] secrets set on host + Worker — `AGENT_TOKEN_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM`, `ELIZA_LOCAL_ROOT_KEY`, `HEADSCALE_API_KEY`
- [x] daemon healthy + claiming jobs (no KMS/preflight errors)

## ✅ Staging provision E2E — GREEN (@standujar, 06-25)
- [x] fresh agent → `headscale_ip` → `running` → reachable → `/pair` (`e2e-dedicated-test`, robot node `100.64.0.37`)
- [x] preauth-TTL crash-loop root-caused + fixed (10→60min); repo-durability follow-up `97dfde2`

## 🟢 Apps cutover (Product-2) — ARMED + PROVEN on prod (06-25)

## ✅ Staging provision E2E — green end-to-end (dedicated tier, on the robot)

Closing my lane: a fresh **Dedicated Sandbox** provisioned all the way through on staging → `running` + a real `headscale_ip`, on the dedicated robot node, reachable over the tailnet.

```
e2e-dedicated-test → status=running, node=eliza-staging-robot-1 (the robot),
headscale_ip=100.64.0.37, bridge=http://100.64.0.37:2138, heartbeating
```
Live: `job claimed → image pulled on the robot → container created → VPN registered (100.64.0.37) → tailnet health probe (retried on warmup) PASSED → running`.

### Daemon + robot hardening (merged)
- **#8455** — the provisioning-worker wrote its liveness heartbeat once per work cycle; one slow op (a ~140s `agent_delete` holding a DB lock across SSH/headscale I/O) starved the 60s heartbeat → cloud-api 503'd **every** provision. Decoupled the heartbeat onto an independent 15s interval + bounded every op + a watchdog.
- **#8456** — the dedicated robot couldn't pull the (public) image: a stale ghcr cred in `/root/.docker/config.json` overrode anonymous access → `docker pull` = `denied`. `ensureRegistryAccess` clears the stale cred when no token is set. Proven live.

### Robot back in the fleet
It had been disabled after that heartbeat outage, so staging was on a paid autoscaled cloud node instead of the dedicated robot. Re-enrolled (`enabled=true`), renamed `milady-core-1 → eliza-staging-robot-1`. `node health check {total:2, healthy:2}`.

### 3 pre-existing bugs the E2E surfaced
1. **cloud-api orphaned-pending → FIXED + MERGED (#8465).** `POST /api/v1/eliza/agents` commits the sandbox (`pending`), then mints the KMS API key + updates env **unguarded**, then enqueues the job (rollback only around the enqueue). A throw in that window orphans a `pending` sandbox with **no job and no `error_message`** — the daemon only claims `jobs`, no sweeper → stuck in `pending` forever (the generic "unexpected error" on the dashboard). Fix guards the whole `createAgent→enqueue` span + a reconciler that marks job-less pending rows as error. **Not shared-only — it'll hit the prod dedicated/non-shared path too.** Root: the cloud-v2 provisioning PRs (#8112/#8223).
2. **headscale stale API key → FIXED.** The daemon's `HEADSCALE_API_KEY` no longer matched the staging headscale's key (server apikey regenerated, daemon `.env.local` not updated) → VPN 401 → no `headscale_ip`. Regenerated + restarted. Same drift class as @NubsCarson's prod finding.
3. **Steward staging flaky → FLAGGED.** The auth gate (Steward user lookup) 500'd intermittently during the deploy (the "api: offline" flap). Self-recovered for the successful provision, but worth checking the staging Steward tenant before cutover.

### 🔑 Prod = iso-staging: headscale on the CP, not Railway (lead call)
@NubsCarson's prod blocker — dedicated agent containers don't complete tailscale registration with the **Railway** headscale (60s timeout; only `eliza-tunnel-proxy` registers). The answer isn't to make the Railway instance work — **prod must be iso to staging.** On staging, headscale is **self-hosted on the CP** (`headscale-staging.elizacloud.ai` → CP nginx → `127.0.0.1:8080`), and that's exactly the setup that registers external agent containers and hands them a `headscale_ip` (my E2E → `100.64.0.37`). So prod runs the **same CP-hosted headscale**: point `headscale.elizacloud.ai` at the **prod CP** (not Railway), front it with nginx/cert + bootstrap users like staging, daemon `HEADSCALE_API_URL` → the prod CP headscale. I'm leading this — **prod mirrors staging**, and the Railway headscale comes out of the agent path.

### Prod follow-ups
- [ ] **Promote `develop` → `main`** — ships #8465 (the orphaned-pending fix) + the other merged quality fixes to prod. The orphaned-pending bug hits the prod dedicated/non-shared path too, so prod stays exposed until this promote lands.
- [ ] **Prod container↔headscale = make it iso-staging**: self-host headscale on the prod CP (the staging recipe — DNS `headscale.elizacloud.ai` → prod CP, nginx/cert, bootstrap users), retire Railway from the agent path.
- [ ] **Decommission the Railway headscale service(s)** — once prod is on the CP-hosted headscale, the Railway headscale (`headscale.elizacloud.ai`, + any residual `headscale-staging` Railway service now that staging's headscale lives on the CP) is dead weight: tear it down to stop paying + kill the drift risk that already bit us (the prod daemon was pointed at a stale instance).
- [ ] Two daemon code bugs @NubsCarson flagged, worth real fixes: headscale-integration passing the user **name** instead of the numeric **ID** to the preauth API (400); registry-probe building a malformed ghcr token scope with the `@sha` digest (breaks the fleet auto-upgrade probe).
- [ ] **CI-wire the daemon `HEADSCALE_*` config (#8464)** to point at the **prod CP** headscale (iso-staging) so it can't drift back to Railway or a stale local.
- [ ] **Steward** tenant/DB reachability (the staging 500s) before cutover.
- [ ] Dedicated-tier server gate (the user API overrides `executionTier→shared` on prod).

### ⚠️ Cloud frontend — needs investigation
I haven't dug into this, but I have the impression there's been a fair amount of **regression on the cloud frontend** — flagging it so it gets a proper investigation; it's not in the provisioning path I worked tonight.
